in writing. today, italian prime minister matteo renzi presented the results of his country's presidency of the council of the european union and handed over the reins of the presidency to our neighbour latvia. i agree with the prime minister that the economic crisis has left a deep scar, but europe has another great challenge to overcome: to rediscover trust in its citizens and in europe. i think we need to fight the recession even harder and abandon austerity. europe must respect the principles of the social dimension, invest in people, in their minds and in the future of our children. italy has failed to achieve satisfactory results in areas that directly affect the lives of our people. i hope that latvia, having taken over the presidency, will be able to find common agreement among the member states on the maternity leave directive and that we will not lose it. i very much hope that the anti-discrimination directive, which many europeans are waiting for, will be unblocked. the fate of the directive in the boards of wives' companies is also to be decided, since the member states have not yet reached agreement on it. i would urge latvia to take account of current events, because without freedom there is no security and no rights for citizens. it is essential to continue the work already undertaken, i.e. to ensure the implementation of the stability and growth pact, to carry out the mid-term review of the europe 2020 strategy, to implement the european semester in the member states, in order to accelerate economic recovery and growth.
the agreement reached, ladies and gentlemen, is an optimal compromise and gives the member states the right to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of genetically modified organisms on their territory. gmos must not be authorised against the will of elected governments or their citizens. this directive, although not the best, does ensure that, and i think it should be approved. i believe that gmos should only be authorised if there is strong evidence that they are not harmful and cannot harm us or our children. we cannot allow the lobbyists to leave legal loopholes to legalise gmo cultivation in the european union and impose it on the people of not just lithuania but all your countries against their will. each party has to decide for itself, taking into account the precautionary principle. we must not give in to domestic pressure and allow the gmo empire to take hold in the european union. this principle needs to be incorporated in eu documents, including the free trade agreement with the united states. sooner or later, interfering with mother nature's affairs will backfire on us. so, colleagues, let us be vigilant, let us love nature and let us support this document.
in writing. statistics show that as many as 58% of eu citizens are against the cultivation of genetically modified crops in the european union. however, this issue has not yet been adequately addressed at eu level, particularly with regard to the decision-making process itself for the cultivation of gmos. it is not justified that 19 out of 28 governments oppose the legalization of a new gmo crop, but that the commission takes the final decision without taking into account the positions of democratically elected governments. as regards today's document, i can only welcome the fact that member states are being given more powers to decide on the cultivation of gmos on their territory. although these new rules do not address the labelling of gm products, this issue remains relevant. gm products must be properly labelled and the public must have the choice of whether or not to consume products containing gm crops.
in writing. mr president, the debate on the parliament and council directive touches on a very important question for the european union to answer, one that is of importance to all europeans. this is about allowing member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of genetically modified organisms. not much is known about the dangers of gmos, but there are a few things to keep in mind. there's no way to stop the spread of the modified genes. there will always be irreversible contamination from gmos. this will affect small and medium-sized family farms, such as those in lithuania, which are engaged in organic farming. the cultivation of transgenic plants creates monoculture areas where many traditional varieties are killed. the farmer is virtually dependent on chemical corporations (the seeds are patented and have to be bought annually). in addition, gmo cultivation contributes to the decline in production and alters the natural balance of existing ecosystems. then comes the worst of all: barren soil, poor harvests, and the constant threat of disease. pesticides and herbicides also lose their effectiveness, forcing farmers to use mixtures that are several times more toxic. the result is an increase in the incidence of allergies and respiratory diseases in the general population. the vote must take account of the growing discontent of the european public with gmos. the vast majority of citizens are against gmo farms in europe and we should allow member states to ban gmo farms on their territory, increasing their competence in this area.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal for the renewal of the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe. the agreement allows eu vessels to fish in its waters. under the previous protocol, 40 eu tuna vessels were authorised to fish. the financial contribution amounted to eur 682 500 per year, of which more than 35% was earmarked for the support of the fisheries sector in the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe. i support the new protocol, which is for the next four years and which gives 34 eu vessels the right to fish. the annual financial compensation will be eur 710 000 for the first three years and eur 675 000 for the fourth year, a large part of which will be allocated to support the fisheries policy of são tomé and príncipe. i agree that the agreement should be renewed and that the recommendations set out therein could increase support for the fisheries sector.
in writing. i voted in favour of this recommendation on the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe. the agreement is part of a network of tuna fisheries agreements in west africa and gives eu vessels the right to fish in its waters. the first fisheries agreement with the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe was signed in 1984. since then, eight protocols have been implemented, two of them under the fisheries partnership agreement. however, the results of sectoral cooperation so far have been very limited. this situation should be changed urgently. this protocol, together with other development support instruments such as the european development fund, should promote the genuine and sustainable development of the fisheries sector and other related industries and activities in the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe, enhancing the added value that the country derives from its natural resources. the european parliament's rapporteur believes that the commission must take the necessary steps, including a possible revision of the part of the agreement relating to sectoral support and an increase in funding, to effectively change the direction taken over the last 20 years.

in writing. i give my consent to the conclusion of this agreement. the new four-year agreement will be mutually beneficial, taking into account the interests of both parties. in particular, european union fishing vessels will be granted fishing opportunities in são toméan waters. it will also strengthen cooperation between countries and promote the same principles of good fisheries regulation and sound maritime management worldwide. stronger cooperation between the two countries will allow for the implementation of a sound fisheries policy and contribute to the responsible use of fisheries resources. it is important to note that the eu has a major responsibility in ensuring the conservation and sustainable management of international fisheries resources. in this context, the commission should pay greater attention to controls to ensure the effective use of aid. the control mechanisms applied shall be proportionate. they cannot violate the sovereignty and legitimate priorities of the country.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims at approving the agreement between the european union and the republic of seychelles on the operating possibilities for fishing vessels in mayotte waters. the agreement covers the operational possibilities of vessels flying the flag of seychelles and the exploitation of marine biological resources in mayotte waters. this agreement is special in that it allows vessels flying the flag of a third country to fish in european waters. in order to obtain a fishing authorisation that they can keep on board, shipowners will pay the fees directly to the european union. these charges will be collected by france for the eu account and redistributed to mayotte in order to efficiently meet the sectoral needs of the island in relation to port infrastructure, unloading, control and marketing of products. i am in favour of the conclusion of this agreement as it will be beneficial for both parties and for the economic development of mayotte and the seychelles.
in writing. i voted in favour of this recommendation to approve the agreement between the european union and the republic of seychelles on fishing opportunities for vessels operating in mayotte waters. this agreement covers the operational possibilities of vessels flying the flag of seychelles and the exploitation of marine biological resources in mayotte waters. this agreement between the republic of seychelles and the european union (on behalf of mayotte) has been negotiated in order to allow a certain number of vessels flying the flag of seychelles which have historically fished in mayotte waters to continue fishing activities in the exclusive economic zone of mayotte, in compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy. this is the first such agreement, and it is unique in that it allows vessels flying the flag of a third country to fish in european waters. in order to obtain a fishing authorisation which they can keep on board, shipowners pay fees directly to the european union. these charges are collected by france for the european union and redistributed to mayotte in order to meet the island's sectoral needs in relation to port infrastructure, unloading, control and marketing.

in writing. i give my consent to the conclusion of this agreement. it should be noted that this is the first agreement of its kind. under the terms of this operational agreement, vessels flying the flag of a third country will be granted the right to fish in european waters. it is noted that the agreement will benefit both parties and the economic development of mayotte and the seychelles. it will encourage the development of sustainable and responsible fisheries, while increasing the value of fishery products. i think it is appropriate to provide in the agreement for the conditions for its suspension, in particular in cases where the principles of human rights, democracy, the rule of law and good governance are being violated. furthermore, the mid-term review provided for in the agreement will allow the usefulness and effectiveness of the agreement to be assessed.

in writing. — in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, we must note that gmo cultivation is an issue to be dealt with in greater depth at member state, rather than eu institutional, level. thus, the member states should be able to decide whether they prefer to restrict or ban the cultivation of certain gmos on their territory. in addition, we should take into account the problem of crop contamination deriving from gmo cultivation which, according to the reported evidence, has resulted in increased costs for farmers trying to safeguard their crops from contact with gmos. the motion for a resolution should also make for better consumer protection, which is one of parliament’s priorities. improving the authorisation of gmos, including through uniform risk-assessment procedures and a gmo labelling system in the eu, would give consumers more access to information. lastly, since the measures taken by member status in application of this directive will have to be made public, this will allow for better scrutiny and more transparency in relation to gmos. overall, creating more room for manoeuvre and greater legal certainty, with regard to both national and regional legislation, is a substantial step forward in terms of the quality of food security in the union.

in writing. i voted in favour of this recommendation on the council position on the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of genetically modified organisms (gmos). it is very important to examine the position adopted by the council on the directive with great responsibility, as an increasing number of europeans are publicly opposed to genetically modified organisms and, in particular, to gmos in food. it is worth noting that according to a special eurobarometer report on food-related hazards in december 2010, only 21% of europeans agree (58% disagree) that food produced from gmos is safe for future generations. the european parliament considers that member states should be given more flexibility to prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory, including on grounds of environmental protection, jealousy, the protection of biodiversity or the conservation of habitats and ecosystems. in addition, the risk assessment approach needs to be strengthened, as the long-term effects of gmo cultivation have not been sufficiently taken into account until now.
in writing. i voted in favour of the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos because i believe that it is appropriate to follow the principle of subsidiarity by giving member states more flexibility to decide whether they want gmos to be grown on their territory, without prejudice to the environmental and human health risk assessment provided for in the eu gmo authorisation system. it also calls for measures to prevent the accidental introduction of gmos. it is essential to preserve freedom of choice and provide clarity for stakeholders on the cultivation of gmos in the eu.
in writing. the cultivation of genetically modified organisms has been a hot topic for many years. i therefore welcome the recent decision of the european parliament to give member states the right to decide whether to authorise or prohibit gmos. food safety and health issues are a member state prerogative and therefore highly debated, sometimes even conflicting, issues of various interests can best be addressed by taking account of member state interests.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive. in particular, member states will be given more latitude and legal certainty. they will be able to decide whether to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of genetically modified organisms on their territory. this directive is a major step forward in protecting its citizens from potential adverse impacts. thus, in each case, the public interest and values will be taken into account when deciding on gmos. it should be noted that to date no comprehensive studies have been carried out on the effects of gmos on human health. moreover, allowing gmos to be grown, even with restrictions, would destroy organic or other farms sensitive to the impact of gmos. it is therefore essential that countries that grow gmos properly implement safeguards to prevent them from crossing borders and spreading to neighbouring countries. it is also essential that the eu institutions exercise strict controls and ensure a scientifically based risk assessment of gmo cultivation.
in writing. i voted against because the directive is harmful in principle: it will make it possible to grow gmos in europe. the debate in the ep and public opinion polls show opposition to gmos both among meps and the public. today the european parliament had a great opportunity to ban gmos in europe. instead, through the efforts of the big factions and the small right-wing factions, we have created a fuzzy, unclear, national licensing system that not only fails to ensure food safety, but also creates a huge opportunity for corruption, fueled by the lobbyists of the big agribusiness corporations. i am afraid i am right, but i do not want to give the impression that many members of the european parliament have today played the role of extras in a prearranged spectacle, which has been staged by the gmo lobby.

in writing. as the current painful events concerning our lithuanian children in norway show, the hague convention on international child abduction, which complements the convention on the protection of children, is of paramount importance in protecting the interests and rights of the child, as the convention provides for the immediate return of abducted children to their country of residence. this hague convention is important because it provides a framework within which participating states can cooperate to find solutions in cases of international child abduction. it also provides for the courts with jurisdiction and the law applicable to the decision on the child's place of residence. most important, it is this convention that provides for the prompt return of abducted children to their country of residence. in many cases, these problems arise when couples separate. if the mother and father are from different countries, there is a desire to take advantage of the lack of cooperation between these countries in order to secure custody of the child. in these cases, the main problem is the national bias of the legal systems of individual countries. often, the courts of both countries recognise their jurisdiction and each country grants custody to the parent who is a national of their respective country. this area falls within the exclusive sphere of external competence of the eu. the member states therefore no longer have the right to act on their own initiative. the main problem is that the convention does not provide for the possibility of independent action by international organisations.
in writing. mr president, the report under discussion raises very important questions relating to the civil aspects of international child abduction. this is regulated by the 1980 hague convention. today, the european parliament is voting to accept the accession of eight new countries to the convention. i think there shouldn't even be any doubt. the more countries adopt international standards on this issue, the better off the children will be. the family is one of the fundamental values of society and the institutions should protect it also through legal means, in particular by protecting the best interests of children. according to the latest eurostat data, as many as 140 000 families of different nationalities are separating each year in the european union. it is increasingly the case that former spouses live in different countries, including outside the european union, and that children are abducted by one of the parents. for this reason, the hague convention is an important instrument in establishing a mechanism allowing states to cooperate in addressing issues of abduction. the biggest problem in such cases is the state's legal framework. it is often the case that the courts grant custody to a parent who is a national of the country where the court is located. this convention seeks to remedy such situations. the accession of 8 new countries to the convention is a cause for celebration, as it is about protecting children worldwide.

in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims at gabon's accession to the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 provides for a framework for cooperation between contracting parties in dealing with cases of international child abduction and has been ratified by all eu member states. often, such problems arise when couples of different nationalities separate. the lack of cooperation between states is often exploited to secure custody of the child. the media is full of reports of international child abductions by divorced couples. the convention aims to address these problems at international level by establishing that the competent courts and the applicable laws are those of the state in which the child resides. the convention also provides for a system to ensure the prompt return of a child who has been abducted. gabon's accession to the convention is a positive step towards ensuring the protection of those children.

in writing. i voted in favour of this motion, which aims to bring the seychelles into line with the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 provides for a framework for cooperation between contracting parties in dealing with cases of international child abduction and has been ratified by all eu member states. often, such problems arise when couples of different nationalities separate. the lack of cooperation between states is often exploited to secure custody of the child. the media is full of reports of international child abductions by divorced couples. the convention aims to address these problems at international level by establishing that the competent courts and the applicable laws are those of the state in which the child resides. the convention also provides for a system to ensure the prompt return of a child who has been abducted. the accession of seychelles to the convention is a positive step towards ensuring that the protection of those children is ensured.

in writing. the accession of all countries, including europe's neighbours, to the hague convention, which aims to ensure the prompt return of children who have been illegally removed to or retained in any contracting state, is of the utmost importance. however, i would like to point out that there is great concern today about the actions of the authorities in some countries, such as norway, which restrict or deprive citizens of other countries living there of their right to fatherhood. reports have surfaced that parents in russia, poland, and lithuania are forced to break the law and kidnap their children from foster homes. i would like to draw the attention of members of parliament to this problem and to stress that cultural differences, child-rearing traditions, even a poor knowledge of the local language, lack of money cannot be grounds for taking children away from their legal parents. in the meantime, the european parliament must take measures to protect the children and families of european union citizens. norway has already announced the search for several illegally removed children and today we are faced with a difficult situation. it is also important that the norwegian courts cannot give custody of the child to the grandparents or relatives because they live in another country. we must ensure that the illegal abduction of children is prevented, but we must also protect the interests of children, the interests of citizens of the european union. if so, parents would no longer have to take drastic measures to save their families.

in writing. the legitimate interests of the child must always and everywhere be paramount, since children are victims themselves, caught in the war of parental ambitions. the more states that accede to the convention, the easier it will be to resolve international child abduction conflicts and to ensure effective protection of the interests of the child at international level. only in close cooperation between states can the full well-being of children be ensured. it should be noted that any issues concerning the child must be assessed in the light of the child's best interests and must be ensured that these interests are not prejudiced. the child must not become a hostage to the ambitions of the parents but also a victim of imperfect international law and its application. it is therefore essential that the child's best interests are protected and that his or her right to contact both parents is guaranteed in the context of a custody battle in divorce cases. it is essential that all states act in a targeted manner to prevent international child abduction and that a system of judicial and administrative institutions is established that is operational.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to declare the mandate of the members of the european parliament whose election has been notified by the competent authorities of the member states as valid. this proposal relates to the results of the direct elections to the european parliament, which were held on 22-25 may 2014. i support the proposals set out below, which provide the competent authorities of the member states with the names of the persons who can immediately replace meps, listed in order of the number of votes received. it is also necessary to conclude without delay the examination of the disputes submitted to them and to inform parliament of the results. i support calls for member states to ensure that registration formalities for citizens of other member states participating in european elections are simplified, whether they are voters or candidates, in particular by removing unnecessary administrative barriers.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it concludes the european parliament's examination of the credentials of the members of the european parliament elected in the member states on 22 may 2014 and publishes the list of members of the european parliament currently in force. this is necessary because, for some time after the elections, the member states are still debating the final list of members of the european parliament elected in those countries. the reasons for the conflicts are varied, ranging from the right to stand for election as defined by national law (a problematic situation in cyprus, denmark, ireland, malta and the united kingdom) to conflicts of interest incompatible with the duties of a member of the european parliament. the list of members of the european parliament approved is annexed to this communication.
in writing. — i voted in favour of this proposal of broadening the initial directive 2011/82/eu because it provides the legal basis for improving security of european roads. to begin with, it allows the sharing of information relating to road safety violations between traffic enforcement agencies of member states at union level. i think this will help to stop impunity of traffic violators who committed a violation in a state other than their home state because it will be much easier to find, notify and if necessary punish those breaching traffic rules accordingly. in addition, the proposal has broadened the initial scope of the directive by including such offences as driving a vehicle without a helmet, driving while using mobile devices or being under the influence of drugs as well as incorporating such countries the united kingdom, ireland and denmark into the agreement. in my opinion it is likely that more extensive scope of resolution will contribute to the lowering of the overall number of fatalities in the eu. overall, i believe that this resolution, like its predecessor, will ensure greater traffic safety throughout europe and will work as a deterrent regarding reckless driving.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal, which will allow eu member states to exchange information on road safety violations and good drivers. most offences, especially speeding, are committed by foreigners rather than by residents of the countries where they are committed. one of the main reasons is that the authorities, not knowing the residence of the owner of the vehicle, cannot notify him of the fine. the proposal provides that the authorities responsible for road safety in the member states could request data on the owner of a foreign-registered vehicle if he has committed an infringement, in order to be able to inform him of the infringement committed in the language of the country concerned. the directive contributes to the eu's target of halving the number of road traffic fatalities and reducing the number of injuries by 40% by 2020. i support the proposals to strengthen this system so that infringements can not only be reported but also be effectively sanctioned.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it is the european parliament's endorsement of police cooperation in all eu countries in cases of road safety violations. drivers who break road safety rules in another eu country will now be fined in their country of residence. the eu decided to adopt legislation to allow police to exchange data on offenders between member states, as it was found that most offences, particularly speeding, were committed by foreigners rather than by residents of the countries where they were committed. this directive thus enables the authorities of the member states responsible for traffic and road safety to require the owner of a foreign-registered vehicle to provide information on him in the event of an offence involving a serious risk to road safety, in order to be able to inform him of the offence committed in the language of the country concerned. it was agreed that fines would be imposed across the eu for the main offences: speeding, driving without a seatbelt, running a red light, driving in a reckless manner, driving in a restricted lane and using a mobile phone while driving.
in writing. i believe that this directive should enter into force as soon as possible in order to fill the legal vacuum in this area. it is worth noting that many countries have invested heavily in the relevant systems and that the exchange of information is already taking place. this is a necessary measure to combat road safety violations. in particular, it will make it possible to prosecute drivers irrespective of the country of registration of their vehicles, thus complementing the already established mechanism for the exchange of information. the proposed system will also make it easier to collect fines, prevent impunity for foreigners and ensure that all europeans comply with road rules.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims at concluding a sustainable fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and senegal. one of the principles of the agreement is to create a level playing field for eu fleets by stipulating that senegal undertakes not to grant more favourable conditions to other fleets when the characteristics of the vessels are the same and they fish for the same species. senegal will receive a financial contribution of eur 8 690 000 for the annual financial compensation and support for the senegalese fisheries policy. given the availability of fish stocks and the possibility of future cooperation on other fish species, as well as the possibility of supplying quality fish products to the eu market, this new partnership agreement is beneficial for both parties.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it gives the european parliament its support for the conclusion of a sustainable fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and senegal. the commission has proposed to conclude, on behalf of the eu, an agreement aimed at establishing a new framework for cooperation between the eu and senegal. one of the principles of the agreement is to create a level playing field for the eu fleets by providing that senegal undertakes not to grant more favourable conditions to other fleets than those provided for in the agreement, where the characteristics of the vessels are the same and they fish for the same species. the port of dakar is a commercial port of senegal, internationally important due to its geographical location. the new partnership agreement is mutually beneficial, given the fish stocks available and the possibility of future cooperation on more species, as well as the possibility of developing the local fisheries industry in cooperation with eu vessels and supplying quality fish products to the eu market.
in writing. i give my consent to the conclusion of this agreement. the provisions of this agreement will create a level playing field for the eu fleet and ensure fair competition. it is worth noting that this partnership is beneficial to both parties, as it would help both the republic of senegal and the european union to create new jobs and develop a fisheries-related industry. it is important to stress that the eu has a major responsibility for ensuring the conservation and sustainable management of international fisheries resources, and it is therefore essential that each fisheries partnership agreement sets out the principles of good regulation of the fisheries sector and sound maritime management, thus ensuring the development of sustainable and responsible fisheries and the enhancement of the value of fishery products worldwide.
in writing. i support this resolution, which aims to assess the torture of suspected terrorists by the us central intelligence agency and to instruct the committee on civil liberties and foreign affairs and the subcommittee on human rights to reopen the investigation into possible cia prisoner transfers and illegal detention in european countries.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. in view of the gruesome details contained in the report, it is necessary to reopen as soon as possible the investigation into the alleged transportation and illegal detention of prisoners by the cia in european countries. the cia's program of secret detention and extraordinary rendition has fostered an atmosphere of impunity and facilitated the perpetration of atrocities. in addition, the authors of the detention and interrogation programme or its direct implementers have not been held legally accountable to date. it is therefore essential that member states carry out independent and comprehensive investigations into cases of illegal transfer, detention and torture and finally bring the perpetrators of these offences to justice. each country has a duty to protect itself, but it must do so by legitimate means. it is therefore essential to close legal loopholes, to ensure a fair legal process and to prevent the implementation of such opaque programmes in the future.
in writing. first of all, i would like to emphasise that this resolution is gaining weight because of several accents. first, it calls on the united states to cooperate in response to all requests from eu member states for information on the investigation carried out. only then can we ensure that thorough investigations are carried out in europe and help to uncover the truth. secondly, the resolution instructs the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, with the participation of the committee on foreign affairs and, in particular, the subcommittee on human rights, to reopen the inquiry into 'the alleged cia prisoner trafficking and illegal detention in european countries' and to report to the plenary within one year. this will also encourage research in the member states, as they will be more interested in collecting the information themselves before the report is published in the european parliament. i also want to take this opportunity to say that i do not condone the use of harsh interrogation methods, which are inhuman, torture, and unlawful detention. these are huge mistakes that have been made here in europe as well. while i realize that this cannot make up for the damage done, as a european, i want to feel for all those people who have been tortured and have gone through a real hell. i condemn those who have contributed to this, who have turned a blind eye or pretended not to know what is happening.
in writing. — i voted in favour of this resolution because it offers a comprehensive approach to counter-terrorism policy by addressing both: ways to tackle the root causes of terrorist behaviour and other preventive measures to counter radicalisation. i believe that not only atrocities committed in paris but all the acts of terrorism and glorification of such acts should be decried in the strongest terms and an appropriate preventive mechanism for dealing with this phenomenon should be implemented. subject to this, i agree with this resolution by being strongly convinced that freedom and security dimensions are closely interrelated and co-dependent and, hence, there has to be a balance between the two. this means that failing to secure one has detrimental repercussions on the other. in addition, i support the reasoning expressed in the resolution that the european institutions need to invest more in combating the root causes of terrorism and in order to be prepared for counter-terrorism actions at all times. moreover, as stressed in the text, i agree that it is very important to demand democratic oversight of these efforts to ensure that protection of personal liberty, which is one of the core human rights, is not undermined.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to introduce measures to combat terrorism. i support calls for member states to improve the exchange of information needed to combat terrorism, both among themselves and with third countries, and to ensure full cooperation with specialised agencies, in particular eurojust and europol. i believe that the fight against the illicit trade in arms should be a priority area in the eu's fight against serious transnational organised crime, in line with the calls for proper implementation of the anti-money laundering directives. it is essential to establish a european passenger name record (pnr) system, to ensure the prevention of radicalisation, to improve the exchange of information and to strengthen the protection of the external schengen borders.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because it is a call for counter-terrorism measures by parliament, especially after the recent tragic events in paris. in its resolution, parliament stresses that prevention strategies to combat terrorism should be comprehensive, aimed at directly combating the preparation of attacks on eu territory, and also include the need to respond to the causes of terrorism. the fight against terrorism must aim at combating in a coherent manner factors such as radicalisation leading to violent extremism, developing social cohesion and inclusion, political and religious tolerance, avoiding the creation of ghettos, addressing and countering incitement to commit terrorist attacks via the internet, as well as preventing and restricting the movement of persons to join terrorist organisations, preventing and restricting the recruitment for armed conflict, disrupting the provision of financial assistance to terrorist organisations and individuals joining them, ensuring strong prosecution where necessary and providing law enforcement authorities with the appropriate means to fulfil their duties in full respect of fundamental rights. the other crucial element in the fight against the threat of terrorism, which parliament stresses, is education, and it therefore calls on the member states to invest in education systems aimed at addressing the causes of radicalisation and to promote integration, social inclusion, dialogue, participation, equality, tolerance, intercultural and religious understanding and rehabilitation programmes through education programmes.
in writing. the growing threat of terrorism and violent extremism poses a major threat to the security of europe as a whole and to the freedom of every citizen. the recent tragic terrorist incidents not only within europe but also in the eu's immediate neighbourhood are a constant reminder of the need to update and concretise the current counter-terrorism strategy and to promote as much as possible cooperation between international organisations, member states and specialised agencies in this field. the fight against terrorist groups and organisations supporting them must be one of the eu's top security priorities. for these reasons, i strongly support this european parliament resolution and its calls on the commission and the council to review and thoroughly assess the current eu counter-terrorism measures without delay and to adopt an updated counter-terrorism programme.
in writing. it is crucial today to address the causes of terrorism rather than fighting the consequences. clearly, in many lands, the idea is that having a large number of armed soldiers and police on the streets will provide security. but is that really the case? i did the opposite. this is a great example of how to deal with consequences. countering terrorism, especially given that terrorists are often people living in europe, is a multi-faceted process. first, investment in the education system. european values must not remain on paper, they must be taught in schools. there is no doubt that fostering conflict between people of different religions, beliefs, backgrounds leads to destruction. secondly, reducing social inequalities. today we are nurturing an increasingly evil society, whose representatives - unemployed, without access to medicine, forgotten and abandoned by all - are becoming more and more radical. and that leads to self-destruction. thirdly, we must ensure that the institutions responsible work effectively. we cannot tolerate the kalashnikov vending machines on the streets. we must ensure that security personnel are prepared for challenges, are well informed and know how to act in the event of a threat. security officers must not be tasked with posing weapons, but with constant, consistent work.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to extend the mandate of the internet governance forum. the purpose of the igf is to provide a forum for forward-looking discussions on a wide range of internet governance issues and, where appropriate, to provide recommendations to the international community. the ep sends delegations to each annual igf meeting, promoting european values and communicating with civil society organisations and representatives of national parliaments who have participated in those events. the eu has a duty to increase the influence of these shifts in opinion in the political debate. i agree that there is a good chance to learn from the productive discussions held at the igf so far and to take action, particularly in the areas of regulatory aspects of electronic communications and data protection.

in writing. – today the commission presented a new energy union package. energy union was neglected for too long, leaving the eu with a highly unsatisfying and fragmented energy market overly dependent on states’ regulation. therefore, now the eu needs to speed up its work in order to become more energy independent and produce energy more efficiently and hence cheaply, simultaneously taking into account environmental standards. this can be done only by tackling the market and geopolitical security nexus, meaning that the energy sector should be considered as a part of the internal market with easy entry access, transparent rules and efficient connectivity working in full accordance with free-market principles. we have to keep a high level of advancement in creating a european energy union, especially taking into account a great need to ensure energy security as an integral part of the overall european union security strategy.
in writing. the decision to create the eu energy union is undoubtedly one of the most significant developments of the decade. however, for this union to be truly effective and to ensure the energy security and competitiveness of the eu as a whole, decisions that have often lacked political will until now will also have to be implemented. i expect the future union to pay greater attention to and support the baltic states, which have often been left to reduce their total energy dependence on a single external supplier with their own resources. we hope that the synchronisation of the baltic states with the continental european networks will become one of the key areas of the energy union. we also want to see significant changes to ensure a level playing field with third countries and greater integration of eu energy affairs into the eu's external policy.
in writing. the commission's proposal for an energy union, which is very necessary and important for europe today, is to be welcomed. this union is important because the energy system is facing increasing challenges to ensure a secure, sustainable and affordable supply of energy for all citizens. our people, their households and businesses are increasingly concerned about affordability and competitiveness of energy. unfortunately, the economic crisis has also increased energy poverty, because heating and electricity bills are so high that not everyone can afford them. another priority for the energy union is to complete the internal energy market during this new commission's term of office, in particular by fully implementing existing legislation. increasing competition should help reduce costs for citizens and businesses, increase competitiveness and stimulate job creation and economic growth. we need to pay particular attention to the needs of vulnerable consumers and take these social aspects into account. finally, i would like to mention that the situation of the baltic states with regard to full integration into the eu internal energy market is specific, as the electricity networks are operated by a third-country (russian) transmission system operator. it is therefore important to ensure the synchronisation of the member states with the continental european networks. this is the only way to ensure the integration of the baltic states into the eu's internal energy market.
in writing. – i support strongly the creation of the resilient and robust energy union, which will provide for secure, sustainable, competitive, affordable energy for every european. member states’ vulnerabilities, such as dependency on third-country suppliers and lack of interconnections with the eu networks, affect also the eu as a whole, and many of them were addressed with the third energy package as well as moving forward on infrastructure projects reflecting the european priority. however, we are still on the way to attaining goals set at the highest eu level and, with fading hopes of building a civilised relationship with our biggest supplier of energy, russia, it becomes clear that we need enhanced commitment, coordination and trust among the member states – a true energy union. among the things to be done are creating a transparency mechanism and ensuring the synchronisation of member states’ electricity networks with the eu. we also should take into account our closest neighbours, as the developments there affect the eu. i hope this european project will match the ambition and success of the projects that lay at the foundations of the european union we know today.
ladies and gentlemen, yesterday the lithuanian milk producers' conference was held. the crisis has not yet been resolved, and lithuanian milk producers are faced with the fundamental question of whether anyone still needs their milk, which costs just 12 cents a litre. this is a desperately low price that does not cover the cost of production. the compensation received by the baltic producers for the russian embargo has unfortunately not sufficiently alleviated the situation. as a result, most of our dairy farmers are in a state of total despair. it is no secret that lithuanian farmers also receive one of the lowest direct payments in the european union. this situation also reduces the competitiveness of our farmers on the european union market. the analysis shows that the price of raw milk received by the farmer has decreased significantly. meanwhile, production costs and other costs have increased several times over the decade. i call on the commission and parliament not to leave the milk producers to their own devices.

in writing. a year after russia applied discriminatory customs procedures to lithuanian trailers at its border, russian discriminatory actions against lithuanian carriers are being repeated. russia is closely monitoring lithuanian shipments, as eu countries ship 'embargo' products, i.e. food and agricultural products, to russia via lithuania. russia has been able to rely on such a formal but unrealistic ground, which could discriminate against any eu country, since it ceased to benefit from the tir system more than a year ago. after withdrawing from the tir system, russia introduced a separate guarantee system, which is not approved in europe. as early as last december, i asked the commission what measures it was going to take to prevent such blatant discrimination against eu member states. the commission has not received any comments from the russian authorities on the exporting producers concerned. i received a 'concerned' reply from the commission, but it did not provide for any specific action by the commission. the commission also did not explain in its reply on what basis compensation should not be granted to lithuanian carriers to compensate for the losses they suffered as a result of discriminatory actions by russia.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to introduce a lower charge for bank cards. the new rules limit the fees charged by banks to businesses for the use of bank cards to settle accounts with customers. these rules aim to increase transparency in the charge applied by banks, which would encourage competition and allow the choice of the most appropriate card-based payment scheme. the new rules will also apply to banks operating in lithuania, which means that card payments in lithuania will be subject to a charge. in lithuania, banks generally charge a tax on business of between 0,8% and 2% of the purchase value, which is usually included in the price of the goods or services. the draft new regulation would limit the interbank charge for credit card payments to 0.3% of the value of the purchase or service. the interchange fee for international debit card payments cannot exceed 0,2%. however, eu countries are allowed to calculate this threshold for another five years, not from the price of the good or service, but from the average annual value of transactions in a separate card scheme. in addition, after the transitional period, a fee of up to eur 5 per transaction will be available for debit card settlements of small amounts.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it is clear that the commission and the national competition authorities have so far failed to tackle the abusive levels of interchange fees. but now the situation should improve somewhat. the good news is that in the near future, debit cards will be subject to a maximum interchange fee of 0.2 percent and credit cards to a maximum of 0.3 percent. prices of goods and services will probably remain the same. on the other hand, a lower tax would have a number of positive aspects. first, the decision is important for small and medium-sized businesses, which, in order not to pay excessive fees, were often unable to offer their customers payment by bank cards. i believe that, once this decision has been adopted, the number of card-based payment facilities will gradually increase. secondly, the reduction in the tax should encourage people to use bank cards more often, which will also help to combat the shadow economy.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report to support the dismissals of the belgian company 'the saint-gobain securitisation' because it had become unprofitable. according to the information provided by the belgian authorities, the automotive stainless glass sector has suffered from severe economic shocks due to several factors, such as the decrease in the production of stainless glass for the automotive industry in the eu, the increase in the market share of competitors from outside the eu and the increase in imports of these products into the european union. the activities of sgs benelux were closely linked to the production trends in the automotive industry, which declined in the period 2007-2012. in addition, a general trend was observed for automotive manufacturers and suppliers to shift production from one eu country to another, i.e. from western europe (in particular france, belgium and spain) to eastern europe. the european parliament therefore agrees with the commission that this application meets the criteria of the european globalisation adjustment fund and that belgium is therefore entitled to financial assistance to help redundant workers find employment, contribute to their training, help them find work and provide career guidance.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of supporting 257 workers who have lost their jobs because of the general trend by manufacturers and suppliers in the automotive industry to transfer production within the eu, from western europe to eastern europe. i agree that the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) has to help these redundant workers to reintegrate into labour market.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the provision of funds to re-train and re-employ people who have lost their jobs after the automotive stainless glass sector in belgium suffered a major economic shock and one of the saint-gobain securite (sgs) group companies, which produced this glass, was forced to lay off 257 workers. the dismissals from the sgs concern mainly production line workers (83% of such workers have the status of worker), and in order to address emerging social problems as quickly as possible and in the light of the labour market situation in the affected area, these dismissed workers are expected to undergo retraining to enable them to find work in other professions and/or in other sectors. this appropriation is intended to cover the cost of the european globalisation adjustment fund.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution, which aims to assess progress in the european union on gender equality the 2013 the resolution highlights the consequences of gender inequality: violence against women, wage disparities and unequal career opportunities. according to the commission, as many as 22% of older women and 35.5% of single parents in the eu are at risk of poverty. although the employment rate for women has risen slightly since 2002, it has been affected by the crisis. in order to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, the eu must not only achieve a 75% employment rate, but also improve the quality of work. if gender equality existed in the labour market, eu gdp could increase by up to 12%. the cost of care services remains a major barrier to women's employment. it is therefore necessary for member states to establish accessible and high-quality care services that are available on a full-time basis. the fight against violence against women is also very important. i agree with the suggestions that, in particular, it is necessary to collect comparable data on violence against women in all member states, and the work of the european institute for gender equality is crucial in this regard.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because equality between women and men is still a challenge in the european union, and there are still problems with lower wages and pensions for women, discrimination against women in the labour market, women's participation in decision-making and politics, and violence against women. the european union is making progress on gender equality, but it is too slow. according to the european parliament's rapporteur, if we continue at this rate, we will not have closed the gender pay gap by 2084. the increase in female employment is very small, for example from 60% to 63% over a five-year period, but it is not enough. therefore, more attention needs to be paid to female employment and job quality, as more and more women are working part-time or on temporary contracts. as a result, women receive lower pensions later in life and suffer poverty and social exclusion. the fight against violence against women is a key priority, and i therefore ask the commission, together with other members of parliament, to declare a european year dedicated to this problem. this would help to draw the attention of the member states and our citizens, who are not always willing to speak out about this in our society. it is also necessary to ratify the istanbul convention on violence against women.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the progress on equality between women and men in the eu. one of the europe 2020 goals is to reach 75 % employment and without the progress in this sphere, this goal will not be reached. since 2002 female employment increased only by 4.7 % (62.8 %). if no extra effort is put in, this number will not increase.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report on common rules for imports from certain third countries. the commission proposal for a regulation lays down safeguard and surveillance measures which may be applied to imports of products, including coal and steel, but excluding textile products covered by a separate regulation. the regulation applies only to a limited number of countries, namely azerbaijan, belarus, kazakhstan, north korea, turkmenistan and uzbekistan. the safeguard measure is rarely used in practice and, as regards surveillance, the last safeguard measure was for steel products and expired on 31 december 2012. a substantial change in the new version of the regulation concerns the update of the annex by deleting the countries which have now become members of the world trade organisation armenia, russia, tajikistan and vietnam.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report on the codification of the rules of the stabilisation and association agreement with the republic of montenegro. the commission attaches great importance to simplifying and clarifying european union law, so that it is more understandable and accessible to citizens, who will be able to take advantage of new opportunities and of the specific rights conferred on them. this objective will not be achieved if many provisions which have been amended several times, in part and often substantially, remain scattered among the various acts and therefore have to be sought in part in the original act and in part in subsequent amending acts. therefore, to find the rules in force at a given moment, it is necessary to carry out a study by comparing different legal acts. for this reason, it is important to codify the rules, which have been frequently amended, in order to ensure that the law is clear and transparent.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to amend the agreement establishing the common fisheries commission for the mediterranean (cfp). the agreement is amended in order to clarify the objectives and functions of the jccc and to increase its effectiveness. the new agreement sets a clear objective: the biological, social, economic and environmental sustainability of living marine resources. the functions of the cfp are also better defined: to promote common fisheries management through multiannual management plans, to define restricted fishing areas and to collect and disseminate data. the agreement includes provisions on sanctions for non-compliance by members and non-members. in addition, a specifically defined dispute settlement mechanism is in place to be used in the event of a dispute between the contracting parties.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution, in which the european parliament assesses the 2014 progress report of montenegro. parliament welcomed the progress made by montenegro in the reforms aimed at ensuring the independence and efficiency of the judiciary, but called for substantial reforms in the areas of appointment, promotion and disciplinary procedures for judges and prosecutors. the lack of progress in the fight against corruption is a cause for concern, which, despite the significant financial resources allocated to public authorities by international donors, continues to threaten the proper functioning and stability of democratic institutions, the rule of law and economic development. the european parliament also stresses the need to improve consultation with civil society organisations in order to increase transparency in policy-making and legislation and to ensure the openness of these processes. it is also necessary to underline that progress in the areas of women's rights, gender equality, the proportion of women in politics and the labour market and the fight against domestic violence remains limited. progress in the areas of women's rights, gender equality, women's participation in politics and the labour market and the fight against domestic violence is therefore urgently needed.
in writing. i agree with the progress report presented by montenegro. each developing country must have a clear european perspective. progress towards membership depends on the steps taken by each country to meet the established criteria based on the principle of merit. progress towards membership is welcome, but all efforts must continue to be made to implement reforms effectively. a fundamental review and strengthening of economic governance and sustainable economic reforms are needed. particular attention should be paid to reforms related to the rule of law, as this is an essential element of the european integration process. it is therefore essential to strengthen democratic institutions and ensure inclusive democratic processes in order to implement the basic democratic principles and shared eu values. it should be noted that progress has been made in the implementation of reforms aimed at ensuring the independence and greater efficiency of the judiciary. the mechanisms for consulting civil society organisations have also been improved. however, the problem of impunity in war crimes cases still remains. moreover, corruption also remains a major problem requiring more effective solutions.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution in which the european parliament assesses the 2014 progress report of the former yugoslav republic of macedonia. parliament believes that the authorities and civil society should take appropriate measures to achieve historical reconciliation in order to eliminate the inter- and internal segregation of the different ethnic and national groups, including the bulgarian nationals. welcomes, however, the fact that a legal and institutional framework to combat organised crime is already in place and that a number of successful police operations have been carried out against organised crime groups, in particular in disrupting international drug trafficking and the smuggling of migrants. but they still regret that there is not enough cooperation with civil society organisations and public stakeholders in the development of legislation. such cooperation should be based on a genuine willingness of the government to consult a wide range of stakeholders both in the legislative and policy-making processes.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution in which the european parliament assesses serbia's 2014 progress report. the european parliament welcomes the commitment shown by the serbian government to the european integration process and calls on serbia to undertake systemic, social and economic reforms with determination and without reservations. it should be emphasised that the careful implementation of legislation and policies remains a key indicator of a successful integration process and that serbia should therefore improve the planning, coordination and monitoring of the implementation of new legislation and policies. parliament stressed that serbia had ratified the main conventions of the international labour organisation on labour rights, including the revised european social charter. however, despite constitutional guarantees, labour and trade union rights are still limited and serbia should continue to strengthen these rights. the european parliament also calls on the serbian authorities to undertake structural economic reforms throughout the country in order to promote economic growth, improve the business and investment environment, ensure balanced social and economic development in all regions, combat high unemployment and poverty, implement fiscal consolidation and combat corruption, which remains the main threat to the business environment.
in writing. i agree with the progress report submitted by serbia. it is very important that the country strictly adheres to the rules of the democratic game. eu enlargement should be based on a concerted policy. european integration is a continuous and dynamic process. it is therefore essential that it reflects the overall changes taking place in the eu. it is to be welcomed that serbia has made clear progress towards fulfilling the conditions of the stabilisation and association process. however, it is essential that systemic, social and economic reforms continue with determination and without compromise. in particular, structural economic reforms are needed to boost economic growth and improve the business and investment environment. the legal framework must also be strengthened, ensuring uniform compliance with the law. serbia needs to accelerate its progress in the energy sector. in this context, it is essential that the commission supports the efforts of the serbian government to reduce the country's dependence on imported energy and to increase the diversity of energy resources.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which discusses the process of kosovo's european integration. despite some progress, kosovo still faces difficulties in implementing legislation on the protection of ethnic minorities and cultural rights. in this area, therefore, a sustained effort is needed to amend the law to include a provision on the rights of national minorities in order to avoid direct and indirect discrimination. the european parliament is concerned about the high level of unemployment, especially among young people, and about discrimination on the labour market based on gender. it should be noted that progress on property rights remains slow and is detrimental to long-term economic growth. parliament considered that kosovo's accession to international and regional organisations and mechanisms should be a priority and therefore called for the strengthening of relations with and representation of kosovo in regional organisations, international agencies and bodies such as the council of europe, as well as cultural and heritage institutions, with full membership. it is also important to improve its representation in european and international media organisations so that kosovo artists can participate in all international cultural events.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution. progress in transposing eu standards is an essential criterion for assessing the candidate's readiness to open formal membership negotiations. the eu has also been active in the fight against corruption and organised crime, and has been active in the fight against organised crime. every state must respect the principles of human rights, freedom, democracy and the rule of law. however, despite some progress, the kosovo authorities should make greater efforts to combat unemployment systematically and effectively, and to promote structural economic reforms and sustainable development by establishing a regulatory framework and incentives for small and medium-sized enterprises, in addition, urgent action is needed to combat criminal gangs and high levels of corruption.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a european semester for the coordination of economic policies: employment and social aspects. the forecasts for economic growth in europe this year suggest that unemployment will remain high, indicating that a major structural reform in the economic and social spheres is still a long way off. i support the investment plan presented by the president of the commission, but it should not be seen as an alternative to the necessary reforms, but as a complementary instrument to allow funds to be allocated to projects with a european and economic and social return. the single energy market needs to be accelerated and eu countries' energy independence promoted. the creation of an energy union is essential to make member states more competitive and more resilient to political pressure from third countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which calls for reforms to create a new business environment that encourages new business, new investment and innovation, and that ensures a return on investment, which is a key factor in attracting financial capital to the european economy. moreover, the financing of investments requires a well-functioning financial system, where increased stability and existing cross-border institutions can facilitate liquidity and market formation, in particular for small and medium-sized enterprises. the european parliament welcomes the investment plan for europe as an important instrument to boost private and public investment. it should be noted that the plan aims to stimulate additional investment, develop new projects, attract investors and restore the confidence of our citizens in europe. in this context, parliament called for the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) to be used in such a way that it is allocated to projects that provide economic returns or have a positive social cost-benefit ratio. the european parliament therefore calls on the member states to actively support the investment plan and contribute to the esif to complement the eu budget and eib funding in order to encourage and encourage private sector investment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european semester for economic policy coordination: annual growth survey 2015. i do believe that country-specific recommendations are very helpful; and it is a shame that member states are barely implementing them (only 9% were fully implemented in 2013). i call for increased involvement of national parliaments, with a view to strengthening national ownership of structural reforms.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because the european semester process ensures that member states' budgetary and economic policies are in line with their obligations to the eu (to meet the debt and deficit commitments under the stability and growth pact, the economic reform plans outlined in the 2014 country-specific recommendations and the long-term growth and job creation targets set out in the europe 2020 strategy). the commission's proposed integrated approach to economic policy is based on three main pillars: stimulating investment, accelerating structural reforms and pursuing responsible and growth-friendly fiscal consolidation.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report. it should be noted that the euro area is still not out of the exceptionally long recession, although recovery is visible, but it is still very fragile and should be strengthened. in particular, the european semester needs to be improved, existing procedures streamlined and national responsibilities increased. the three-pillar approach must be effectively implemented. investments are needed, structural reforms need to be accelerated and fiscal consolidation needs to be pursued in a responsible and growth-friendly manner. the need to increase innovation-driven efficiency should lead member states to reduce current costs rather than investment commitments. it is worth noting that a significant number of countries still need structural reforms. in this context, more attention should be paid to the social and employment impact of reforms. increasing inequality, declining purchasing power, high long-term unemployment and youth unemployment remain among the major problems.

on behalf of the efdd group.– mr president, boris nemtsov was the leader of opposition and free thought in russia. boris nemtsov was russia’s hope to become a democratic state. it is less important who actually pulled the trigger: we must ensure that not only the killers but also those who ordered this assassination are punished. it is obvious that boris was killed by forces that spread darkness, aggression and hatred in russia. it is unfortunate that today it is precisely these forces which are represented by the current russian leadership. for this reason, the russian leaders are responsible for the death of boris nemtsov. boris nemtsov is gone, but let us hope that this tragedy will become a stimulus for the opposition’s unity in russia. his unfinished work must be continued.
mr president, the picture of the body of boris nemtsov lying in front of the kremlin was a message someone chose to send in such a shocking way. this message is for us who represent democracy and values and who knew boris personally – knew him as a man of exceptional courage and strength. but, first and foremost, this is a brutal reminder for those in russia who are still trying to save their country from sliding into the darkest ages of its past. the parallel with the ussr of blood and terror of the 1930s is appalling and the message is that the dark times may become the unfortunate reality of russia tomorrow. everyone who perceives russia as a european state and nation is a spy, whoever speaks about corruption is an enemy, and whoever has his own opinion is a traitor. no one can feel safe – anyone could be next. it is clear that the atmosphere of hatred towards the west and of hostility to the open—minded people of russia made it possible for this to happen. it is a logical outcome of the policy line pursued in the last 15 years, namely putinism. today, by respecting the memory of boris nemtsov, we should not forget the fate of nadia savchenko. putin, free savchenko! (the speaker agreed to take a blue-card question under rule 162(8))
blue-card answer. – i believe we have common sense and we know the colours of black and white. this is not painting in different colours; we know who is waging war in ukraine. those soldiers have insignia and armoured vehicles and we recognise those tanks and colours. please do not try to get away from the truth; face it and you will be freed.
mr president, a long list of opposition members who have been killed during recent years has been made longer after the death of boris nemtsov. these people are the casualties of war for a right to oppose the government, for a right to tell the truth, for a right to have your own opinion. all of them were murdered for their beliefs. it might also raise a question: is there a next target? the murder of boris nemtsov might bring the kremlin regime ever closer to the point of no return for russia. we might never know the exact truth about this murder. but it is obvious that the kremlin is responsible for creating an atmosphere of hatred, impunity, unlawfulness and terror. this is a scary message to the west. information that mr nemtsov was working on a report on russian soldiers’ involvement in ukraine is even more disturbing. there are two possible impacts that this murder might have on russian society. one, it can increase fear. another, that it can consolidate like—minded people under the banner for change. if this is the case, then there is hope for russia. the eu must not remain silent. we must encourage, help and protect all those who fight for democracy. europe has to be their safe haven, their shelter, if they should seek it.
in writing. mr president, the annual report on human rights and democracy covers very important issues of people facing discrimination. for this reason, we should make a special effort to ensure that citizens' rights are respected. the lisbon treaty places a high priority on cultural and linguistic heritage, while promoting the protection of linguistic and ethnic diversity as one of the fundamental principles of the european union. this right is conferred on citizens of the union by articles 21 and 22 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, which means that the attempt to introduce the exclusivity of a particular language constitutes a restriction and a violation of the fundamental values of the union. in order to ensure that these standards are respected in the world, we must first of all introduce the principle of non-discrimination on grounds of language and ethnicity throughout the european union. unfortunately, there are still countries where the rights of minorities, especially indigenous ones, are violated. the european parliament and the commission should therefore urge all eu member states to ratify the council of europe framework convention for the protection of national minorities and the european charter for regional or minority languages without delay. it is also appropriate to recall the european parliament's resolution of july 2013 on linguistic diversity. it called on those countries which had not yet signed and ratified the charter to do so as soon as possible. he also called for the condemnation of all acts of language discrimination or forced, covert assimilation which are hostile to the languages and identities of other communities. in the 21st century europe, there can be no discrimination on ethnic grounds.
