in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report. the european security and defence policy strategy needs to be revised and concrete efforts made to meet current and future security challenges. this is extremely topical as the current russian federation aggression against ukraine brings continuous violations of international norms and breaches of human rights. i truly support the rapporteur’s view that a new comprehensive political vision and strategy are needed in order to contain russia’s revisionist ambition, sustain international norms and withstand the on-going information and propaganda war against the eu and our values. the eu should step up its diplomatic efforts, urging russia to respect its commitments and international obligations regarding georgia, moldova and ukraine. bearing in mind the worrying geo-political developments in the eu neighbourhood, one must reiterate the member states’ responsibility to act in solidarity when it comes to addressing security threats, move from reactive to proactive approach, strengthen collective defence and collaboration with nato and respond in a univocal manner to common threats. for example, sanctions against russia can be lifted only when it withdraws from crimea and fully implements the minsk agreement, and this should apply to every member state.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for an annual report from the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy to the european parliament. i agree that the priority objectives of eu foreign and security policy should be to protect european values and interests, to enhance the eu's contribution to the territorial defence of its member states and to the security of its citizens by strengthening its capacity to defend itself against the threats it faces, including terrorism, arms trafficking, drugs and human trafficking. it is necessary to support security, democratisation, the rule of law and economic and social development in the eu's neighbourhood. the eu must also take a leading role in conflict resolution and peace-keeping activities.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because an effective european union foreign policy must be based on a common understanding of the fundamental european interests, values and objectives, a common vision of external relations and a common understanding of the threats facing the eu as a whole. the main tasks of the eu's foreign and security policy are thus to protect european values and interests and to consolidate the political and legal order in europe, thus restoring and ensuring peace and stability. it is also essential to enhance the eu's contribution to the territorial defence and security of its member states' citizens by strengthening its capacity to defend itself against the threats it faces, including terrorism, arms trafficking, drugs and human trafficking. it is also necessary to support security, democratisation, the rule of law and economic and social development in the eu's neighbourhood. the european parliament considers it necessary to strengthen and combine the political, economic, financial and defence resources of the european union and its member states in order to maximise the eu's influence in the world, to develop interactions and to ensure peace and stability in europe and its neighbourhood.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased to acknowledge that this report, along with its annexes, was born out of a constructive and vivid dialogue between different parliamentary bodies, political groups and consultations with ngos. such a systematic approach was crucial to achieve its objective, namely to complement and not duplicate already existing reporting mechanisms. the rapporteur struck a balance between providing a view of the most critical human rights breaches around the world on the one hand and guidelines for the international community in foreign assistance on the other. it is absolutely essential that this report address such themes as impunity and international criminal justice, freedom of expression, rights of women and children, lgtb rights, business and workers’ rights and – most importantly – protection of human rights defenders. human rights defenders are crucial to the work of european parliament. we must also remind ourselves that those who speak up for human rights and their violations are extremely vulnerable. we have witnessed such cases in ep hearings when many of those human rights defenders who spoke in front of the sub-committee were afterwards exposed to risks to their security or even detained and tortured by their own governments.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal for an annual report on human rights and democracy in the world in 2013 and for an eu policy on this matter. i support calls for human rights provisions to be included in eu international agreements, including trade and investment agreements with third countries, while ensuring that these agreements facilitate the economic and social development of the country. i agree with the need to develop a human rights-based tool for crisis prevention and to integrate it into the eu's approach to external conflicts and crises, as well as in the future revised european security strategy. it is important to apply a common european asylum system and to ensure common eu-wide standards for the reception of refugees in order to protect unaccompanied minors and the most vulnerable. the situation in ukraine, the continuing military action and the deteriorating human rights situation are among the eu's most important challenges today, which need to be addressed urgently and with a unified voice across the eu. it is also necessary for the eu to review its strategy towards china, which is increasingly facing serious human rights violations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, in which the european parliament calls on all the institutions of the european union and the member states to focus on human rights in the eu's relations with all third countries, including strategic partners, and in all high-level statements and meetings. it is essential that member states adopt a common position in support of the indivisibility, inviolability and universality of human rights, and in particular by ratifying all international human rights instruments adopted by the united nations. the european parliament welcomes the adoption by the council of the eu annual report on human rights and democracy in the world in 2013 and calls on the new high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy and vice-president of the commission to commit to participating in the two annual debates on eu human rights and democracy policy in the future, to be held during the plenary sessions of parliament, to present the eu report and to discuss the parliament's report. parliament called for the fight against torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment to be continued, as the eu's action in this area remains insufficient and does not comply with its obligations under the eu guidelines on torture. the eu should give greater support to the establishment and strengthening of national and regional mechanisms for the prevention of torture.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution on the eu-arab league agreement on cooperation in the fight against terrorism. the eu faces a major threat from so-called eu foreign fighters, i.e. individuals who travel to other states to commit terrorist acts. today, between 3 500 and 5 000 eu citizens have left the eu to become foreign fighters in syria, iraq and libya. i agree that the eu must work more closely with the league of arab states, create a dedicated mechanism to curb arms trafficking, pay particular attention to the threat posed by the islamic state group, which has become the main sponsor of terrorism in and outside its control, and support international initiatives to combat radicalisation and terrorism. i support calls for closer cooperation with key partners and countries in the fight against terrorist financing. it is important to address the root causes of radicalisation by supporting initiatives across the arab world in the areas of youth, education, vocational training, employment opportunities and civil society.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because the european union is facing a constant and growing threat from terrorism, which has significantly damaged several member states over the last decade, attacking its citizens and threatening the values and freedoms on which the union is founded. terrorist propaganda is spread more rapidly through the use of the internet and social media, and cyberterrorism allows terrorist groups to establish and communicate without the physical barriers of national borders. the european parliament therefore welcomes the continuing and joint efforts of the european union and the arab states to work together to address issues of common interest, noting the regular meetings of the foreign ministers of the european union and the league of arab states and the memorandum of understanding signed between the european external action service and the general secretariat of the league of arab states. the eu and the league of arab states shall engage in a strategic dialogue, which shall include exchanges on political and security issues, through the regular meetings of the eu political and security committee and the permanent representatives of the league of arab states.
in writing. ‒ the scientific information on the status of the common wolverine, its exact habitat boundaries, migration routes and breeding sites is insufficient. the common herring is a prized fish and is in high demand in the fisheries industry because of its exceptional economic value. in 2013, it was established that the stock of this fish was at a level exceeding the maximum sustainable yield. i support the calls for an assessment of the state of the stock of plain whiting, a proposal for a multiannual management plan to ensure that the stock exceeds the maximum sustainable yield, a scientifically based decision on minimum landings and a temporary cessation of fishing in certain areas to protect breeding grounds.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution because the state of stocks of common trawls is a matter of concern. the common wolverine is a prized fish which is in high demand in the fisheries industry because of its exceptional economic value. unfortunately, the mortality rate of this species remains very high and the common wolverine is slow to mature and grow, so it takes a long time to restore its population size. the european parliament therefore calls on the commission and the member states to assess the state of the common wolverine stock, its habitat boundaries, the migration of the species and the precise breeding sites. calls on the commission and the member states to make use of the european maritime and fisheries fund, which provides substantial funding for the collection of scientific data; it should be noted that it is important to assess precisely the different segments of activity related to the fishing for plaice and the percentage of the segment of amateur fishing in relation to the catch of this species. commercial and recreational fishing measures therefore need to be coordinated in order to maintain stocks in excess of the maximum sustainable yield, in line with the objectives of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution, which aims to assess the eu's priorities in preparation for the 2015 session of the un human rights council. the regular sessions of the human rights council, the application of the mechanism for periodic assessment of the protection of human rights and the delegation of persons under special procedures to issues relevant to the situation in a particular country contribute to the promotion of and respect for human rights, democracy and the rule of law. i support calls for all governments to promote and support civil society organisations and human rights defenders and to allow them to operate without fear, repression or intimidation. i support calls for the eu, the commission and the eeas to integrate human rights into all areas of external policy in third countries. i agree that the un human rights monitoring mission and the osce special monitoring mission in ukraine need to be supported and strengthened.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because all states must respect the fundamental rights of their people, take concrete steps to facilitate respect for these rights at national level and cooperate at international level to remove obstacles to the enjoyment of human rights in all areas. the promotion of and respect for human rights, democracy and the rule of law shall be contributed to through the regular organisation of sessions of the human rights council, the appointment of special rapporteurs, and the application of the universal periodic review mechanism. parliament expresses its concern at all restrictions on freedom of assembly and association, including bans on civil society organisations, the use of aggressive criminal laws against the defamation of honour and dignity and other restrictive laws. we therefore call on all governments to promote and support civil society organisations and human rights defenders, and to allow them to operate without fear, repression or intimidation, and to cooperate with the united nations human rights council through the universal periodic review mechanism and to ensure that states responsible for dealing with human rights activists should assume this responsibility.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution on the situation in venezuela. the arrest of democratically elected politicians and the imprisonment of opposition leaders in venezuela since february 2014 has sparked street protests, resulting in the deaths of 44 people. resolution urges the venezuelan government to release imprisoned political protesters and to stop allowing the use of firearms by security forces to quell civil protests. i support calls on the venezuelan government to ensure that citizens are not punished for exercising their rights to peaceful assembly and freedom of expression. it is also important that the government abide by its constitution and international commitments regarding the independence of the judiciary and political pluralism, which are the foundation of democracy. the government of venezuela must also ensure that the country has the right conditions to hold parliamentary elections in 2015. i agree that the european external action service should continue to monitor the investigations and trials of opposition leaders.

in writing. the last european council discussed issues of major importance for europe as a whole. the european council first considered the energy union as proposed by the commission, as it is necessary to ensure a secure, sustainable, low-cost supply of energy for all citizens. our people, their households and businesses are increasingly concerned about affordability and competitiveness of energy. unfortunately, the economic crisis has also increased energy poverty, because heating and electricity bills are so high that not everyone can afford them. the european council has given the highest priority to energy security and calls for a strengthened legal framework for the security of electricity and gas supply. energy security can also be enhanced by ensuring stable networks, energy efficiency and the use of local resources and safe and sustainable low-carbon technologies. the european semester and the annual survey of employment growth were also discussed. the european council exchanged views on the economic situation in europe and on the implementation of major structural reforms by the member states. it endorsed the three main pillars of the annual growth review, namely investment, structural reform and growth-friendly fiscal consolidation, and asked member states to reflect these priorities in their future national reform programmes and stability or convergence programmes.
rapporteur.– madam president, today we will vote on a small part of eu history. we are voting for eur 1.8 billion of macro-financial aid to ukraine, which will be the biggest financial package given by the european union to any third country. but that alone is not as important as the political message that the european union is united in its effort to help ukraine and to back it when the help is most needed. it has to be noted that our friends as well as our adversaries are looking for cracks in our unity. ukraine needs our unity in order to sustain clear reasoning for their reforms. just yesterday, we had an opportunity to talk to the ukrainian minister of the economy. he gave us a cold but clear overview on the reforms that his ministry and the government are undertaking. fighting the oligarchic structures, battling corruption and addressing inefficiency in the public sector are just a few of the points that he raised. it seemed to me that even the critics should have been convinced that ukraine is doing its utmost to reform itself. it is chilling to imagine any of our countries going through those sorts of reforms, actually changing dramatically many fields of life that people were accustomed to. that was one reason why a colleague asked if the minister is sure that the people of ukraine will keep up with and support the pace of the reforms. we were reassured that, with a clear message from europe that europe is standing by them, the people will support and understand the need for reform. our foes would rejoice if they saw us disunited and would use it for their propaganda. we already know what they would say: ‘see, europe cannot help the country that itself wished to sign an association agreement!’ the council, the commission, the committee on international trade (inta) and the committee on foreign affairs (afet) are all calling for agreement on the proposed report without amendments, for one main reason. that reason is that time is of crucial importance here. if we vote ‘yes’ on the report today, the commission will be able to issue the first tranche of the funds to ukraine at the beginning of the summer. if we want the country, which is still fighting for its territory, to be able to stabilise its budget and economy, we have to agree on providing the funds as soon as possible. of course, i have heard critics say that we are not sure whether the money will be used transparently or whether there are enough incentives for reform in the report. i believe, at this stage, that the commission has provided for enough controls in the document that would be signed with ukraine after our vote and following approval by the council. we are, and will remain, in close contact with the support group for ukraine regarding the reforms and regarding transparency in relation to the funds provided. when the situation in ukraine stabilises, and i want to believe that it will, we will come back to the debate on how we can help ukraine on its path to reform. dear colleagues, i call on you to support this report as presented without amendments, and to demonstrate our resolution to stand by ukraine.

i am referring to the commissioner, and i am asking him whether it is lawful for national laws in one country to be imposed on other countries in the transport sector. on what grounds? the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules on competition are applied in a fair and transparent manner. market fragmentation and unfair competition are indeed a very serious threat to carriers in eastern europe, including my native lithuania. because they're not going to be able to compete with the demands that germany has put on them. so the worst-case scenario is that our carriers go bankrupt. workers will lose their jobs, their income. and finally, in all this, we must take into account the workers themselves and their rights. they do a really hard job, so they should be properly paid and socially protected. commissioner, i'm going to ask you again. the commission, in cooperation with the member states, must take the necessary measures in the transport sector to ensure that workers have jobs with adequate social guarantees.
the question asked when the blue card is raised. i would like to ask the honourable member whether, in your opinion, this decision is not directly related to the protection of your market?
the question asked when the blue card is raised. mr izmail and i have known each other since the last term and this issue today really shows that there are many unresolved issues within the european union itself. this is not the central issue in the debate on social dumping today. by joining the european union, we had to open up our markets. and everybody knew very well that there were different economic situations, different tax systems, and so there were different minimum wages. we have one in lithuania too. but the point is that germany, by actually introducing this law, is trying to compete with carriers from other countries in order to create a freer market for them to occupy. and does it not seem to you, my colleague, that we must, as you have said, make sure that the very basic principles of mutual trust in our european union are not undermined?
the german law is not in line with economic logic or the fundamental principles of the functioning of the internal market of the european union. it's been all over the place tonight. it is not just one country's interference in the social and labour policies of other countries. such laws are ostensibly designed to combat social dumping, but in reality they are a means of closing down national carriers and eliminating competition, especially from carriers from eastern and central european countries. and that will create additional social tensions in those countries. russia already imposes restrictions on carriers, especially from neighbouring countries of the european union. the carriers affected by this restriction have made a great effort to reorient their services from east to west in order to preserve their businesses and jobs, and it is therefore incomprehensible that the member states of the european union themselves introduce burdensome measures for carriers from other countries at such a difficult time. this undermines confidence in the single market, solidarity and free competition.
i think that this question has been clarified and studied from all sides enough. and i think that on the one hand we have to tell ourselves very clearly that there are huge differences in europe and we have to make a clear enough plan to reduce those differences as quickly as possible, to reduce them. and i think that the commission should withdraw its right in this case, relinquish its right, send a clear signal to germany that germany has exceeded its powers and that germany should immediately stop applying them to other countries and apply them only to its own country. and then we'll have time to figure out and predict the system and then we'll be able to run it.
in writing. today's debate on employment conditions, including minimum wage rates in the transport sector, touches on a service issue of major importance to most european countries and their priorities. this is of particular importance for countries where road transport services are an important part of the economy. this is the case in lithuania, where transport services account for 10 percent of the country's gdp. the union's decisions in this area must therefore take account of the interests of parties such as myself. the recent senseless german regulations requiring the application of the minimum wage also to carriers from other countries have contributed to the crisis in the european transport industry. it is unacceptable that the legal acts of one country impose obligations on entrepreneurs from other countries who do not carry on economic activity in that country. after all, using car transit in a country is not the same as applying for a job as a driver in that country. the german regulations in this case went too far and led to disturbances in the internal market of the union and restricted free movement of products. the best solution seems to be for the european commission to introduce the old and proven 'country of origin' principle for transport service providers and international transport. this will avoid discrimination against companies and workers from the new member states for whom transport services in transit through third countries are an important part of their economy.

in writing. ‒ the european union has signed an association agreement with ukraine, which clearly outlined ukraine's choice to pursue a path to democracy on the one hand, and reaffirmed the eu's commitment to support ukraine on its path to democracy and progressive change on the other. ukraine is currently in a situation where it is not only simultaneously trying to implement the necessary structural reforms, but is also involved in an aggressive military conflict with neighbouring russia. to wage war and seek progressive change at the same time would be an extremely difficult test for any country with a solid foundation in values and economics. meanwhile, ukraine is a country that is still maturing in many areas of national life. in order to support the reforms being undertaken by the legitimate authorities of ukraine and to stabilise the country's financial situation, the eu is obliged to provide macro-financial assistance to ukraine. on the basis of these arguments, i voted against the commission's proposal without amendments.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i support the commission's proposal to grant macro-financial assistance to ukraine. ukraine is experiencing a complex economic and financial crisis as a result of the russian occupation its currency has depreciated, international reserves have been depleted, and its ability to borrow on the international market has been reduced. the commission has also received comments from the ukrainian authorities. the objective of the eu's macro-financial assistance is to help ukraine maintain financial stability, reduce its balance of payments deficit, demonstrate support for the reforms being undertaken by the ukrainian government and show solidarity with the war-torn population. financial stability in ukraine will help ensure its economic and political stability, and at the same time contribute to the security of the entire european region.
in writing. - i voted for this report. macro-financial assistance to ukraine is necessary as the ukrainian economy is facing a severe and serious crisis. in view of this, we must be united in helping the country to stabilise its economic and financial situation. however, solidarity is not possible without a commitment to the reforms that ukraine urgently needs. the financial assistance provided will contribute to the gradual restoration of confidence and support the reforms under way in the country, in the context of the implementation of the policy programme to be agreed with the ukrainian authorities. it should be noted that macro-financial assistance is a unique eu crisis response mechanism that ensures a sustainable way out of a difficult economic situation. this additional assistance will undoubtedly be important for the development of a new international support package for ukraine. it will also complement the support provided by other donors under the imf-funded economic programme.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which proposes a common approach to tax policy that can serve as a pragmatic tool for stimulating growth. tax fraud and tax evasion cost the eu around €1 trillion in potential tax revenue each year. the main priorities for international tax policy at present are: to develop a comprehensive strategy to combat tax evasion and avoidance and to establish a global standard for administrative cooperation. three priority areas are identified. first, it identifies important initiatives that can help to ensure legal certainty, promote crossborder trade, help to exploit the full potential of the single market and thus stimulate growth and employment. second, coordinated and comprehensive action is needed to combat tax fraud, tax evasion and tax havens. such urgent action could be an alternative to the introduction of new levels or forms of taxation and provide much-needed additional funds to boost public investment, growth and employment. third, tax policy coordination through clearly defined structural tax reforms that would stimulate growth, employment and investment in the medium to long term.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because it is the european parliament's annual report on tax policy in the member states of the european union. in this report, parliament notes that tax fraud and tax evasion cost the eu some eur 1 trillion in potential tax revenues each year and that these losses pose a serious threat to the efficiency and fairness of the eu's tax systems, as the tax burden increases for all honest citizens and businesses. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer. parliament called it a first step in the right direction.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the annual tax report because it sets out the european parliament's clear and pragmatic position on the priorities of international tax policy the fight for a more transparent tax system and the setting of a standard for global administrative cooperation. firstly, it will reduce the administrative burden on businesses and remove barriers in national legal systems to make more effective use of the opportunities offered by the single market, thereby boosting growth and employment across the eu. also, given that tax policy provides a revenue base and is one of the key elements of fiscal sustainability, the transparency of tax systems will be pursued. finally, coordination in the field of tax policy will be strengthened, as only through concerted action and the sharing of relevant information can tax policies be designed to stimulate investment, job creation and economic growth across the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the annual tax report because i support the main lines of action and initiatives it contains in the fight against tax fraud, tax evasion, tax avoidance and tax havens. the communication calls on the european commission and the member states to develop tax policies that promote growth, employment and investment and reduce the administrative burden on honest taxpayers.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report on the annual tax report. coordinated action at eu level is needed to combat tax fraud, tax evasion, tax avoidance, aggressive tax planning and tax havens. transparency standards should be incorporated into future trade agreements. member states should not pursue aggressive tax policies that have a particularly negative impact on business operators. to promote growth and employment, it is necessary to maintain healthy and transparent tax competition between member states. the national tax authorities have a special role to play as guarantors of an effective, efficient and lawful national tax policy. in addition, strict penalties must be applied to prevent companies from infringing tax standards or avoiding liability for infringements. it should be noted that tax policy must help to exploit the benefits of the internal market. to ensure a long-term and growth-friendly economic policy, the coordination of forward-looking tax policies should be encouraged.

in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i support the proposed amendment to the regulation to transfer to this year the eur 21.1 billion that were not used in 2014. the amount of unused funds was due to the delay in agreeing the mff regulation. as a result, the various legal acts laying down the provisions for implementing the operation of the funds were also adopted late. this is the case for the european regional development fund, the european social fund, the cohesion fund, the european agricultural fund for rural development, the european maritime and fisheries fund, the asylum, migration and integration fund and the internal security fund. their provisions were only approved in may 2014. as a result, 300 programmes (47%) could not be adopted in 2014 and their appropriations could not be used. it is therefore necessary to adopt the amendments to the regulation as soon as possible and to transfer unused appropriations to the current year's budget in order to ensure the implementation of all the programmes envisaged.

the stories of all our countries are different. different tragic and painful. but despite our painful histories, the suffering of nations and the tragedy of broken families, it is very important to remember the past as it really was. only by being honest with ourselves and acknowledging our past can we look to the future with confidence and seek reconciliation. it is the only way to ensure that such cruel and inhuman events will never happen again. therefore, as we approach the centenary of the armenian genocide, i would like to remind you that back in 2005, the seimas of the republic of lithuania adopted a resolution, and a few days ago pope francis, and today the european parliament commemorated the victims of these terrible massacres by calling them by their true name genocide. and that's very important. the past is the foundation of the future, colleagues, and we should not be afraid to look back.
it is clear that the issue of employment quotas for disabled people is linked to positive discrimination, which also shows the maturity of our society and the willingness to take action to address the problems of specific groups. but are quotas the answer? i think we should change the evaluation system for the selection of candidates. if we give higher scores to disabled people who want to work in the european union institutions, we will create a real opportunity for them to get into the eu. in ways that disabled people don't feel excluded, and being excluded, being treated differently is a huge problem. another important aspect is the willingness of the european union institutions to accept disabled people. i think if members of parliament closed their eyes and tried to get into their offices with a blind stick, they would probably be surprised at how hard it is to do that, because there's not much infrastructure in place. i'm talking about not having special people escort a blind person to his workplace, because it will again be perceived as discrimination, often labeled as the annoying discrimination of the disabled. let's adapt buildings, equip suitable workplaces, inform disability organisations in all member states of the work we have done, let's allow disabled people to come and see the change, set up systems of positive discrimination against job vacancies and make sure that change happens. that's what i'm calling you to do.
commissioner, we have discussed in this european parliament many times the need to employ as many people with disabilities as possible. however, despite the adoption of numerous conventions, directives and policies prohibiting any discrimination against disabled people in the field of employment, we still do not provide disabled people with sufficient opportunities to work. for example, in the european disability strategy 2010-2020 we call on member states to take the necessary action to facilitate the employment of people with disabilities, but in this strategy we have completely forgotten about the possibilities for the employment of people with disabilities right here in the institutions of the european union. why would you do that? this needs to be fixed immediately. commissioner, i understand from what you said that we do not have specific, accurate statistics on the number of disabled people employed in the european union institutions. we may not know whether those people who are already working have sufficient opportunities to work at a high quality level. in other words, whether they have a suitable working environment. i would therefore ask the commission, which has only recently started its work, to present to us here in the european parliament, perhaps as early as autumn, a strategy with concrete measures on what needs to be done to make the european union institutions an example for all member states in the employment of disabled people.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund for french needs. the application relates to an allocation from the egf of eur 6 052 200 for the benefit of france. it will be allocated to 2513 redundancies at the 'mory-ducros' company. according to the bank of france, the annual number of bankruptcies in the road freight sector increased by 35% between 2007 and 2013. the global financial and economic crisis is thought to have led to a decline of 13.7% in the eu and 21% in france between 2007 and 2012 in the volume of road freight transport by vehicles over 3.5 tonnes. the package of services tailored to the dismissed employees will include guidance and counselling, skills assessment, retraining, vocational training and advice on entrepreneurship.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal to set up a social security committee. this committee will be an advisory body to the council and the commission, and will seek to improve cooperation between the two institutions in the field of social protection. its tasks are to monitor the social situation and the development of social protection policies in the member states and the eu, to promote the exchange of information and good practice between member states and the commission. it also prepares reports and formulates opinions in its fields of competence, either on its own initiative or at the request of the commission or the council. the committee shall be composed of two representatives from each member state and two representatives from the commission.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report on the council decision establishing the social security committee and repealing decision 2004/689/ec. in its conclusions of 17 december 1999 on cooperation in modernising and improving social protection, the council endorsed the commission's proposal to establish a stronger cooperation mechanism, which had been drawn up by a group of high-level officials for the implementation of this action. the council stressed that such cooperation should cover all forms of social protection and, where appropriate, help member states to improve and strengthen their social protection systems on the basis of national priorities. it also recalled the competence of the member states to organise and finance social protection and endorsed the four general objectives of the commission's overall objective of modernising social protection systems: first, to work towards paying for work and guaranteeing a guaranteed income; second, to work towards guaranteeing pensions and creating sustainable pension systems. third, to promote social inclusion and fourth, to ensure high quality, sustainable and accessible healthcare. the council also stressed that the principle of equality between men and women must be respected in all areas of action in order to achieve these four objectives.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the council decision renewing the mandate of the social protection committee and adding new functions. the committee is active in a very important area - providing advice on social security, healthcare, pensions and social inclusion - which is not largely covered by eu law. in the absence of binding decisions for member states, the search for compromise, the exchange of good practice and the identification of elements of good european practice through compromise are of particular importance. i therefore believe that the committee's renewed and clarified mandate will contribute both to more effective coordination of member states' social policies and to the further development and improvement of the informal european governance tool, the open coordination model.

answer to the question posed by the blue card. i think that right now (and this document we're talking about) that's the incentive and the search for a solution to the question you're asking. on one side. on the other hand, we must also take account of the interests of the member states of the european union, the situations in the various countries of the european union, and finally the investments made by businesses, and so on. in this place, we have to look for a reasonable consensus and a reasonable compromise to maximize results. otherwise we will have ambitious goals, we will have high aspirations and, unfortunately, a poor result.

the use of plastic bags is growing. worldwide, about a million are used every minute. it's a serious threat to the environment and to people, so we can't do anything about it. first, new rules and measures to reduce the use of plastic bags must not only be ambitious, but also have a real positive environmental impact. environmental protection must be made economically viable for people. second, only if the reduction targets are based on real consumption data will real and measurable results be achieved. the european union should therefore develop a methodology for the accounting of lightweight plastic bags and only then set mandatory targets for the reduction of plastic bag use, otherwise we will not achieve the result. third, a plastic bag tax could be a good solution to the problem. however, under no circumstances may hidden charges for their use be included in the price of the product. the transition to the new taxation cannot be drastic. together we must promote the use of alternative means.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to empower member states to ratify the international convention on the staff regulations of fishing vessels. international convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for fishing vessel personnel the international maritime organisation adopted the convention in 1995 and the convention in 1996. this convention has been ratified by four member states: spain, denmark, latvia and lithuania. it aims to ensure that the personnel on board fishing vessels are qualified (hold appropriate official certificates) and able to perform their duties (as demonstrated by medical examination) in order to minimise the risk to life and property or the marine environment during fishing operations. fishing is the occupation with the highest accident rate, with 24 000 deaths per year. i agree with the suggestions that in addition to training, it is important to ensure minimum standards of work and safety on board ships in order to prevent accidents at work, and that therefore all member states should apply uniform provisions in accordance with international safety recommendations and that those standards should also apply to ships operating in eu waters.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it expresses parliament's support for the council decision authorising member states, in the interests of the european union, to become parties to the international maritime organisation convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for fishing vessels. it is true that four eu member states, including lithuania, have already ratified the convention. the convention aims to ensure that personnel on board fishing vessels are qualified (hold appropriate official certificates) and capable of performing their duties (as evidenced by medical examination) in order to minimise the risk to life and/or property or the marine environment in the course of fishing vessel operations at sea. the convention requires that the crew have at least the necessary knowledge of certain subjects and have at least the minimum required period of service on board. the convention also promotes vocational training, thus aiming to establish and maintain an appropriate level of productivity in the fisheries sector and to help reduce risks.

in writing. ‒ the international convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for fishing vessels (stcw-f convention) was adopted by the international maritime organisation (imo) in london on 7 july 1995. lithuania is one of the four countries that have ratified the convention. the convention aims to ensure that the personnel on board fishing vessels are qualified, promoting vocational training to help reduce risks and maintain an appropriate level of productivity in the sector. i therefore voted in favour of the decision and i call on the other member states to contribute to the common security and to the training of qualified personnel on board fishing vessels.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to introduce an automated emergency call system 'ecall' in new passenger car models from 31 march 2018, allowing emergency services to respond more quickly to traffic accidents. in 2014 alone, accidents on eu roads claimed 25 700 lives, and the new system is expected to reduce this number by a tenth. the ecall service will be free of charge and independent of the type or price of the vehicle. in the event of a serious accident, the system will automatically collect the single european emergency telephone number 112 and transmit the incident information to the emergency services. this will allow officials and rescuers to reach the scene of an accident faster, reduce injuries and save more lives, and reduce traffic congestion. it is important to strengthen data protection provisions and to ensure that cars are not constantly tracked. the system shall only be activated in the event of an accident or when the driver has pressed the appropriate button. only the minimum set of data will be sent to the emergency services: vehicle class, type of fuel used, number of passengers, and exact time and location of the incident. i agree with the calls for the commission to assess within three years of that deadline whether it would be appropriate to install such a system on buses and lorries. the rules adopted last june obliged eu countries to have the infrastructure in place to receive and process 'ecall' calls by october 2017.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to oblige member states to reduce the use of plastic bags, as they pollute the environment and water bodies and damage ecosystems. in 2010, the average european consumed 198 plastic carrier bags, 90% of which were lightweight. in the same year, more than 8 billion plastic bags were thrown away. these figures are increasing every year. this proposal requires member states to choose between two obligations: either to adopt measures to ensure that the average annual consumption of lightweight plastic shopping bags per person is limited to 90 lightweight plastic shopping bags per person by the end of 2019 and to 40 lightweight plastic shopping bags per person by 2025, or to ensure that no free distribution of plastic shopping bags at the point of sale of goods or products is allowed by the end of 2018 until equally effective measures are in place (i.e. taxation). i agree that member states should report annually on the annual consumption of plastic shopping bags. i support the obligation to label biodegradable and compostable plastic shopping bags and the proposal to assess the environmental impact of biodegradable plastic shopping bags aerobically (additives are added to conventional plastic to break it down into micro-particles over time).

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report and welcome the commission's commitment to advance funding for youth employment programmes. the youth unemployment rate has been dramatically high for several years and is rising steadily. the european union has proposed a number of mechanisms to member states to combat this negative phenomenon, which affects our younger generations. one such instrument is the european union's youth employment initiative, which aims to set policy objectives for the youth guarantee in regions with the highest levels of youth unemployment. unfortunately, this mechanism, which provides opportunities for regions where unemployment among 15-25 year olds exceeds 25%, has not been sufficiently exploited by the member states. one reason for this misuse is that there is not enough public funding to launch projects to offer young people jobs, traineeships or training. member states with the highest levels of youth unemployment are also those with the greatest difficulties in finding common funding. to get started on these crucial projects, the european commission decided to act quickly to mobilise €1 billion.
in writing. ‒ the youth unemployment rate has been dramatically high for several years. despite the fact that the eu has established a mechanism to address youth unemployment, primarily through the youth employment initiative, the member states with the highest youth unemployment rates, above 25%, have not yet been able to make full use of the existing instruments. one reason is the lack of funds needed to co-finance projects and programmes. in view of these problems and the urgency of the matter, the european commission's initiative to allocate eur 1 billion for the financing of youth employment measures at an early stage of projects is timely and should be implemented as soon as possible. i therefore support the proposal for an advance payment to help take the necessary action to reduce the problems of unemployment and youth employment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to repeal council regulation no 3030/93 on common rules for imports of certain textile products from third countries. in recent years, the eu has applied only the bilateral textile trade agreements with russia and serbia. following the accession of russia to the wto and the entry into force of the stabilisation and association agreement with serbia, regulation no 3030/93 lost its primary purpose. therefore, in order to ensure legal certainty, this proposal provides for the repeal of council regulation (eec) no 3030/93.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it supports the commission's proposal to repeal the eu regulation adopted in 1993 laying down common rules for imports of certain textile products from third countries. this regulation was only applicable to third countries with which the eu had concluded bilateral agreements, signed protocols or concluded other agreements. such were russia, serbia, and china. the entry into force of other legal relations with these countries (accession of russia to the wto, entry into force of the stabilisation and association agreement with serbia) has deprived the latter of its primary purpose.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge for the 2013 budget of the imi joint undertaking for innovative medicines. for the third year in a row, the court gave the company a negative opinion, on the grounds that the error rate in the claims for reimbursement of costs remained high (2,3%). - however, imi has taken specific preventive measures to reduce the risk of future errors. moreover, although the error rate remains too high, it has fallen sharply compared to the error rate of 5,82% in 2012 and is therefore not a sufficient reason for not granting the imi discharge.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as it confirms the european parliament's confirmation of the interim executive director of the innovative medicines initiative joint undertaking that the joint undertaking's budget for the implementation of the joint technology initiative 'innovative medicines' for the financial year 2013 has been implemented. the joint technology initiative 'new medicines' was established in december 2007 for a period of 10 years to significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the drug development process and to achieve the long-term goal of making the pharmaceutical sector produce more effective and safer innovative medicines.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge for the joint undertaking for the implementation of the joint technology initiative 'new medicines' for the financial year 2013, as the court of auditors has found that the joint undertaking's annual accounts present fairly, in all material respects, its financial position as at 31 december 2013 and the results of its operations and cash flows for the financial year ended on that date, as required by its financial rules and the accounting rules adopted by the commission's accounting officer. i support the resolution's call for the institution's shortcomings to be addressed as soon as possible, in particular with regard to the observations of the commission's internal audit service. i agree with the need to ensure the added value and the effective implementation of union research, technological development and demonstration programmes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the discharge for the implementation of the budget of the european joint undertaking for the development of fusion energy and iter for 2013. the cont committee voted in favour of postponing the discharge of the iter budget on the grounds that the cost of implementing this project was twice as high as planned, that no system for monitoring expenditure deviations had been set up, that there were delays in public procurement and that the court had not been fully informed of the progress made. however, it is important to underline that the court of auditors has delivered a favourable opinion on the iter 2013 accounts, which is the basis for granting discharge. the joint undertaking is also well aware of the problems listed and has taken action to address them. since 2013, iter has made a number of improvements in its internal control and cost assessment systems, reporting, conflict of interest management, intellectual property protection and dissemination of results. the iter project is the first international research project of its kind and is very complex from a technical point of view, which has led to delays and cost overruns. for these reasons, it is important that iter be granted a discharge.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is the european parliament's confirmation to the director of the european joint undertaking for iter and the development of fusion energy that the joint undertaking's budget for the financial year 2013 has been implemented. parliament gave its discharge to the court of auditors on the basis that the 2013 annual accounts of the joint undertaking correctly present, in all material respects, the financial position of the joint undertaking as at 31 december 2013 and the results of the operations and cash flows for the financial year ended on that date, in accordance with the provisions of its financial rules.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal on money market funds (mmfs). pff provides short-term financing to financial institutions, companies or governments. by providing funding to these entities, mmfs contribute to the financing of the european economy. i agree with the rules for the operation of the prg set out in this proposal. as regards the risk mitigation requirements for mmfs, they need to be harmonised by establishing clear rules that impose direct obligations on mmfs and their managers across the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because it is the european parliament's proposal for a regulation on money market funds. money market funds (mmfs) are an important source of short-term funding for financial institutions, corporations and governments. in europe, about 22% of short-term debt securities issued by the government or corporate sector are held by money market funds. the prf also owns 38% of the short-term debt securities issued by the banking sector. in relation to demand, mmfs are short-term money management instruments that ensure a high level of liquidity, diversification and value stability, as well as market-based returns. prfs are mainly used by companies wishing to invest surplus money for a short period, for example, until large costs such as wage costs are incurred. thus, the mmf is the essential link between short-term money demand and supply.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because the eu's money market funds are a great tool to help finance the european economy. in providing short-term financing, these entities use investments in mmfs as an efficient means of allocating credit risk and exposure, rather than relying solely on bank deposits. however, it is essential to ensure appropriate regulation and to assess the risks. i would point out that the authorities must cooperate and exchange information in order to ensure an appropriate monitoring and control process. the money market funds must be a sound instrument for the union industry's money management.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal to codify and recast regulation no 517/94 of 7 march 1994 on textile products.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it supports the commission's proposal for a new version of the regulation on textile products not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols or other agreements or by other specific union import rules. the proposal is part of the harmonisation process following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon to ensure that the previous decision-making procedures in the field of trade policy are aligned with the new procedure for delegated and implementing acts. during this process, the commission identified certain errors that needed to be corrected. in order to incorporate some substantive changes, it was decided that the codification should be replaced by a new wording. these amendments are essentially technical corrections.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols or other agreements or by other specific union import rules, since many of them are only technical changes that need to be implemented after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon in order to ensure that the previous decision-making procedures in the field of trade policy are aligned with the new procedure for delegated and implementing acts. during this process, the commission identified certain errors that needed to be corrected. it is important that the rules applied are clear to the operators concerned, easy to apply and provide legal certainty.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it sets out the european parliament's position on the estimates of revenue and expenditure for the financial year 2016. the communication notes that parliament, in assessing the current high level of public debt in the member states and the budgetary consolidation they are undertaking, must show a responsible approach to the budget and to austerity, while ensuring that sufficient resources are allocated to enable parliament to exercise all its powers and to ensure the proper functioning of the institution. the communication also reiterates that structural and organisational reforms aimed at greater efficiency, environmental sustainability and effectiveness should continue to be pursued in the context of the exploration of synergies and cost savings, and recalls that a substantial amount of money could be saved if the institution had only one, rather than three, posts as it has today.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution, but against the proposals to increase the budget of the assistants, to increase the budget of political parties and foundations, because it is a waste of taxpayers' money. i voted for the amendment to the so-called 'one-seat' system, i supported the proposals for greater transparency of payments.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to establish a european public prosecutor's office. in cases of fraud to misappropriate eu funds, increased prosecution, and recovery of funds, criminal offences will be investigated and prosecuted by a single independent prosecutor at european level. even if the current system works well in some member states, it is ineffective at eu level in terms of prosecution and recovery. the recovery of a relatively small proportion of our citizens' taxes is unacceptable and must change immediately. in its resolution of 12 march 2014, the european parliament called on the council to ensure its full involvement in its work and made a number of policy proposals to address the most important aspects, namely the structure, autonomy, decision-making process, competence, investigative measures, admissibility of evidence, judicial review and legal protection. the council of justice and home affairs has so far focused on a collegiate service, composed of one european prosecutor from each member state and headed by a prosecutor-general, and the competing jurisdiction of the new prosecutor's office and national prosecutor's offices.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it is the european parliament's position on the structure, mandate and operating procedures of the future european public prosecutor's office. the eu loses at least 500 million in expenditure and revenue every year as a result of suspected fraud. the european public prosecutor's office will investigate crimes involving eu funds and prosecute suspects in national courts. the new prosecutor's office would be an independent body and a link between the criminal justice systems of the eu member states, whose powers are limited by national borders, and the eu institutions, which do not have the power to investigate crimes. the european public prosecutor's office will be integrated into national judicial systems, and eu prosecutors will investigate and prosecute crimes in the eu. they will work with national work groups and apply national law. the eppo will ensure that prosecutors in all countries follow the same operating methods.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a council regulation on the establishment of the european public prosecutor's office because, having read the document and the jurisdictional situation, i have come to the conclusion that, while the current system works well in some member states, it appears to be rather ineffective at union level in terms of criminal prosecution and recovery. in the context of the european institution, fraud to misappropriate eu funds, increased prosecution, and recovery of funds, criminal offences will be investigated and prosecuted by a single independent prosecutor at european level. this will increase eu citizens' confidence in eu jurisdiction and institutions.
madam president, it is very regrettable that from year to year we see so little progress on the bosnia and herzegovina side in the european integration process. remaining major blockages, as well as internal political divisions and tensions, do not allow agreement and the adoption of required strategies that would enable the country to use the available european pre-accession financial instruments. the lack of clear political direction in the country and lack of determination deprive the country and its people of the long-term economic and social benefits the eu is willing and able to offer to bosnia and herzegovina. thus i call on the leaders of the country to show initiative and willingness to direct the country to the european path.
in writing. ‒ the european union is one of the top alcohol consumers in the world, with an annual average of 10.7 litres per person (aged 15 or older). the misuse of alcohol is one of the major causes of preventable death and of diseases such as liver and heart disease and cancer. it has been estimated that the social cost of alcohol misuse is more than eur 150 billion per year. at the moment the commission is doing nothing to solve the alcohol misuse problem. therefore, i support ms willmott’s resolution urging it to take action. the commission had an alcohol strategy from 2006 to 2012: however, it was not renewed after its expiration in 2013. i believe that an immediate and effective strategy is needed for the upcoming years in order to raise awareness about important issues such as drink driving and drinking while pregnant. it is essential for the wellbeing of our society that the new strategy is adopted as soon as possible. i hope that this resolution will make the commission take further steps with regard to this issue.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution, which aims to encourage the commission to draw up a new eu alcohol strategy (2016-2022) and to encourage the labelling of alcoholic beverages to indicate their energy value, as alcohol is very high in calories, but many people do not know this. i agree that consumers have a right to clear and fair labelling of alcoholic beverages in order to make correct, objective and informed decisions. the objectives of the new strategy are to help national governments reduce alcohol-related harm, support the collection of reliable data, promote prevention, health promotion and education, early diagnosis, better treatment options, provide ongoing support to dependent individuals and their families, including psychological counselling programmes, and reduce alcohol-related road accidents, etc. in 2010, the social costs of alcohol abuse in europe, directly or indirectly, amounted to €155.8 billion. alcohol abuse causes 3.3 million deaths a year, or 5.9% of all deaths, and harmful drinking is the third leading preventable cause of illness and death in europe, alcohol is linked to more than 60 chronic diseases, including cancer, heart and liver disease and obesity. alcohol abuse is also associated with other social problems, including job loss, divorce, and violence. europe also has the highest alcohol consumption in the world.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it calls on the european parliament to update the eu resolution on the eu strategy against alcohol for 2016-2022. alcohol abuse is one of the most common causes of lifestyle-related diseases in the eu, and alcohol dependence puts more than 60 chronic diseases at risk. in the eu, alcohol is the main cause of premature deaths, accounting for 5.9% of all deaths. in the 20-39 age group, a quarter of all deaths are alcohol-related. parliament believes that the future eu alcohol strategy should aim to update the regulatory framework to help national governments reduce alcohol-related harm, support monitoring and the collection of reliable data, promote prevention, health education and training, early diagnosis, better treatment options, provide ongoing support to dependent individuals and their families, including psychological counselling programmes, and reduce alcohol-related road traffic accidents and better differentiate alcohol consumption habits, behaviours and attitudes.
in writing. ‒ the i welcome the efforts of the european commission to reduce alcohol consumption in europe. addiction and health are problems at european level that unfortunately cannot be effectively addressed by states and communities. according to official statistics, 12 million people in the eu are dependent on alcohol. 1 in 4 road accidents in the eu is caused by non-drivers. in 2010, almost 31 000 europeans died on the roads, 25% of these deaths were attributable to alcohol. the social damage caused by alcohol consumption is estimated at eur 155.8 billion per year, and is the main cause of poor health and premature death among the working age population (25-59 years). in considering the alcohol strategy in the european parliament and analysing the proposals, i also understand the efforts of representatives of individual southern countries to legalise the notions of responsible consumption. however, what may be normal in spain or italy, with their culture of moderate consumption, is not at all appropriate for lithuania and many northern and eastern european countries. in lithuania, nearly a quarter of 15-year-olds drink alcohol every week. alcoholism rates are similar to those in russia and belarus. i believe that the european union cannot compromise on this issue and that the direction of the stock exchange policy must be totally unfavourable to alcohol consumption and aimed at reducing alcohol sales every year. therefore, no consumption, even moderate consumption, can be encouraged. therefore, recital p, paragraph 5 and in particular paragraph 16 of the draft had to be corrected.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which aims to mark the second anniversary of the collapse of the rana plaza building and to assess progress in the implementation of the sustainability agreement. two years ago, the rana plaza garment factory complex collapsed in bangladesh. the disaster killed 1,100 people. as the world's second largest exporter of clothing, the country exports more than half of its production to the eu. but the people who make it work under dangerous conditions. with the support of the eu and the international labour organisation, a number of changes have been made. it was agreed to improve supervision of the operation of factories and to improve fire and electrical safety rules. in addition, the minimum wage has increased and the role of trade unions has been strengthened. the bangladesh sustainability agreement is an agreement between the eu and the government of bangladesh, also supported by the ilo. in part, this agreement has led to changes in bangladesh's labour law. public pressure and the potential damage to reputation led international brands associated with 'rana plaza' to become more involved in the resolution of this issue.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it marks the second anniversary of the rana plaza building collapse and the progress made in implementing the bangladesh sustainability agreement. on 24 april 2013, an eight-storey building called rana plaza, which housed several garment factories, collapsed in the savar area near dhaka, killing over 1,100 people and injuring more than 2,500. the collapse of the rana plaza building is the worst industrial disaster in bangladesh and the deadliest tragedy in modern history caused by a structural defect. on 24 november 2012, a fire at a factory in tazreen, dhaka's ashullia district, killed at least 112 people. parliament welcomed the steps taken to establish a permanent national occupational accident insurance scheme and, in this regard, called on the government of bangladesh to fulfil its commitment to the implementation of the national tripartite action plan. however, it remains concerned about the alleged corruption between health and safety inspectors and garment factory owners in bangladesh and calls for more efforts to be made to combat this practice.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it is the european parliament's expression of support for the victims and their families on the second anniversary of the collapse of the 'rana plaza'. the collapse of the rana plaza building, which housed several garment factories and in which more than 1,100 people died and more than 2,500 were injured, was the worst industrial disaster in bangladesh and the deadliest tragedy in modern history. parliament welcomed the steps taken to establish a permanent national occupational accident insurance scheme and, in this regard, called on the government of bangladesh to fulfil its commitment to the implementation of the national tripartite action plan. it also calls for the rooted corruption between health and safety inspectors and garment factory owners to be addressed.
