author.– mr president, the detention of nadiya savchenko is unlawful and inhumane. the minsk agreements must be respected in full. this was still being pointed out by 61 members of this house back on 17 october of last year, when we co-signed the first public appeal to president putin. in addition, for the last three months, on every single day, yet another member of the european parliament sends a letter to the russian ambassador in brussels. sixty letters have been sent up to now. it is not that we expect to get any kind of reply; what we expect is for russia to act in a civilised and 21st century european manner. it is appalling that president putin chooses to keep nadiya savchenko detained as his personal prisoner. as a consequence, the savchenko list, together with the magnitsky list, are becoming tools for dealing with putin’s russia, and this is very sad.
on 17 june 2014, a terrorist group in the lugansk region took hostage a former ukrainian air force (kop) pilot, nadezhda savchenko. on 24 june 2014, she was illegally transferred to russia, where she was charged with criminal offences by the russian investigative committee. as of 1 january 2014, she was a member of the 'people's council' of the so-called 'donetsk people's republic'. following a prolonged hunger strike, savchenko's health is in very poor condition. in the framework of the exchange of prisoners of war provided for in the minsk agreements, 'all for all' was to include mr savchenko in the list of prisoners of war, but the russian side rejected this possibility. the european parliament strongly condemns the russian federation for the abduction and unlawful detention of ms savchenko, which has been going on for a year, and calls for her immediate release.
mr president, in 2007 during the plenary debates the european parliament praised the agreements signed between the commission and philip morris, and generally the agreements with other tobacco producers were regarded as a success story. a lot has been achieved in combating illicit cigarette trade and smuggling, especially when we look back to the 1990s. however, the eu continues losing around eur 10 billion annually, and the greatest influx of smuggled cigarettes comes through external eu borders, including in the baltic region. thus cigarette smuggling remains a very acute problem and further improvements are vitally required in this area. but in order to take a position on whether we should continue with such agreements with tobacco companies after 2016, we must have relevant information on what was achieved and what the shortcomings were under the current agreements.
mr president, it is a pleasure to have the commissioner and vice—president here tonight. commissioner, i am not sure if you are the right member of the commission for this issue that we have with vat. i can see the uk has a lot of problems with it; other countries are happy about the changes because smaller countries are sometimes at a disadvantage when there is competition in relation to taxation and vat rates. it is a very complex situation, and we tend to make things very complex in europe, unfortunately. i would suggest something though, which is to change the name ‘e-book’ into simply ‘dc’ (digital content). we should just change it to dc because we no longer know what a book is or what it becomes, and once you open it up you have live content and you are doing something else with it. so let us start thinking ahead of the curve, forget the past and see where these things will be in the future. the future will be a digital content single market. we need to be proactive and not reactive. i know the commissioner is himself, so i would say: be brave; make very simple decisions to simplify europe – for businesses to understand how things work. whatever the tax is, make it very easy so that they can pay it easily and not have to close down. that is all it is about. it is going to be difficult to agree on rates for all of us, but we can definitely make things very simple and understandable.
in writing.– currently the eu’s ambitions to create a common digital single market are being largely obstructed by administrative hurdles such as different vat rules across the union and, more specifically, an unequal treatment of similar non—digital and digital services and goods. i hold the view that this not only distorts fair competition, discourages smes and e-commerce but also makes digital goods much more difficult and expensive for eu consumers to access. hence, i think that there is a great practical need to have a uniform vat regime in the eu. moreover, i believe that the derogations and reduced vat rates should be applied for digital books, journals and magazines as they are now already applied for the printed books (their physical counterparts) due to being classified as cultural goods. this would not only benefit producers and consumers but could have a positive impact on the development of digital information base, research and innovation. finally, it must be noted that the digital sphere develops extremely fast, and if we want to keep up our competitiveness on the world scale there is an urgent need for action and the commission should step up its efforts to address this issue.
it must be recognised that smes already provide services that contribute to environmentally sustainable economic growth. however, often due to a lack of resources, they operate in a defined territory and their ideas, products and services are known only to a limited number of people. so it's not uncommon for small businesses to invest a lot of time and resources reinventing the bike. i therefore support the ideas put forward in the report that not only should these enterprises be supported and the conditions for their use of aid facilitated, but that european networks of small enterprises should be developed. both informal networks and the european centre of excellence for resource efficiency should help companies to exchange good practices and knowledge to ensure efficient use of resources. in order to promote green and sustainable economic development, we also need to develop a simple consumer information system. by empowering consumers, we will not only support sustainable business, but we will also change people's daily habits and attitudes towards the damage they do to the environment.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council covers crucial aspects of security and peace in the world. the extraction of natural resources, especially in conflict-affected countries of the so-called third world, can be a source of conflict. the commission has also found that the use of rare earths in the mining sector is not in line with the environmental objectives of the union. this regulation, which seeks to break the link between illegal mineral exploitation and international disputes, is therefore worth reviewing. the main objective of our legislation in this area must be to promote peace and stability in the world's most at-risk areas. in this context, the project establishing an eu certification scheme for importers who wish to develop responsible imports of rare metals into the european union is of positive significance. this means that international relations must be conducted in accordance with specific standards that are in line with oecd recommendations. however, the recommendations explicitly state the obligation to ensure thorough security in the mineral supply chain from conflict-affected areas in order to eliminate any potential risk of human rights violations. and that's what we're seeing today. the oecd reference should be recognised as one of the most important references in the development of new international law. the commission's proposal, known as the 'do no harm' principle, deserves support. the union must take the lead in this area in order to be able to influence more effectively the way peaceful conflict resolution is achieved.
mr president, we are very fortunate to have such a bright commissioner in a very important post in an area that is going to be the future of europe. however, commissioner, let us be very pro-active and not reactive. for example, uber is a great service from america and there are now so many fighting back against it, so many states – including the big country that we are in right now – fighting this company that allows young people to work and make a fair living by working hard. that is what applications and the digital single market will achieve for europe: letting young people work and be rated by what they do. people can order their services, so let us be proactive, let us allow young people to earn a fair living – and ‘fair’ is whatever they are worth. whatever work they do, however good they are. that is what being fair is – it is not what states tell you ʽfairʼ is, or the red tape and the bureaucracy that we propose. let the digital single market be a revolution. good luck to you, commissioner. we support you. let us all work and focus.

in writing. - i voted for this motion. directive 98/84/ec establishes a common eu-wide legal framework to combat the unauthorised use of pay-tv services and to protect such services effectively. such protection means that any commercial activity involving the use of facilities which provide access to services without the authorisation or payment of the supplier is considered illegal and subject to penalties. as early as 1999, the council started work on the european convention on the legal protection of conditional access services and conditional access services. the eu signature of the convention should encourage more council of europe member states to ratify it, thus extending the legal protection of conditional access-based services beyond the eu.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which gives parliament its support for the conclusion of the european convention on the legal protection of services based on conditional access and of services based on conditional access. the european council started the preparation of this european convention back in 1999, as a comprehensive and effective protection of conditional access services and conditional access services is necessary. this convention extends the directive adopted by the council and the european parliament in 1998 which establishes a common legal framework for the european union as a whole to combat the unauthorised use of pay-tv services and to protect them effectively. the protection also extends to the transmission of traditional television and radio programmes and their transmission via the internet. many european countries outside the european union can become havens for the development and distribution of pirated content based on conditional access services, when their legal systems do not provide for sanctions for this very specific pirated activity. the application of the provisions of directive 98/84/ec should therefore be extended and a common and effective system of protection of those services should be established at european level.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft european convention on the legal protection of services based on conditional access and of services based on conditional access on behalf of the european union, as such a decision is based on european union law and does not contradict the case law of the court of justice of the european union.
in writing. ‒ the i am in favour of the conclusion of the convention, as a common and effective system of protection for these services needs to be established at european level. an effective common eu-wide legal framework should be in place to combat illegal means of unauthorised access to pay-tv services and to protect such services effectively. the protection of conditional access services and conditional access services is necessary in view of the specific nature of this piracy activity. it is necessary to harmonise national provisions on measures against illegal devices that allow unauthorised access to protected services, thereby preventing illegal activities. providers of conditional access services or services based on conditional access must be given access to appropriate legal remedies and must be provided with an effective mechanism for redress.

in writing. ‒ the i support the vote to postpone this proposal for further discussion. it provides for new rules to increase the credibility of interbank interest rates, which determine the price of loans. the draft new rules aim to prevent conflicts of interest that could affect the formation of benchmarks such as libor (london interbank offered rate) or euribor (euro interbank lending rate). these two interbank interest rates affect the value of financial instruments and contracts in excess of eur 500 billion and can therefore directly affect the stability of eu financial markets. it is proposed that all index administrators who collect, analyse and process non-public data should register with the european securities and markets authority and publish an 'index certificate' indicating what is being measured by the index and how reliable it is.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the common position on the council and european parliament regulation on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts. benchmarks are essential for pricing cross-border transactions and thus for facilitating the effective functioning of the internal market in a wide range of financial instruments and services. many benchmarks used as reference standards in financial contracts, in particular mortgages, are drawn up in one member state but used by credit institutions and consumers in other member states. moreover, these credit institutions often hedge their risks or obtain financing to enter into these financial contracts in the cross-border interbank market. the scope of this regulation should be as broad as possible in so far as it is necessary to establish a system of preventive regulation. the development and setting of benchmarks is discretionary and inherently entails certain types of conflicts of interest, which means that there are opportunities and incentives to manipulate those benchmarks. those risk factors are common to all benchmarks and should therefore be subject to appropriate governance and control requirements.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report containing the european parliament's proposals for the draft regulation on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts presented by the commission. this regulation establishes a common framework to ensure the accuracy and fairness of those indices. this contributes to the proper functioning of the internal market while ensuring a high level of consumer and investor protection. the amendments aim to reduce the possibility of manipulation and abuse of benchmarks, to ensure a wider range of benchmarks and thus to increase the transparency of the system.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to ensure the accuracy, soundness and fairness of benchmarks and the process of setting them. in order to achieve the objectives pursued, a regulatory framework for benchmarks should be established and applied in the eu to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market and to guarantee a high level of consumer and investor protection. greater attention should be paid to the protection of benchmarks against manipulation. it should be noted that such illegal activities may undermine market confidence, cause losses to consumers and investors, and distort the real economy.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the report. the eu is the world's leading donor of development aid. it is therefore essential that clear and transparent data on all eu development budgetary allocations are provided on a regular basis. it is worth noting that financing the sdgs is a major challenge. in this context, the global partnership should be given greater attention. in addition, the use of all forms of financing and non-financial instruments should be encouraged. it should be noted that private funding can complement public funding but cannot in any way replace it. clear spending priorities are essential to achieve the objectives set. i believe that the eu's strong commitment to focusing more on the quantity and quality of development aid should also serve as an example for other public and private donors who must honour their financial commitments.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to improve patient safety and bacterial resistance. healthcare-associated infections affect 8-12% of patients admitted to hospital in the eu. according to the european centre for disease prevention and control, these infections affect an average of 1 in 20 patients admitted to hospital in the eu, or 4.1 million patients per year, and cause over 37 000 deaths in the eu each year. it is estimated that 20 to 30 percent of these infections could be prevented by implementing intensive hygiene and control programmes. the threat to patient safety is posed by austerity measures that reduce healthcare costs. i support the proposals put forward to invest in continuing education, monitoring and prevention of medical and health services in order to avoid a significant number of adverse events. it is also important to establish forms of compensation and to assess how the presence of specific preparations in the premises where patients are treated is regulated. the main focus of patient management should be on prudent use of available antibiotics and on national and international action to restrict the movement of patients infected with resistant bacteria.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with patient safety and the fight against drug resistance, in particular antimicrobial resistance. it is therefore more important than ever to ensure that patient safety, i.e. the right of the patient not to be harmed by therapeutic treatment, is a central element of healthcare systems. unfortunately, the economic crisis has put increasing pressure on member states' budgets, which has affected patient safety, and many member states have drastically reduced the budget and staffing levels of their health systems by failing to address the issue of efficiency. in addition, the economic crisis has further exacerbated existing disparities in access to healthcare. it is therefore necessary to draw attention, first of all, to the fact that the risk to patient safety is posed by austerity measures implemented to cut healthcare costs. these horizontal cuts directly affect the quality of care, which is unacceptable. the treatment must therefore be patient-centred and the funds allocated to health systems must not be unnecessarily cut in order to save money. investment is needed in continuous training, medical and health services monitoring, early warning systems and prevention to avoid a significant proportion of adverse events, including those caused by medication.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on safer healthcare in europe because i agree with the provisions contained therein no cuts in health systems' budgets due to economic difficulties can be a reason to compromise on patient safety. it is unacceptable that funding cuts in national health systems are at the expense of quality of care. you have to save wisely. improve national health systems: invest in continuing education, monitoring of medical and health services, early warning systems and, most importantly, prevention. this would make the work more efficient and would not endanger the lives of patients.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report. patient safety is a key element of healthcare systems. treatment should be for the patient's well-being. it is therefore necessary to continuously improve patient safety and to remove barriers to improving patient safety. health care is becoming increasingly complex and risky. quality assurance and continuous improvement, with a particular focus on health safety, therefore become a major challenge. first, it is necessary to ensure adequate funding of health systems. the budgetary allocation for health systems must not be allowed to be unduly cut in order to save money. strict austerity measures should not affect patient safety. in addition, investment in continuing education, monitoring of medical and health services, early warning systems and prevention needs to be encouraged. specific ambitious targets should be set to reduce the use of antibiotics.

madam president, europe does not belong to federalists or eurosceptics. it belongs to europeans, and they need peace and security. we must act accordingly and reflect real needs. indeed, the european union needs to take practical and effective steps towards a well-functioning common space of security and defence. we need to be able to react properly and in a timely way to tackle emerging risks and especially to prevent them from happening. there is no risk that the eu, by strengthening its common security and defence policy, will become a hard power and a risk to its neighbours. the european union is a democratic structure and is run by the rule of law. i believe our discussion today will help us to go in this direction, and indeed to build this common space of security and defence on our continent.
despite the important decisions taken in recent years, it is clear that member states still lack greater focus on this issue. let's be honest, almost all member states are looking at each other right now, expecting who will provide their security. or they're just concerned about the security of their country. we cannot wait, we must know today what concrete measures we will take together in the face of any internal or external challenges. proper coordination, clear planning, a greater focus on crisis prevention and preparedness, adequate funding for the implementation of security and defence policy - that is what we lack. there is no doubt that increased funding also requires greater transparency, and i fully agree that there should be an evaluation of the effectiveness of the 17 european missions abroad. but funding is not the only problem. a telling fact: not all member states are involved in the military operations conducted by the union. it is time to put an end to the loud declarations and to start working on the substance of european security and defence.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am categorically opposed to the application of quotas to the european union member states in the so-called african immigrant relocation programme. it's the wrong way. it will not solve problems but will make them worse. what does a quota of 20,000 migrants mean when 150,000 refugees reach europe each year from the mediterranean alone? again, we are told to deal not with causes but with consequences. it's unreasonable, illogical and ineffective. refugees' quotas are not milk production quotas for the eu countries, which are much easier to regulate mechanically. quota policy will be nothing in the end, it will only encourage more migration to europe, because it will send a signal: 'you are welcome here, you will be taken care of here'. but the message to african countries, to their governments, should be very different. only stable peace in the region, only adequate control of its borders, must henceforth be the sole and indisputable condition for the negotiations by the european union institutions on donors' financial, technological and humanitarian aid and trade agreements.
in writing. globalisation is a path to greater prosperity, but any fundamental process has negative consequences. we can be neutral when it comes to the movement of goods, but when economic hardship causes mass migration, we must speak first of all about human dignity, ethics, human rights. it is clear that in a europe without borders, solidarity on migration needs to be promoted, and it should not be a matter for border states alone. if europe was in solidarity with us, the baltic states, when we suffered the consequences of the russian embargo, today we must be in solidarity with italy. solidarity cannot be partial or one-sided. it is to be welcomed that the member states have come together to tackle this important issue. however, the distribution of migrants among different countries is not a long-term solution. i think we can invest more in preventing the influx of migrants and crises. it is equally important to ensure that the public is adequately informed about the implementation of the common agenda on migration. there are a lot of stereotypes, a lot of fears that are being raised by politicians in this room. we must ensure that the people of the european union understand the justification for our actions.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation, in which the european parliament supports the conclusion of an additional protocol to the eu-south africa trade, development and cooperation agreement. the additional protocol was approved by the council on 9 october 2014 and by south africa at the end of december 2014. the additional protocol is intended only to incorporate into the trade, development and cooperation agreement (tdaa) of the republic of south africa a number of technical and linguistic amendments which are necessary following the accession of croatia to the european union. the signature of the additional protocol is necessary for the republic of croatia to become a contracting party to the saa. the croatian language is added to the list of languages in which the texts of the additional protocol to the teu are authentic. the government of the republic of south africa is currently deciding which authorised representative it will instruct to sign the additional protocol. the council shall wait for the adoption of the said decision before arranging for signature. once the protocol has been signed, the council will formally request the european parliament to give its consent to the conclusion of the protocol.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal on the protection of the financial system against the use of money laundering and terrorist financing, which aims at strengthening the fight against money laundering. money laundering accounts for between 2 and 5 percent of global gdp each year. the new rules will require the publication of the true owners of companies in the central registers of eu countries, and make this information available to public authorities and to persons with a legitimate interest, such as journalists. it also lays down new rules on the transfer of funds, which should facilitate the traceability of funds. in negotiations with the eu council, the european parliament succeeded in ensuring that the updated money laundering directive would oblige eu countries to publish the beneficial owners of companies, funds and other legal entities in their central registers. in addition, banks, auditors, lawyers, real estate agents and casinos will have to monitor suspicious customer transactions more closely.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation, which supports the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purpose of money laundering or terrorist financing. this directive is proposed to strengthen the internal market and, in particular, to reduce the complexity of cross-border movement, to protect the public against crime and terrorist acts, to safeguard the economic well-being of the european union by ensuring an efficient business environment and to enhance financial stability. the removal of barriers in the internal market not only makes it easier to set up or develop a legitimate business across the eu, but also creates more opportunities for money laundering and terrorist financing. therefore, money laundering criminals may try to conceal or disguise the true nature, source or ownership of the assets concerned. european legislation has been adopted to safeguard the proper functioning of the financial system and the internal market. however, the evolving nature of money laundering and terrorist financing threats, which is facilitated by the continuous evolution of technology and criminal tactics, requires the legal framework to be continuously adapted to counter such threats.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purpose of money laundering or terrorist financing. the world doesn't stand still. the eu's internal market, financial systems, economic conditions and technology are changing. criminals who launder money or help finance terrorism are adapting to a changing world. it is therefore necessary to keep the legal framework up to date and modernised in order to adequately counter these threats.
in writing. ‒ the i agree with the position. we must do more to protect society from crime and terrorist acts, and the economic well-being of the european union by ensuring an effective business environment. financial stability needs to be enhanced by ensuring the soundness, orderly functioning and integrity of the financial system. it is therefore essential to ensure that the eu has an effective system in place to prevent the use of the financial system for money laundering or terrorist financing. in order to achieve the objectives pursued, it is appropriate to extend the scope of the directive beyond casinos to the entire gaming sector. in addition, it is necessary to include tax crimes in the scope of the directive. it is essential to strengthen the sanctions regime. in particular, it is necessary to lay down the minimum rules of principle for the purpose of strengthening administrative penalties. it is also appropriate to carry out a threat assessment and to take timely mitigation measures.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal on information on transfers of funds, which aims to strengthen the fight against money laundering. money laundering accounts for between 2 and 5 percent of global gdp each year. the new rules will require the publication of the true owners of companies in the central registers of eu countries, and make this information available to public authorities and to persons with a legitimate interest, such as journalists. it also lays down new rules on the transfer of funds, which should facilitate the traceability of funds. in negotiations with the eu council, the european parliament succeeded in ensuring that the updated money laundering directive would oblige eu countries to publish the beneficial owners of companies, funds and other legal entities in their central registers. in addition, banks, auditors, lawyers, real estate agents and casinos will have to monitor suspicious customer transactions more closely.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation, which endorses the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on information to be provided in the context of transfers of funds and repealing regulation (ec) no 1781/2006. given the changing nature of money laundering and terrorist financing threats and the growing number of threats due to the continuous development of technologies and tools available to criminals, the commission proposed to revise regulation (ec) no 1781/2006 on payer information to be provided when funds are transferred, in order to increase the traceability of payments and ensure that the eu system is fully in line with international standards. this proposal is consistent with and complements the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the protection of the financial system against money laundering and terrorist financing. these two legal instruments share the common objective of reviewing the existing system of the european union for the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing in order to improve its effectiveness while ensuring its compatibility with international standards. the proposal is also in line with the eu's internal security strategy, which identifies the most pressing eu security challenges for the coming years and proposes five strategic objectives and specific actions for a safer eu in 2011-2014. among them addressing money laundering and terrorism prevention issues, in particular updating the eu system to increase transparency of beneficial ownership information on legal entities.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the council position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on information to be provided in the course of transfers of funds and repealing regulation (ec) no 1781/2006. the commission has proposed to complement the relevant legislation with provisions to facilitate the traceability of payments and to ensure that the eu legal framework is in line with international standards. this and other related legal instruments pursue the common objective of a safer european union. this is particularly important in the light of changing circumstances and technologies used by criminals who also engage in money laundering or terrorist financing.
in writing. ‒ the i agree with the position. i believe that the time has come to review the eu's existing system for preventing money laundering and terrorist financing in order to improve its effectiveness. it is important to note that the nature of money laundering and terrorist financing threats is constantly changing and that threats are increasing due to the constant evolution of technology and the tools available to criminals. it is therefore important to ensure that the eu system is fully in line with international standards. in particular, the eu should have common and sufficiently stringent rules on information provided by the payer and the payee when transferring funds. this will improve the traceability of payments. in order to prevent discrimination in relation to national payments within a member state and international payments between member states, an international standard needs to be transposed into national law in a uniform manner throughout the union.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to make the european system for crossborder insolvency proceedings more efficient, thus ensuring the smooth functioning of the internal market and its resilience to economic crises. the bankruptcy regulation establishes a european framework for the cross-border insolvency of companies. the regulation applies where the debtor's assets or creditors are located in more than one member state. the regulation establishes the court with jurisdiction to open bankruptcy proceedings the main proceedings must be brought in the member state where the debtor's main interests are located and the consequences of the proceedings are recognised throughout the eu. the bankruptcy regulation applies to all member states except denmark, which does not participate in judicial cooperation.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation, which endorses the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on insolvency proceedings. this new proposal amends council regulation (ec) no 1346/2000 on the insolvency procedure. the bankruptcy regulation establishes a european framework for the cross-border insolvency of companies. the regulation applies where the debtor's assets or creditors are located in more than one member state. the regulation establishes the court with jurisdiction to open bankruptcy proceedings the main proceedings must be brought in the member state where the debtor's main interests are located and the consequences of the proceedings are recognised throughout the eu. the secondary proceedings may be brought in the place where the debtor is established; the secondary proceedings shall be brought only in respect of the debtor's assets situated in that state. the regulation also lays down rules for determining the applicable law and for coordinating certain main and secondary insolvency proceedings. the bankruptcy regulation applies to all member states except denmark, which does not participate in judicial cooperation under the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the objective of the review of the bankruptcy regulation is to increase the efficiency of the european system for the crossborder insolvency of creditors, thereby ensuring the smooth functioning of the internal market and its resilience to economic crises. this objective is in line with the current eu policy priorities to promote economic recovery and sustainable growth, investment and job preservation, as set out in the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on bankruptcy proceedings. the bankruptcy regulation establishes a european framework for the cross-border insolvency of companies. this regulation shall apply where the debtor natural or legal person has assets or creditors in more than one member state. other rules on the conduct of bankruptcy proceedings of this type are also laid down. the regulation is being reviewed with a view to making the european system of cross-border insolvency proceedings more efficient.
in writing. ‒ the i agree with the position that the changes envisaged will not create better conditions for the protection of companies in financial difficulties and on the verge of bankruptcy. in particular, the new regulation will help to address the practical problems of the administration of insolvency proceedings involving persons from several member states of the european union. it will also prevent abuse of rights in the pursuit of a more favourable legal position. issues relating to the opening of main and ancillary insolvency proceedings and their interrelationship, as well as issues relating to the disclosure of information on insolvency proceedings and the exchange of information between courts and administrators, will be dealt with more efficiently and more quickly. the entry into force of the provisions of the proposal on the mandatory cooperation between courts and insolvency practitioners in main and ancillary proceedings and in the insolvency proceedings of members of groups of undertakings may lead to a longer duration of insolvency proceedings and to an increase in the administrative costs of insolvency proceedings, but is likely to contribute to a better final outcome of insolvency proceedings. it is noted that the provisions of the proposal will improve the economic, business and competitive conditions by enabling more efficient insolvency proceedings involving entities from several member states of the european union.
in writing. ‒ the eu is one of the biggest importers of minerals and metals originating in conflict areas. this means that trade of such minerals cannot be treated as an isolated issue but should be considered in the broader eu foreign and security policy context. taking this fact into account, the eu should establish regulatory mechanisms in order to make sure that trade in such minerals will not result in financing of military groups or indirectly contribute to human rights violations in the countries of extraction. in the absence of such regulation, such trade subsequently undermines eu peacekeeping efforts and results in ineffectiveness of eu aid. therefore, i am convinced that in order for ores and minerals to be sourced responsibly, the supply chain needs to be made more transparent. for this reason, i voted in favour of the ep resolution calling for mandatory compliance on implementing the oecd due diligence guidance on responsible sourcing of gold, tin, tantalum and tungsten originating in conflict—affected and high—risk areas.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims at a more responsible trade in minerals from conflict zones. the eu is one of the largest markets for tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold, with more than 400 importers of these ores and metals. the new regulation establishes an eu system for the authentication of those importers who have chosen to import these metals responsibly into the eu. the verification requires eu importers of these metals to apply the due diligence principle in monitoring and managing their purchases and sales in accordance with the five stages of the oecd due diligence guidance. this is intended to limit the ability of armed groups in conflict zones to finance their activities through the mining and trade of tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold. i agree that it is necessary to require eu smelters and refiners to carry out independent audits to assess whether they are responsible in their purchases of minerals. in order to enhance the social responsibility of smelters and refiners and the transparency of the supply chain and to facilitate the responsible sourcing of minerals, the eu should publish an annual list of eu and global responsible smelters and refiners.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which states that on 5 march 2014 the european commission presented a proposal for a legislative act aimed at restricting the ability of armed groups in conflict-affected and high-risk areas to finance their activities through the extraction and trade of minerals. the main objective of the proposal is to facilitate the responsible sourcing of tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold by businesses and to promote legitimate trade channels. the commission proposes a draft regulation (as well as a response to parliament's resolutions) establishing an eu system of certification for importers of tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold who choose to import these metals responsibly into the union. the regulation allows eu importers to further their current activities aimed at ensuring the cleanliness of supply chains for economic operators engaged in legitimate trade with countries in conflict. in order to increase the social responsibility of smelters and refiners and the transparency of the supply chain and to facilitate the responsible sourcing of minerals, the eu aims to publish an annual list of responsible smelters and refiners in the eu and worldwide.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which sets out the commission's proposals for restricting the ability of armed groups in conflict and high-risk areas to finance their activities through the extraction and trade of minerals. we must do everything possible to break the link between the world's most brutal military conflicts and the trade in minerals. the commission proposed to facilitate the responsible and transparent sourcing of tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold by businesses. this would reduce the possibility of using illegal channels of trade. the commission also proposed a draft regulation establishing an eu system for the certification of importers of those minerals who choose to import those metals into the union in a responsible manner. we need to do more in this area. the commission must ensure that the provisions laid down in the document are implemented. it is also essential that we do not lose sight of the wider range of measures that are preventing bloody conflicts around the world in the legal promotion of legitimate trade.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution which aims to urge the eu to take measures to prevent the spread of xylella fastidiosa, a bacterium that is harmful to olive trees in the region of apulia, italy, and to prevent further damage. xylella fastidiosa is a very dangerous bacterium and poses a very serious direct threat to the production of certain crops in southern europe. bacteria can cause devastating damage with huge economic, ecological and social consequences. the focus has so far been on domestic response to the outbreak and no measures have been put in place to prevent the spread of the disease into the eu from third countries. i support calls on the commission to take targeted measures against xylella fastidiosa to ensure that the infected material does not enter the eu. i support calls for the commission and the member states to compensate farmers for the destruction measures and the lost income, i.e. income not only from agricultural production but also from cultural heritage, history and tourism-related activities.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution because of the outbreak of xylella fastidiosa, a bacterium that is harmful to olive trees. this bacterial plant disease has already destroyed large areas of crops in third countries, such as vineyards in california and citrus groves in brazil, and is widespread in the united states and latin america. there are currently no treatments for diseased plants and affected plants usually remain infected throughout their life cycle or die quickly. a wide range of plants, including wild plants free of signs of the disease, may be infected with this disease in the european union. the commission does not always react quickly enough to the need to prevent plant diseases from entering the eu from third countries, as the import control system is strictly based on a reactive approach which does not provide sufficient protection against harmful organisms such as the bacterium xylella. the european parliament therefore calls on the commission to verify the source of the contamination and to review the eu's official phytosanitary import system in order to protect the eu territory. in addition, the council and the commission should resume discussions on the review of the eu's official phytosanitary control system in order to protect the eu territory.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the outbreak of the olive tree pest xylella fastidiosa, because the consequences of this disease have crossed continental boundaries, there are no treatments for diseased plants, there are no preventive measures to stop the spread of the infection, and the regulation of imports from third countries is a complex and lengthy process. it is therefore necessary to ensure the protection of the eu territory by checking the source of infection as a matter of urgency and to resume interinstitutional work to address this problem.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. the outbreak of the olive tree-damaging bacterium xylella fastidiosa is a major threat to an important european agricultural sector. action at eu level is necessary to prevent the spread of this bacterium, as the scale of the epidemic is very high. in particular, measures should be laid down to prevent the spread of the disease to the eu from third countries. the precautionary approach should be followed in response to this outbreak. in order to protect the eu territory from xylella fastidiosa, the commission should carry out a cost-benefit analysis of the eradication strategy in the short and long term. i think we should have demarcation zones. it is also essential to limit the large-scale use of pesticides, which pose risks to human and animal health and the environment.

on behalf of the alde group.– madam president, the eastern partnership launched five years ago is an example of the european union in real action. despite all the difficulties – and even open attacks – the eastern partnership is something we should be proud of today. the alde group fully supports the eastern partnership policy, as it represents a highly effective stimulus for furthering democratic change and the process of reform in the partner countries in eastern europe. as a result, we have today three associated partners of the eu on the map of europe: georgia, moldova and ukraine. we all know the price they are paying for their european choice: the one of unprecedented military, political and economic pressures and propaganda. we initiated an open letter to the eu heads of state and their governments concerning the declaration of the riga summit. this letter has been signed by 98 members of this house. we believe that the riga summit should act in an ambitious way and in the spirit of solidarity with our associated partners. firstly, we call on the eu leaders in riga to recognise the future membership perspective of georgia, moldova and ukraine. clarity on this, along with the criteria and requirements, will be the right step and is needed today, not tomorrow. secondly, we urge in riga to commit to extending the visa-free regime to the citizens of georgia and ukraine by setting definite deadlines, hopefully by the end of this year, for the completion of their visa liberalisation plans. it is eu policy vis-à-vis russia which has failed, to everybody’s regret, and it is the eastern partnership which proved to bring positive results.
russia today is making it clear that what is happening in ukraine can be repeated in other countries of the eastern neighbourhood. in the face of such economic and security threats, the european union must be even more united and strong in its support for the eastern partnership countries. today we must talk about real support, tangible support that can be mutually beneficial. we need to ensure that the eastern partnership countries are better informed about the work of parliament, the commission and the council and about future legislation. this requires funding for the work of journalists from the eastern partnership countries here in strasbourg and in brussels. we need to promote regional cooperation, and increase support for projects that promote the sharing of experience, skills and knowledge. today we talk a lot about the necessary reforms in the eastern partnership countries, but they must not only be a means of joining the european union, but also an aspiration of the people of georgia, ukraine and moldova themselves, which will help them to secure their own prosperity. i therefore invite everyone to invest in the people of the eastern partnership by sharing the strength of europe's founding ideas.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the common security and defence policy (csdp). the eu's strongest and most important feature is its ability to pool resources and to apply a wide range of diplomatic, security, defence, economic, trade, development and humanitarian instruments in a coherent manner, in accordance with the provisions of the united nations charter. the european parliament considers that the financing of missions and operations under the common security and defence policy is a matter for the future. no concrete proposals have been made yet since the council started to discuss this issue in december 2013. parliament therefore calls for the costs of conducting csdp operations and missions, in particular those carried out with the assistance of eu combat groups, as well as the costs of the infrastructure for the accommodation of forces, the costs of the entry points for the forces into the area of operation and, where appropriate, the costs of food and fuel stocks, to be systematically covered by athena. it is also encouraged to use this mechanism to manage bilateral funding received from member states and funds received from third countries or international organisations in such a way that they can contribute to the financing of a specific operation.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the implementation of the ep resolution on the common security and defence policy (based on the council's annual report to the european parliament on the common foreign and security policy) because i believe that the security environment for the eu and its eastern neighbours is becoming increasingly fragile and volatile, with a large number of old and emerging security problems, and that the conflict in ukraine, the conflicts in syria and iraq with the activation of the terrorist organisation isil, the libyan crisis and the threat of terrorism in africa (especially in the sahel, libya and the somali peninsula) pose a direct threat to the security of the european union. in addition, the union and its member states must adapt as quickly as possible to new security challenges. i also supported proposals to consolidate the eu as a major player in the common defence context with nato. we must take into account the importance of accelerating cooperation with nato in the field of cyber defence.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which discusses the need to reconsider the financing of csdp missions and operations and to make better and more cost-effective use of budgetary appropriations, while ensuring appropriate democratic control of all mission operations, both civilian and military, at the level of the eu institutions. the european parliament welcomes the concrete measures and pragmatic decisions recently proposed by the commission under the applicable financial rules framework to shorten the financial procedures related to csdp civilian missions. however, parliament calls on the commission to address the existing weaknesses in the system, to develop a template for the financial rules specific to civilian csdp missions and to adapt the existing guidelines to their needs in order to facilitate the swift, flexible and more efficient execution of missions, while ensuring sound management of eu finances and adequate protection of the financial interests of the union. it is important to emphasise that transparency and accountability are essential requirements to ensure not only democratic control of eu missions but also their proper functioning and reliability. the european parliament attaches great importance to the control of the budgeting of the various csdp missions and operations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the financing of the common security and defence policy, as the increasingly complex security situation within and outside the union, with new threats and risks that no member state can address alone, requires a strengthening of the common security and defence policy (csdp) and a more effective policy instrument to ensure that it is a genuine guarantee for the security of eu citizens and the promotion of european interests and values. the european union therefore needs to improve the protection of its external borders, rethink the financing of csdp missions and operations and make better and more cost-effective use of budgetary appropriations, while ensuring appropriate democratic control of all mission operations, both civilian and military, at the level of the eu institutions and ensuring transparency and accountability of funding. at the next european council on defence, concrete measures must be adopted to help build up the eu's defence capabilities and complement nato's forces, to support and consolidate the european defence agency and to strengthen the common industrial and technological base.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which deals with security and defence capabilities in europe. parliament expressed its deep concern at the escalation of armed conflict in the eu's immediate neighbourhood, low-intensity crises, hybrid and proxy warfare, state failure, instability and widespread human rights abuses, as well as the threat of terrorism within the eu. the security environment is facing increasingly complex and challenging challenges, and the european defence sector is threatened with becoming dependent on external factors. it is necessary to address complex security and defence issues such as the uncoordinated defence budgets of the member states, the continued fragmentation of the market despite new market rules, the increasing dependence of the defence industry on exports outside the eu and the growing foreign investment in the european defence sector in some countries. it is also necessary to take into account the fact that the eu has recently been facing increasing cyber threats and challenges, which pose a serious threat to the security of individual member states and the eu as a whole. such threats should be properly assessed and action taken at eu level to provide for technical and other security measures in the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the impact of developments in european defence markets on security and defence capabilities in europe, as the security of the european union and its neighbours is of paramount importance in terms of the provision of adequate capabilities and equipment. moreover, the success of peacekeeping and security missions under the csdp is highly dependent on the ability to react quickly and immediately, and the main objective is therefore to create a real european defence market, avoiding duplication and reducing bureaucratic obstacles.
in writing. ‒ the the current security threats are of concern to the eu as a whole and should be addressed in a unified and coordinated manner. however, it is essential that the principles of proportionality and subsidiarity are respected in addressing these highly complex issues. the sovereign rights of the member states shall not be infringed or restricted. in order to ensure security and stability in europe and in neighbouring countries, particular attention should be paid to certain projects relating to the autonomy and independence of the eu. the consolidation of the defence industry must be a level playing field for all parties. the european defence equipment market cannot be created in a way that undermines the legitimate expectations of the member states. full transparency must be ensured and duplication of effort avoided. priority should be given to cooperation and pooling and sharing initiatives. it is essential to ensure efficient use of resources. particular attention and support should be given to promising small and medium-sized enterprises and innovation centres in order to facilitate their entry into european and international markets.

in writing.– living in the digital era entails not only information sharing at increased speed but also more favourable conditions for cyber—hackers to find various security shortcomings. therefore, taking into account the increasing incidence of cyber-attacks against western media agencies in recent years – including attacks carried out by isis and by the syrian regime, and a number of undisclosed attacks – efforts to step up cybersecurity are needed. cyber-attacks pose an imminent threat and can take many forms: interrupted news flows, the distortion of media information for terrorist purposes, the leaking of sensitive personal data such as the identities of whistle-blowers, etcetera. such attacks are extremely dangerous, especially at times when critical coverage of events is required. they are an aspect of information warfare, with the aim of distorting facts and fuelling an unwanted response to the originally intended media communication; and, in turn, they endanger the security of states and their citizens. i believe that a new cybersecurity directive is extremely timely. we need to make sure that, at least, a minimum level of security is guaranteed in sectors of critical importance, such as media, health, banks and transport, and to ensure that these sectors step up their security cooperation with the european agencies.
in writing. cybersecurity is becoming an increasingly important issue in europe. attacks occur daily, affecting all countries of the european union, without limiting geographical borders. the internet is an open platform and a tool for various terrorist groups and radical groups to pursue their destructive goals. the baltic states are concerned by the russian cyber-propaganda and cyber-attacks against public opinion platforms, public institutions and the media. the increase in hacking shows that anti-eu forces and special services of hostile countries have mastered the ways of exploiting digital space as one of the most powerful tools for threats and terrorism. cyberterrorism must be seen as a threat to the security of the eu as a whole and must be addressed as a matter of urgency.

the milk sector has been and still is one of the core agricultural sectors in lithuania, but an analysis of the situation of the milk market over the last two decades shows that cooperation in this agricultural sector in lithuania is not strong enough and does not support competition from raw milk imported from the european union countries. even cooperating farmers are unable to build up enough bargaining power to negotiate fair prices for their milk. one reason is the oligopoly of milk buyers and traders, who are subject only to regulation, but such regulation is limited by the common organisation of the milk market in the european union. given the current situation, it is simply necessary to give the member states the possibility of regulating the raw milk market more or to take responsibility for regulatory measures at european union level. the lithuanian government has proposed a law that significantly increases the regulation of the milk market, but its adoption is blocked by opponents of regulation under the guise of european union law.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this decision proposing better synergy between the school fruit scheme and the school milk scheme. better coordination of the schemes and a unified political approach will increase their efficiency and will bring more positive results. promoting the consumption of fruit, vegetables and milk at european educational establishments will not only provide the nutrients and vitamins that children need but will also help to shape healthier eating patterns, starting at a young age, and to fight the rising incidence of obesity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to improve the supply of fruit, vegetables and milk to schools. the school milk scheme has been in operation since 1977 and the corresponding fruit and vegetable scheme since 2009. however, the consumption of fruit, vegetables and milk is declining in europe. 22 million children are overweight, and adolescents on average consume only 30 to 50% of the recommended daily intake of fruit and vegetables. the new rules aim to bring together eu programmes to promote the use of these products in schools. eu member states are encouraged to allocate 10 to 20% of the combined fruit, vegetables and milk scheme to education, for example by organising farm visits or supplying local products such as honey, dried fruit. in addition, it is proposed to increase by eur 20 million the financing of the milk supply part of the programme, which should reach eur 100 million per year.
in writing. ‒ i supported the creation of this scheme. in fact, this is a consolidation of two already existing schemes – the school milk scheme and the school fruit scheme. it should be noted that the milk and fruit sectors combined represent nearly 30% by value of eu agricultural output. obviously, however, the goal of this scheme is not a financial but a health one. modern nutrition trends among children show an increasing switch towards unhealthy processed foods, and this scheme is designed to tackle the associated problems. the priorities should be buying fruit, vegetables and milk from local, environment-friendly farmers, and having regional authorities decide who is the best provider for the schools they administer.

rapporteur.– mr president, first of all let me thank all the shadow rapporteurs – ms jaakonsaari, mr van baalen, ms fotyga, mr meszerics and mr šoltes – for all their work, and for the proposals that were made and amendments that were tabled during the process of preparing this report. i would also like to thank all those colleagues – meps and parliament staff – for their very valuable input into this very sensitive and important matter that we are here to discuss: eu-russia relations. i would like to note that while preparing the report i was planning on going and taking the opportunity to hear what the officials in moscow had to say. unfortunately, my fact-finding mission did not take place, since my delegation was not let into russia. we can only regret that now, 19 of our colleagues find themselves on the illegal russian visa ban list. this is not only disrespect to the european parliament but an insult to the eu as a whole, which bases international cooperation on transparent and peaceful dialogue. when preparing for this speech i looked for inspiration from churchill’s fulton speech. the prime minister of the united kingdom saw the dramatic geopolitical changes that were arriving in his wake when he said these words: ‘if the western democracies stand together in strict adherence to the principles [of the united nations charter, their influence] will be immense and no one is likely to molest them. if however they become divided or falter in their duty and if these all-important years are allowed to slip away, then indeed catastrophe may overwhelm us all’. when everyone in europe was tired after the war, it took great courage to name the situation, as it was – if not acted upon – possibly as dangerous as the situation created by the nazis. there are countries and people who would say the same thing about today’s situation. europe’s post-war peace order is challenged by the occupation of crimea and continuing russian military aggression in ukraine. there should be no fear in naming it that way. but the european continent had not only the cold war: it also had the fall of the berlin wall and the singing revolution, which was one of the reasons that made my speech here today possible. it all happened in a semi-peaceful way. it seemed that history has indeed come to an end: democracy and the rule of law are prevailing over aggression and unlawfulness and war. further eu enlargement is an excellent example of peaceful european order. so one could say that there is a solution, there is a possibility of building a peaceful cohabitation with all the countries on the continent. but at this moment it is not europe which will decide it. the european union adheres to the very clear principles of the rule of law, transparency and self-determination, therefore numerous different formats and initiatives were offered to russia in order to usher the russian people to the path of democracy and reform. the european union was even generous in offering strategic partnership or ‘common spaces’ initiatives, but the respect of human rights and democratic principles kept on deteriorating in russia. europe even turned a blind eye when people in the kremlin were breaking the established order of international treaties. europe did not do much when the russian troops entered georgia’s territory and remained silent during the establishment of the gazprom monopoly in certain countries and during trade wars when russia would close down its borders under political pretexts. but europe is not there any longer. after the illegal annexation of crimea, after the mh17 plane was shot down from the sky, europe took churchill’s advice and spoke out, and it will speak again, i am sure. there will be more and tougher sanctions if the international obligations set out in two minsk agreements are not respected and if more people die because the guns keep flowing through the unprotected border. europe will speak out when the rules of the internal market are challenged by uncompromising monopoly companies which long thought that corrupt deals would keep them above the law. europe will say a word or two when the political parties that disagree with the very principles of european union, like democracy, receive funding from financial institutions linked to the people running the kremlin. (the president cut off the speaker)
mr president, whether we like it or not – and i must stress i certainly do not – we are already back in the times of the cold war. now it is a hybrid cold war. contrary to what he says publicly, this was mr putin’s deliberate policy aim, and he fully achieved it. it is not about getting back ukraine, it is about putin staying in power. it is about the re—sovietisation of russia. the old bolshevik methods are being well tested, through external aggression and foreign enemies, internal suppression and isolation of russian society from the west. we, the democratic world, have learned our lessons from the cold war – though i do have some doubts after listening to our debates today – which are the following: a united and solid eu, a strong transatlantic partnership and full solidarity with those who cherish common values. it is also about us being able to deal with political bribery, such as in the shameful case of madame le pen’s party. in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it sets out parliament's position on the regulation fixing the adjustment coefficient for direct payments for the calendar year 2015. the parliament's notification accepts the commission's proposal with minor amendments. the eu treaties lay down the basic rule for union funding the annual budget of the union must comply with the multiannual financial framework (mff). in order to support the agricultural sector in the event of major crises affecting the production or distribution of agricultural products, a financial discipline mechanism established by the previous regulation provides for the creation of an agricultural crisis reserve by means of a minor adjustment of direct payments at the beginning of each year. parliament has given its consent to this in the present report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council fixing the adjustment coefficient for direct payments for the calendar year 2015 provided for in the regulation. in this report, parliament gave its approval to the de minimis direct payments, which are adjusted at the beginning of each year to create a reserve for crises in the agricultural sector. this is an important step towards reducing the major crises in the agricultural sector, which have a devastating impact on production and consumers.
in writing. eu direct support is essential to develop agriculture and to maintain and increase its competitiveness. it should be noted that direct payments are one of the most important instruments of agricultural policy. it is therefore essential to ensure a level playing field for all farmers and to help them to successfully absorb eu support. it should be noted that direct payments ensure a sufficient level of income and thus provide an incentive to expand agricultural activities, to compete on the market, rather than to withdraw from agricultural production. the budgetary balance requires that direct payments be used in a targeted and efficient manner. the competitiveness of farmers and the stability of their incomes must be enhanced.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a strategy for promoting gender equality, which aims at clearer objectives and better monitoring of the strategy. i agree that the new strategy for promoting gender equality should be clearer in order to tackle discrimination in the labour market, education and decision-making. it is also important to strengthen the mechanism for monitoring its implementation. the european parliament is to vote on the draft resolution on monday and decide whether to approve it the following day.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because we still face problems and challenges in europe in the field of gender equality. we still have an unresolved problem of the wage gap, and this affects the lives of both working and older women, because women, on lower wages, receive lower pensions and are more likely to be poor in old age. these problems must also be addressed in terms of non-discrimination in the labour market, adequate and secure social guarantees and reconciliation between family and professional life. the fight against all forms of violence against women and girls should be a priority on the gender equality agenda, and we therefore call on the commission once again to initiate a european legislative act on combating and preventing violence against women. in addition, women are still significantly underrepresented in political, public and economic decision-making, and discrimination still occurs in business, business and politics. the report therefore calls on the commission and the member states to raise awareness of women's training opportunities in these areas and to ensure that women have the same opportunities as men to obtain appropriate jobs and pursue careers.
