in writing. i do not support the distortion of the traditional family concept. i'm just for traditional marriage between a man and a woman. a family is the union of one man and one woman. i therefore oppose any further consideration of options or the extension of the concept of family. family policy is a matter for each member state. the family, where children are born of the union of a man and a woman, is one of the cornerstones of that state, and by rejecting the concept of the family or by narrowing it down to same-sex marriage, we are destroying that foundation. it is necessary to support and encourage the efforts of the member states to preserve traditional values. the rights of sexual minorities cannot be defended blindly without mentioning or ignoring the interests and rights of other people. sexual orientation cannot and should not be a reason for exclusive rights. it is necessary to ensure equal opportunities and equal treatment for men and women. it is therefore essential that women and men should have equal opportunities to exercise their freedom of choice in deciding how they want to pursue their careers and balance work and family life.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to review the strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries. in the eu, intellectual property-based industries account for about 39% of all economic activities and around 26% of all jobs. nevertheless, since the entry into force of the trips agreement (1 january 1995), only a small number of important ipr agreements have been concluded, although the nature of ipr has changed substantially as a result of technological and societal changes. the communication properly identifies the need to promote research and innovation, the difficulties in accessing medicines and environmental change as important issues of the present and the future. any external policy initiative has implications for internal policies, and it is therefore important that the eu improves its internal intellectual property rules.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution because it is a statement by parliament on the strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries. the eu's competitiveness is increasingly and will continue to depend on creativity and innovation. intellectual property rights help to foster innovation and creativity, and their protection is essential to european competitiveness, and the union needs to develop a broader strategy to protect its intellectual property rights in working with third countries' trading partners. in this resolution, parliament welcomed the commission's efforts to strike a balance between the different interests. the parliament criticised, however, the lack of clarity in the 2014 communication from the commission on the means and methods to be used to achieve the objectives set out in the communication, in particular the resources to be allocated and the sources of those resources, in particular in the light of the limited resources currently available to support european rightholders exporting their production to or seeking to establish their activities in third country markets.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on a strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries, because, although technological and societal changes have also led to changes in intellectual property rights, their protection is an essential challenge to european competitiveness in dealing with third countries. intellectual property rights help to stimulate innovation and creativity, thus promoting competitiveness and the european union moving forward.
in writing. i believe that the commission's proposal to revise the strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries is a step towards a more ambitious strategy. it is necessary to ensure that intellectual property rights are properly protected not only in the eu but also beyond. given the nature and scale of the potential infringements, the strategy should be better adapted to the digital environment and include strong cooperation with customs and market surveillance authorities and ensure horizontal consistency. it should be noted that intellectual property is a legal and economic incentive mechanism. in addition, intellectual property rights act as a mechanism to attract investment by demonstrating innovation potential. in this context, clear measures and methods should be established to help achieve the objectives pursued. sufficient financial support should be granted to european right holders exporting their production to or seeking to establish themselves on third country markets.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution because it is a parliament's call for an eu action plan to renegotiate the protection of intellectual property rights. the resolution notes that the eu is faced with a high incidence of infringements of intellectual property rights and that the scale and cost of these infringements are of concern and that the commission is reporting on this in its report on the application of the directive on the enforcement of intellectual property rights. these figures also show the importance of intellectual property rights to the european economy in global competition due to infringements of intellectual property rights, including counterfeiting, stunted growth, job creation, innovation and creativity, moral and economic damage to european companies and substantial economic and financial losses to governments. parliament therefore stressed that, in order to ensure innovation, creativity and competitiveness, it was essential that the measures for the protection of intellectual property rights were transparent and that the public and all other interested parties had access to all the information. in the resolution, parliament also called attention to the fact that during the financial crisis, when financial support for the cultural sector was severely curtailed, intellectual property rights were often a major source of income for creators. it therefore stressed that ensuring fair compensation for developers should be one of the key aspects of the eu action plan.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the eu action plan for a renegotiation of the protection of intellectual property rights. the countries of the european union face a high number of intellectual property infringements each year, as well as suffering significant financial and economic losses at both the state and business levels. in order to ensure competitiveness and innovation in business, the european union must combat and ensure the protection of intellectual property rights.
in writing. in particular, the eu action plan must ensure effective and evidence-based enforcement of intellectual property rights. it would also help to promote innovation, creativity, competitiveness, economic growth and cultural diversity. i believe that ensuring fair remuneration for creators should be one of the key aspects of the eu action plan. it is also essential to give legal protection to new works as soon as possible in order to stimulate investment and create more innovation. as the use of the internet continues to grow, illicit products are being distributed around the world in an instant. this creates difficulties in identifying and combating infringers of intellectual property rights, as infringements become more international, complex and diverse. it is therefore essential to develop a comprehensive strategy for intellectual property rights at eu level. this strategy should establish a comprehensive legal framework to combat it infringements, adapted to the online environment, in full respect of fundamental rights and freedoms and the principles of fair trial, proportionality and data protection.

communication, cooperation and a united voice with third countries, europe will not be able to achieve a coherent energy policy and energy security. we must ensure that solidarity between member states in the event of disruption of external energy supplies is not just words but concrete actions. i believe that we need to pay particular attention to the coordinated diversification of suppliers, routes and energy sources and to the increase and promotion of local energy production. we have and can use local energy resources, and this includes fossil fuels, renewable energy and basis for ensuring energy security and solidarity between member states. we must pay sufficient attention to the development of connections and their optimal use. it should be borne in mind that need to achieve or how many buildings we need to renovate, but to set out the main guidelines on which to base our security in both the long and short term. other energy-related issues should not be on behalf of the ppe group.– mr president, the situation in the black sea basin has fundamentally changed due to russian aggression against ukraine and the annexation of crimea by russia. the military balance has significantly shifted towards entrenchment of russian military dominance in the black sea. there is a country in the region, a neighbour of the eu, which used to benefit from cooperation with european democracies but which, for many years, has been steadily preparing itself for military endeavours instead. we used to close our eyes to this tendency. experts estimate that since 2009, putin has increased defence spending in roubles more than 20 times over. we all know the economic and social challenges russia now faces, but this does not stop putin spending up to 34% of the national budget on defence and security. too many european nato member states do not manage even 2%. there are new realities for the countries of the region, and they are not the reflection of a greater peace. russia is testing the boundaries of our security. it is up to the eu and nato to make it clear to russia that in the current world you cannot send tanks or amass military forces whenever you think things are not going your way. you cannot bully your neighbours or tear independent states apart. the annexation of crimea will never be recognised, and the minsk agreement must be implemented. the eu must stay firm on this principle because, if the trend is not stopped in ukraine, the limits of our security will be tested further. the military balance in the black sea region may be restored by strengthening our transatlantic link and by a bigger nato presence and increased cooperation under the common security and defence policy (csdp) but, in addition, we should help threatened countries to take more responsibility for security in their region. countries that have the most direct security concerns, due to the changed realities, could combine their efforts by creating a joint military battalion for military exercises, increasing interoperability and furthering modernisation. the issue of the occupation and annexation of crimea should not be abandoned. there are legal ways to challenge it, including by requesting a legal opinion from the international court of justice. it is important to make clear to those responsible for violations of international law and human rights that a crime does not go unpunished. in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, in which the consultative working party of the european parliament, the council and the commission concluded by consensus that the present proposal for a regulation laying down community procedures in the field of the common commercial policy seeks only to codify existing texts without changing their substance. this regulation lays down the procedures of the european union in the field of the common commercial policy to ensure the exercise of international trade rules, in particular the rights conferred on the european union by the world trade organisation (wto), which are designed, in compliance with existing national obligations and procedures, to take action against barriers to trade affecting the european union market in order to eliminate the damage caused by them. it also provides for measures to be taken against barriers to trade affecting the market of a third country in order to eliminate the negative effects on trade which they cause.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, in which the consultative working party of the european parliament, the council and the commission has unanimously concluded that the present proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the protection of ships against injurious pricing is intended only to codify the existing texts without changing their substance. this regulation is important because it is desirable to provide clear and detailed guidance on the factors that may be relevant in determining whether an injurious sale has caused material injury or threatens to do so. in order to demonstrate that injury has been caused to the union industry by a particular level of sales price, it is necessary to take into account the impact of other factors, in particular the prevailing conditions on the eu market. it is also necessary to define the procedural and substantive conditions for lodging a complaint concerning an injurious pricing, the extent to which such a complaint should be supported by the eu industry and the information on the buyer of the vessel, the injurious pricing, the damage caused and the reasons for it that should be included in such a complaint. it is also necessary to lay down the procedure whereby the information requested by public authorities should be communicated to interested parties. interested parties should be given ample opportunity to present all the necessary evidence and to defend their interests.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation on the granting of fishing opportunities to fishing vessels flying the flag of the bolivarian republic of venezuela in the exclusive economic zone off the coast of french guiana in eu waters. the processing industry in french guiana is partly dependent on the exploitation by venezuelan fishing vessels of the living natural resources in the exclusive economic zone off the coast of french guiana. as this activity is of economic and social importance in the region, venezuelan fishing vessels are authorised to fish in this area for many decades, but part of the catch must be landed in french guiana ports. the landing and processing of fishery products is thus an important source of income and employment in french guiana. in the absence of an international fisheries agreement between the eu and venezuela, the cooperation between the two countries is not subject to the requirements of the union legal order. however, in practice, venezuelan fishing vessels are allowed to operate. in this context, the commission has submitted a proposal in which the european union has committed to transfer fishing rights to venezuelan vessels. the legal solution found, i.e. a council declaration submitted to the european parliament for approval, stating that the legally binding european union acts on the conservation and management of fisheries resources (common fisheries policy and other rules) are being complied with, is an appropriate solution given the small scale of this fishing activity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution of fishing opportunities in eu waters for fishing vessels flying the flag of venezuela off the coast of french guiana. in my opinion, the council continues to act reluctantly to accept the european parliament’s competences in the field of fisheries under the lisbon treaty. nevertheless, the european court of justice supported the european commission and the parliament’s claims. the report is to be considered as a crucial step to end the long-standing competence conflict existing between the two co-legislators and to unblock the ‘frozen’ negotiation process where no fisheries management plan has been able to be adopted during the last 5 years.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the development of the fruit and vegetables sector and the 2007 reform. the implementation of the common agricultural policy (cap) over the past 20 years has led to a reduction in the regulation of agricultural markets, allowing production to be directed by market forces. this general approach was particularly applicable to the arrangements in the fruit and vegetables sector, which waived the application of measures such as export refunds or minimum prices to be paid by processors to farmers for certain products. the european union has linked this process of liberalisation to a policy of strengthening producer organisations (po) to enable farmers to take action to defend their interests, for example by selling their production collectively or increasing the value of this production by processing it on the farm. the cap thus provides financial support to the octs, which they use to implement their operational programmes. the go uses such programmes to pursue various objectives consistent with their specific situation, such as investing in marketing campaigns or training activities. in march 2014, the commission published a report on the implementation of the new rules of procedure in the fruit and vegetables sector, introduced following the 2007 reform. this report provides a coherent overview of the situation in the fruit and vegetables sector, identifies areas of progress and highlights certain ongoing problems.

in writing. the reform of greenhouse gas emission allowances is one of the most important issues in climate change policy today. i believe that the european commission's proposed solution to create a market stability reserve will help to solve the current problems of the emissions trading system - i.e. to reduce the surplus of emissions allowances created by the economic crisis on the market, to regulate their price, to encourage industrial companies to invest in modern, environmentally friendly technological solutions that reduce greenhouse gas emissions. in view of the issues and concerns raised by the member states, the council, the european parliament, industry, environmental organisations, it can be said that the agreement reached should strike a balance between high european environmental standards and industrial interests. while this proposal addresses the problem of excess allowances to be auctioned, it does not address issues related to the allocation of free allowances or the provisions governing carbon leakage. an effective reform of emissions trading should ensure that energy-sensitive industries do not move their production capacity to third countries outside the european union that do not have such high environmental standards. it is therefore essential that the commission submits its proposals for measures to mitigate the risk of carbon leakage as soon as possible. i hope that these measures will help to maintain a balance between the european union's ambitious environmental objectives and industrial activity without reducing competitiveness.

on behalf of the alde group.– mr president, first of all i would like to congratulate our colleague, eduard kukan, on his report and thank him for his work. i really enjoyed working as co-shadow from the alde group. as a result, we now have serious input from parliament into the review process to be finalised by the commission and the external action service. the european union’s neighbourhood today is more complex, challenging and fragmented than ever. it would not be fair to blame the neighbourhood policy for all this. the european neighbourhood policy (enp) was the right and timely response after the eu enlargement and accomplished a lot, in eastern europe in particular. equally, we need a right and solid response at this stage. with all the positive things that i have to say regarding our joint work on the report, i must say, however, that i had wished for a more clear conceptual split into two dimensions of the european neighbourhood policy – the eastern partnership and the southern neighbourhood. i remain convinced that these two dimensions should be separated and allowed to develop in their own distinct direction and with no rivalry whatsoever. this split is dictated by reality on the ground and the processes that take place. nevertheless, when it comes to the main principles of our new neighbourhood policy and our report, i believe that the enp has to be ambitious, proactive and policy-driven in the first place. anything else would be seen as the eu’s withdrawal, and this area would be used as a playing field for third countries, the neighbours of our neighbours right on our doorstep – the doorstep where our security, as well as insecurity, is placed. as we all agree, the differentiation principle is becoming key in the enp. for countries in conflict, the eu should focus on conflict resolution, humanitarian work, migration and refugee challenges. the second group of our neighbours is those which currently have less interest in closer relations or in making long-term reforms. here i believe the eu should place greater emphasis on better governance and building sustainable, democratic and stable countries. the third group of our partners are those seeking an advanced level of engagement with the eu. these are georgia, moldova and ukraine, our associated members. it is clear that they are far from ready for membership today and that they need to focus very seriously on implementation of the association agreements. we cannot deny their membership perspective in the long term. the association agreements are clearly not the final step in relations between the eu and these advanced neighbours. this is certainly in the eu’s interest.
the european neighbourhood policy was created with the objective, set out in 2002, of creating an area of security and stability around the european union. the report notes that we spend very little on neighbourhood policy compared to what is spent in third countries. have we already established an area of security, stability and good governance around the european union? the revised neighbourhood policy must offer a wide range of cooperation opportunities to all neighbours. this must include financial support, access to the european union's research and industrial achievements, and openness to human contacts. well, most importantly, of course, visa facilitation, especially for young people, artists, scientists. i propose to speed up the visa-free regime for the people of ukraine and georgia. of course, the openness of the european union must depend on political conditionality. the more democratic, free and market-oriented a neighbouring country is, the more opportunities we must open to it. but above all, let us remember that the neighbourhood policy is for our neighbours. there's a saying that a good neighbor is more important than family. so neighbourhood policy must be properly funded, otherwise we risk continuing to be left wondering how to resolve conflicts in neighbouring countries or where to put the growing flows of refugees.

in writing. ‒ i very much welcome and strongly support this report on tax avoidance and tax evasion as challenges in developing countries. it is not only very timely due to the fact that this year is the european year for development, but also since the european union is the world’s largest donor in the development policy it is of our greatest interest to make sure that development policy works well and our investment bears fruits. the figures of an annual illicit capital flight from developing countries of an estimated usd 1 trillion and a loss of an estimated usd 189 billion in tax revenue annually (as noted in the report), are very worrying and explains why many developing countries cannot attain even the minimum tax level necessary to finance their basic functioning, public services, poverty eradication and sustainable development. there is no doubt that europe must not only remain the leader in providing development assistance to the developing countries but at the same time make sure that the aid is absorbed to its fullest potential by addressing tax evasion, tax fraud and combating tax havens.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report. domestic resources are and will remain the main source of financing for developing countries. despite their increasing share of gdp over the past decade, the average tax-to-gdp ratio in developing countries is still too low: developing countries collect comparatively much less income than advanced economies. the tax-to-gdp ratio in low-income countries ranges from 10% to 20%, and in many such countries it is below 15% (this is generally considered to be the threshold below which governments have difficulty financing their basic functions and services). in the oecd countries, it is between 30% and 40%. experts agree that there is ample scope for increasing tax revenues: oxfam's calculations in 52 developing countries show that significantly improved tax collection could raise an additional $269 billion to fund public services. it is therefore essential to ensure that national tax collection is made more predictable, stable and reliable and that all groups of society - individuals and companies - pay according to their means.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report on tax evasion and avoidance. illicit financial flows, i.e. all unregistered, private financial flows related to illicitly obtained, transferred or used capital, are generally associated with tax evasion and tax fraud activities, such as the misuse of transaction pricing, in breach of the principle that taxes should be paid when profits are made. illegal flows are just one way in which developing countries lose income tax revenue. illegal tax avoidance, where companies seek to avoid taxation by using complex internal structures and finding loopholes in tax laws, is another important problem. corporate tax rates are falling all over the world. this is particularly the case in developing countries, which are heavily dependent on income tax, which accounts for a large proportion of their national income. the european parliament proposes to increase financial and technical assistance to developing countries and regional tax administration systems in order to combat tax evasion and avoidance. it also considers that reasonable solutions should be adopted to increase transparency and strengthen cooperation in the fight against tax evasion, such as the automatic exchange of information mechanism and country-by-country reporting, taking into account the needs and constraints of developing countries. to assess the impact of tax policies on developing countries at eu and member state level.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report. the inefficient use of resources causes environmental damage and economic risks. the amount of resources used by the global economy in global production and waste absorption is equivalent to 1.5 times the planet's resources. by 2030, this number is expected to reach the resources of two planets. annual consumption of minerals, fossil fuels and biomass is projected to double to 140 million tonnes by 2050. this is due to population growth, access to higher incomes, a greater variety of products than before and a shorter product life cycle. to avoid these changes in our biosphere, we need to use fewer resources. we can and must achieve at least the same standard of living and well-being as we do today, using one tenth of the resources we currently use. only by decoupling growth from resource use can we increase our competitiveness, complete europe's reindustrialisation and improve our living standards. better resource efficiency would benefit our economy and security. more efficient use of resources would reduce resource dependency and save on raw material costs. in addition, new business activities and jobs would be created in europe. the european commission estimates that an annual increase in resource efficiency of 2% would create 2 million new jobs in the eu by 2030.

in writing. - i voted for this resolution. in its resolution of 26 february 2014 on the long-term financing of the european economy, parliament stressed the need to improve access to capital markets through new sources of financing, and noted that commercial banks are likely to remain one of the main sources of financing and that it is essential for member states to develop new sources of financing that complement established mechanisms and close the financing gap, while providing for a regulatory and supervisory framework that is adequately adapted to the needs of the real economy. the capital markets union should be gradual and should have a triple priority: first, to promote the most efficient distribution of savings by deepening and diversifying the sources of finance available to businesses and to offer savings holders and investors greater investment choice, greater transparency and portfolio diversification. second, to contribute to enhanced risk mitigation by building stronger cross-border markets, by strengthening the resilience of financial systems to the adverse impact of major financial crises and by mitigating the impact of particularly severe shocks; third, to ensure that an effective additional source of financing for the real economy is found.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because the lack of adequate regulation and control of capital markets was a major cause of the financial crisis. following the financial crisis, the european union institutions adopted a number of legislative measures aimed at preventing future crises and creating an environment of financial stability, which is a prerequisite for sustainable growth. the european parliament notes that, despite the opportunities offered by a well-functioning eu capital market, it is impossible to ignore the existence of major obstacles in other areas such as taxation, in particular the practice of promoting debt-to-equity ratios, insolvency and accounting rules. the future of europe depends on its capacity to innovate. the creation of an innovation-friendly regulatory framework is a prerequisite for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, as is easy, appropriate and diversified access to finance for businesses. the european parliament therefore calls on the commission to examine in depth the current situation of capital markets in each member state, to provide an assessment in a detailed economic study of where and to what extent barriers to investment through capital markets exist at eu level, and to indicate what measures, including non-legislative procedures and market-based strategies, could be taken to remove or reduce these barriers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the creation of a capital markets union because i believe that access to capital markets needs to be improved through new sources of finance. parliament stressed that commercial banks were likely to remain one of the main sources of financing and that it was essential for member states to develop new sources of financing to complement the existing mechanisms and to close the financing gap. this report is one of a series of actions to help diversify funding, develop european capital markets and improve access to finance. all of this is crucial for economic growth, job creation and entrepreneurship in the union.
in writing. ‒ the i voted for this resolution. threats to the internal security of the union have become more complex, hybrid, asymmetrical, unconventional, transnational, fast-moving and difficult to predict and exceed the capabilities of any single member state, and therefore require a coherent, comprehensive, multilateral and coordinated eu response, taking full account of respect for fundamental rights, more than ever. the development of the eu's security policy is a matter of common responsibility, requiring concerted and unified efforts by all member states, eu institutions and agencies, civil society and law enforcement authorities to pursue common objectives and based on the rule of law and respect for fundamental rights. whereas, in order to achieve the best results, the concrete implementation of these common objectives and priorities should be linked to a clear allocation of tasks at eu and national level, based on the principle of subsidiarity and subject to strict and effective parliamentary and judicial oversight. i support the european security strategy 2015-2020 proposed by the commission and the priorities set out therein.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because we need freedom, security and justice, respect for fundamental rights, and appropriate democratic oversight and accountability to ensure that these rights are implemented, both at the level of the european union and the member states. the european parliament welcomes the european security strategy 2015-2020 proposed by the commission and the priorities it sets, but this agenda does not sufficiently address the justice aspect. the european agenda on security is of particular importance as the european union is currently facing threats such as terrorism, radicalisation, cross-border organised crime and cybercrime, which require coordinated action at national, eu and global levels to address. the action plan for this agenda therefore requires a proper balance between prevention policies and repressive measures to preserve freedom, security and justice. security measures should always be applied in accordance with the rule of law and with respect for fundamental rights, such as the right to privacy and data protection, freedom of expression and association and the right to due process. the commission should therefore, in implementing the european agenda on security, take due account of the recent ruling of the court of justice on the data retention directive, which requires that all measures comply with the principles of proportionality, necessity and legality and include appropriate accountability and redress safeguards.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european agenda on security. i believe that the threats to the internal security of the union have become more complex, hybrid, asymmetrical, unconventional, transnational, fast-moving and difficult to predict and beyond the capabilities of any single member state, and that a coherent, comprehensive, multilateral and coordinated eu response, taking full account of respect for fundamental rights, is therefore more necessary than ever. the development of eu security policy is a matter of common responsibility and therefore requires common objectives and priorities. their implementation should be linked to a clear division of tasks between the eu and national levels, based on the principle of subsidiarity and with strict and effective parliamentary and judicial oversight. only by working together and in unity can we ensure the future security of the union, and that is what this report seeks to do.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. the current crisis in yemen is one consequence of the failure of successive governments to meet the legitimate expectations of the yemeni people regarding democracy, economic and social development, stability and security. whereas the current conflict in yemen has spread to 20 of the 22 territorial units of the country; whereas, according to the latest consolidated figures of the world health organisation (who), at least 1 439 people were killed and 5 951 injured, many of them civilians, between 19 march and 5 may 2015; whereas more than 3 000 people have been killed and more than 10 000 injured since the beginning of the conflicts; the eu reaffirmed its commitment to continue supporting yemen and the yemeni people. the european parliament strongly supports the unity, sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of yemen and stands by the people of yemen and expresses its full support for the efforts of the un and the un secretary-general's special envoy for yemen, ismail ould cheikho ahmed, to mediate peace negotiations between the parties. the resolution calls on all parties to the conflict in yemen to seek a political, inclusive and negotiated solution to the conflict through dialogue, compromise and power-sharing, and the formation of a national unity government to restore peace, prevent economic and financial collapse and address the humanitarian crisis.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution on the current crisis in yemen. this crisis is the result of the failure of successive governments to meet the legitimate expectations of the yemeni people for democracy, economic and social development, stability and security. this failure has led to violent conflicts at the source, the failure to form a proper government and to share power fairly, and the systematic ignoring of the country's tribal divisions, insecurity and economic paralysis. these recent developments pose a serious threat to the stability of the region, in particular the somali peninsula, the red sea and the wider middle east. parliament expressed its deep concern at the rapidly deteriorating political, security and humanitarian situation in yemen, expressed its condolences to the families of the victims and called on all parties to the conflict to put an end to the violence without delay. the european union supports the unity, sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of yemen and supports the people of yemen. parliament also condemned the destabilising and violent unilateral actions by the criminal group and military units loyal to the former president. it also condemns the airstrikes by the saudi-led coalition and the naval blockade of yemen, which have killed thousands of people.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the situation in yemen because i am concerned about the rapidly deteriorating political, security and humanitarian situation in yemen. i am not in favour of war and i support the rapporteur's call for all warring parties to immediately cease violence and to express sympathy to the families of the victims. i believe that the european union must fulfil its commitment to continue to support yemen and the yemeni people, the unity, sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of yemen. it is important to ensure peace in the world and to use the influence of the european union in doing so.
in writing. ‒ we are witnessing a dire security situation in the mena region characterized by ongoing insecurity, rising extremism (with these countries, isil) and new waves of internal displacement. in my opinion, this resolution rightly states that political and economic stability of the region is of a crucial strategic importance to eu security. a holistic, ambitious and cooperative eu approach towards mena countries is needed. we should remind ourselves that those countries share a common security interest with the eu in such fields as halting the spread of extremism, addressing migration and helping people who have been displaced. with democratic hopefulness in decline, economic cooperation needs to be complemented by a large-scale political and strategic partnership. the eu needs to promote conflict resolution along with gradual public and private sector reforms and civil capacity-building projects. while the emergency situation on an unprecedented scale is likely to continue for years to come, we need to sustain further mobilisation of our resources and scale up the eu humanitarian response while considering the specific political priorities of each mena country.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report. parliament called on the eu and its member states to address the root causes of the rapidly deteriorating situation in the middle east and north africa region through a comprehensive and ambitious approach, supported the international campaign against the isil (da'esh) group and welcomed the commitment of the coalition partners to cooperate in line with the common strategy. welcomes in particular the actions of the eu member states participating in the international coalition against isil in contributing to the military intervention or providing logistical, financial and humanitarian assistance, but calls for greater concentration of action in all areas and stresses the need for more coordinated action. these actions could be coordinated under eu supervision, if necessary as part of the common security and defence policy (csdp) and to this end calls for the eu to build up sufficient operational capacity and to develop a genuine common european defence. it is necessary to find a tailor-made solution to address the issue of combating isil (da'esh), al-nusra front and other terrorist groups, based on policy and regional differences. the eu must take on the role of a key facilitator in the regional dialogue, involving all stakeholders in the region, including the arab league, saudi arabia, egypt, turkey and iran.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report as it is important and necessary to support capacity building projects and activities in the middle east and north africa, to combat radicalisation and violent extremism, to promote international cooperation, to address root causes and ongoing crises and to strengthen partnerships with key actors. stability and security in the middle east and north africa region are essential objectives for ensuring the security of the european union. the european parliament is concerned about the humanitarian situation in syria, which has been deteriorating for four years. the provision of humanitarian aid is being reduced by deliberate obstructions to its delivery, and these obstructions must be addressed without delay. the number of people living in areas that are difficult or inaccessible to aid agencies has almost doubled in the past two years. the european parliament considers that the lack of democracy is one of the main causes of political instability in the region and that respect for human rights and basic democratic principles is the strongest long-term protection against permanent instability in the countries of the middle east and north africa region. parliament therefore calls on the eu and its member states to look beyond the middle east and north africa region as a short-term security threat and to support actively and consistently the democratic aspirations of the societies in the region.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the report on the security challenges in the middle east and north africa region and the prospects for political stability. i believe that the conflicts in syria, iraq, yemen and libya and the growing tensions throughout the middle east and north africa are the main factors destabilising the region, and that a strategy for conflict resolution and a legitimate and credible basis for inclusive dialogue with the various parties involved are therefore needed. this report seeks to restore peace by leveraging the european union's influence in the region. the communication aims to address threats and ensure security, strengthen the common strategy for democracy and human rights and strengthen cooperation for economic development. i believe that these steps can help the union to restore stability and peace in the region.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report. the european neighbourhood policy (enp) is designed to deepen relations, strengthen cooperation and strengthen the eu's partnership with its neighbours, with a view to developing a common area of stability, security and prosperity, as underlined in article 8 of the eu treaty. as a result of the growing number of old and new security challenges, the neighbourhood is currently changing and is less stable and significantly less secure, and is also experiencing a greater economic crisis than at the beginning of the implementation of the enp. the eu's revised policy must be based on a general accountability and a shared commitment to respecting eu values and principles, including democracy, the rule of law, human rights and effective, accountable and transparent public authorities, and this is in line with the interests of the public in the neighbouring countries as well as the eu's own interests in ensuring stability, security and prosperity. despite the practical difficulties and challenges, the eu must continue to strongly support transition processes in all and any country, democratisation, respect for human rights and the rule of law. events in the region since 2004, and in particular over the last few years, have shown that the ecb is unable to respond adequately and quickly to rapidly changing and complex circumstances. for these reasons, the revision of the esp must be carried out with a view to strengthening it and in accordance with the principle of long-term progress towards a comprehensive and effective overall eu common foreign and security policy.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because of the need to reform the european neighbourhood policy (enp) in order to build strong, strategic and long-term partnerships with the enp countries, based on preserving and aligning with the eu's values and principles and promoting mutual interests. the commission should, on the basis of common interests, focus on sectors identified with its partners as having the potential for progress and global added value, and progressively expand cooperation based on progress and ambition, in particular to contribute to economic growth and human social development, with particular attention to the younger generations. economic reforms must be accompanied by political reforms and good governance can only be achieved through an open, accountable and transparent decision-making process by democratic institutions. it is also important to build a prosperous and active civil society through transformation and democratisation processes involving the social partners and the business community. civil society, local smes and other non-state actors should continue to be supported as they are the driving force behind the reform process. in addition, dialogue and partnership between different civil society actors and sectors in the eu and neighbouring countries in the context of the enp should be further developed.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the review of the european neighbourhood policy because i believe it is important and necessary to ensure that the review of the enp is carried out in a timely manner. the revised enp should ensure a rapid, flexible and appropriate response to the situation and a strong strategic vision for the development of relations with neighbouring countries, both bilaterally and multilaterally, while maintaining the commitment to promote the core values on which the enp is based. this report calls on the commission to focus on areas of common interest identified with its partners where progress and global added value can be achieved, and to progressively expand cooperation based on progress and ambition, in particular to contribute to economic growth and human social development, with particular attention to the younger generations. the report also stresses that economic reforms must be accompanied by political reforms and that good governance can only be achieved through an open, accountable and transparent decision-making process by democratic institutions.
in writing. ‒ a review of the european neighbourhood policy is necessary both in view of the changing situation in the south and, in the light of russian aggression, in the eu's eastern neighbourhood. the esp is one of the most important elements of the eu's external policy. it must therefore be sufficiently flexible, diversified and inclusive to meet the ambitions of the partners for reform and convergence with the eu, both in terms of the eu's objectives and the new tasks and challenges that have emerged. we must do everything we can to help the eastern partnership countries reduce their vulnerability and dependence on russia, which is using its leverage and creating artificial barriers to prevent these countries from making their own decisions about deep cooperation with the eu, which is economically, values-based and politically attractive to them.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report. the european parliament supports the commission's commitment to further develop the eu digital agenda, including the modernisation of copyright, and recognises the need to review directive 2001/29/ec in order to ensure adequate remuneration for authors, performers and other rightholders, adequate protection of those rights and fair interaction between all actors in the european cultural economy (smes, consumers, users, creators and rightholders) in the digital age, which involves a constantly evolving technological environment in which user behaviour changes, opportunities arise and challenges arise. reforming the eu copyright system is necessary to ensure the necessary legal clarity, stability and certainty, as well as the flexibility, to stimulate investment and growth in the creative and cultural sectors, while removing legal uncertainties and inconsistencies that are hampering the functioning of the digital single market.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to consider measures to contribute to the further development of cultural exchanges and to increase legal certainty in this sector, i.e. the need to revise this directive on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights in the information society. it should be noted that the principle of fair remuneration of rightholders should continue to be ensured in the context of the revision of that directive. the european parliament welcomes the new commission's commitment to further develop the eu's digital agenda, including copyright issues, in the context of its mandate. welcomes the fact that the commission's 2015 work programme promises to develop a digital single market package, including a proposal for a legislative act to modernise copyright rules to meet the needs of the digital age; parliament is concerned about the increase in illegal services and piracy online and the increase in infringements of intellectual property rights in general, which pose a serious threat to the economies of the member states and the eu's creative sector. moreover, any reform of copyright legislation should be based on a high level of protection, given the importance of rights to intellectual creation, and in order to ensure a stable, clear and flexible legal framework that encourages investment and growth in the creative and cultural sectors.

commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, let us consider the problems that cloning livestock will solve in the european union's agriculture. the lack of food? no, we have a bigger problem: food waste. improving animal welfare? and no, we know that the consequences of animal cloning are even greater suffering for animals than has been the case before. the quality of the food? i can't believe this. it is claimed that cloned animals have immune problems and are resistant to many diseases, and food products made from them may be contaminated with more than normal vectors of disease. so i don't see the need for cloning farm animals. it is very good that we are discussing this issue, which has not yet been regulated at european union level, and so far the only acceptable regulation is the prohibition of activities proposed by the rapporteurs and the envi and the agricultural committees.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to ratify the convention on forced labour. the convention calls on governments to take action to better protect workers, especially migrant workers, from abuse and fraud in recruitment. i agree that it is important to have a european-wide debate on the risk factors identified in the latest ilo report on forced labour forcing people into forced labour, i.e. reduced income and poverty or dependency on vulnerable groups (women, migrant children). it is also important that the european anti-poverty strategy goes beyond the coordination of national actions and should set binding poverty reduction targets.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it expresses parliament's support for the council decision on the eu's accession to the protocol of 2014 on forced or compulsory labour to the 1930 international labour organisation convention. this protocol updates the 1930 convention by creating new instruments to combat forced labour and by making it legally binding. in the 21st century, 21 million people are in forced labor. they are victims of exploitation, generating about 150 billion dollars in revenue every year for those who organize and manage such work. 880 000 people in the european union (1.6 million people across the continent) are engaged in these new forms of forced labour. men and women offered work abroad are trapped by alleged employers, migrants are trapped by human traffickers, and children are vulnerable to loss of roots. the protocol therefore states that, as the context and forms of forced labour change, it is necessary to establish preventive and protective measures and mechanisms for redress and compensation (such as compensation and compensation for material and physical damage suffered). it also calls for increased resources and cooperation between states to combat modern forms of slavery, recognising their increasingly international character. the protocol strengthens international law by imposing obligations to prevent forced labour and to provide protection and access to victims of forced labour to defend their rights, such as compensation.
in writing. ‒ i support the position of the rapporteur. human rights must be followed and forced labour directly exploits the most vulnerable people: women, children and migrants. physical and psychological violence cannot be tolerated, therefore i strongly believe that by securing and updating the ilo’s protocol of 2014 on the forced labour convention, 1930 we will be able to better protect workers and their rights. also, we must follow the european anti-poverty strategy, thus only national measures are not enough. moreover, prevention of forced labour could only be effective if we also approached third-world countries, which breach the ilo convention of 1930 on forced labour and its 2014 protocol. due to these reasons, i voted for this council proposal.
in writing. i agree with the recommendation. it is essential that deterrent, imperative and innovative measures to combat forced labour are in place in each member state. an appropriate mechanism for the prevention and criminalisation of forced labour must be established. we cannot allow people to continue to be victims of forced and compulsory labour. states must do more to protect workers from abuse and fraud. in order to prevent forced labour and to provide its victims with protection and the opportunity to defend their rights, it is essential to strengthen in practice the means of enforcing labour law. in addition, the impact of european social policy on labour law should be considered when ratifying this convention.

in writing. ‒ during the second reading regarding the correct application of the law on customs and agricultural matters, i voted against the proposal to reject the council position. if we want to achieve the goal of the single market, then customs union is a necessary attribute. moreover, national customs authorities should collaborate in order to ensure legal and protected flows of goods in and out of europe.
in writing. in order to ensure the correct application of customs and agricultural legislation, particular attention should be paid to mutual assistance and cooperation between the administrative authorities of the member states and the commission. it is also essential to address the shortcomings in the existing systems for detecting fraud in customs activities and the delays in olaf investigations. the procedures for administrative and criminal offences need to be further strengthened at eu level. attention should be drawn to the need to simplify data protection supervision and to clarify the possibility of limiting the visibility of data and the conditions for the admissibility of evidence collected through mutual assistance channels. it should be noted that the power to adopt implementing acts is conferred on the commission, but that member states should have the same access to the register of container status reports as the commission.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to strengthen the eu ban on the trade in seal products. since 2009, the eu has banned trade in seal products such as meat, skin, tails or oil. this prohibition was challenged by the world trade organisation, which in june 2014 justified the eu prohibition but imposed an obligation to clarify the exemption to this prohibition. the new rules will reduce the number of exemptions that allow the eu to trade seal products. the rules agreed with the eu council provide that indigenous communities will continue to be able to trade in these products, as seal hunting is an integral part of their culture and identity. however, the exemption which allowed the marketing of seal products caught under a regulated catch regime will be abolished.
in writing. ‒ i voted on the parliament's report amending the 2009 regulation of the european parliament and of the council on trade in seal products. the purpose of this legislation is to implement the world trade organisation recommendations and resolutions related to the 2009 basic regulation on trade in seal products, in order to ensure that seal products harvested for commercial purposes are no longer placed on the eu market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the regulation which endeavours to ensure that products of commercial seal hunts are not found on the eu market. due to the deadline of 18 october 2015 given by the wto, the issue of commercial hunts must be solved by implementing the seal regulation. i believe that the addition of the new criteria, which include the exception of seal hunting for integral cultural reasons, as well as for hunting for food, is a reasonable move which ensures the fostering of community traditions and cultural heritage. after numerous debates, we must reach a solution that will comply with the international obligations set by the wto. thus, i believe the seal regulation is a necessary ban with considerable exceptions.
in writing. it is welcome that an agreement has been reached and that the regulation on trade in seal products will be aligned with the rules of the world trade organisation. in order to prevent possible discrimination, it is appropriate to remove the exemption provided for in the regulation for products derived from seals caught in small quantities and without the aim of profit, solely for the purpose of sustainable management of marine resources. it should be noted that such hunting cannot be separated from commercial hunting and that the prohibition of commercial hunting is therefore considered discriminatory. it is also essential to assess the impact of this legislation on the essential and social interests of inuit and other indigenous communities and to take into account the right of self-determination of those communities. i support the proposal that citizens be duly informed that the placing on the eu market of seal products harvested by inuit and other indigenous communities is legal.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to ban animal cloning and the marketing of animal products. the new rules would ban the cloning of farmed animals, the trade in their products and the import of these products into the eu. the high mortality rate of cloning technology raises animal welfare and ethical concerns, and i therefore support the proposal to tighten the conditions of the ban and extend it to the descendants of cloned animals. given that some third countries allow the cloning of animals for farming purposes, the new rules would prohibit the import and trade of these animals, their genetic material, their progeny and the food and feed produced from them. in its 2008 opinion on animal cloning, the european food safety authority noted that many cloned animals have had adverse effects on their health and welfare, which have often been serious and have had fatal consequences.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a european parliament statement against the cloning of farmed and bred bovine, porcine, ovine, caprine and equine animals. the european commission has presented two legislative proposals on the cloning of animals for food. the proposals suspend the use of cloning technology in eu farm animals, the placing on the market of live animal clones and cloned embryos, and the marketing of food products (such as meat or milk) produced from animal clones. scientific research has provided conclusive evidence that animal cloning poses a risk to animal welfare and therefore cloning for agricultural purposes is currently prohibited in the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the proposal for a directive to ban the cloning of animals which are kept and reproduced for farming purposes. i believe that the cloning ban might be the reason for the stagnation in the progress of science and it might also threaten the improvement in animal welfare. moreover, according to the report of the european food safety authority, there is absolutely no evidence to justify food safety concerns – food from cloned animals is exactly the same as food from conventionally bred animals. therefore, the question is whether the extensive ban would or would not harm the businesses. hence, the cloning ban might even force many small businesses into providing extensive documentation and could threaten the import of meat and dairy products from countries that allow cloning for agricultural purposes in general. these are the main arguments which gave me the grounds to vote against this proposal.
in writing. the cloning of animals kept and bred for farming purposes must be prohibited, as must any cloning technology. such prohibition shall be of a permanent nature, based on human health, ethical and animal welfare requirements. it should be noted that there is insufficient data on the consequences of animal cloning. animal cloning can have negative effects on animal welfare, reduce the genetic diversity of animal populations and increase the risk of disease, and at the same time have negative consequences for human welfare and health. in view of this, i consider it appropriate to prohibit the import of animals, products of genetic material or animal food for human consumption or animal feed from countries where trade in animal clones or their products is permitted. the impact of animal cloning on food and consumer health can be extremely negative. it may also have a negative impact on livestock production and european agriculture.

in writing. ‒ i voted on the report of the parliament on the procedure for hearing commissioners. public hearings of commissioners-designate are an important opportunity for parliament and eu citizens to assess each candidate's priorities and professional suitability for the role. parliament considers that it would be useful to set a deadline by which all member states should submit their candidates in order to give the president-elect of the commission sufficient time to allocate portfolios. procedures to monitor the follow-up of commissioners-designate to their answers given at the hearing can help to improve control and increase the overall responsibility of the commission, and the european parliament therefore calls for a periodic review of the follow-up of the commissioner-designate to the priorities set when he takes up his duties.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the rapporteur and i have voted for the resolution on procedures and practices regarding commissioner hearings, lessons to be taken from the 2014 process. first of all, i believe that the cut of the number of questions from 42 to 25 is a reasonable proposal. furthermore, so far the vote by individual committees on individual commissioners has no legal consequence. therefore, the evaluation of the commissioner within committees should be more important. these and other possible changes are the significant attempts to make the commission more accountable.
in writing. i agree with the report. in particular, the consultation process helps to improve control and to increase the overall responsibility of the commission. it is therefore necessary to ensure that they are conducted in a smooth and constructive manner. in particular, it is an important opportunity for parliament and eu citizens to assess each candidate's priorities and professional suitability for the job. moreover, hearings of commissioners increase transparency and strengthen the democratic legitimacy of the commission as a whole. in order to ensure a more flexible and dynamic process, it would be useful to set a deadline by which all member states should submit their candidates in order to allow the president-elect of the commission sufficient time to allocate portfolios. it is also essential that the member state should present at least two candidates for consideration by the president-elect of the commission.

in writing. ‒ the objective: to promote family businesses in europe. family businesses can play a crucial role in overcoming the financial and economic crisis and in reviving the economy. more than 60% of all enterprises in the eu are family businesses, accounting for between 40% and 50% of jobs in the private sector. the definition of family businesses is not legally binding and is not used at all in the member states. as a result, family businesses that no longer meet the sme definition are excluded from certain support options. moreover, many family businesses try to keep within the sme criteria set by the commission, and the consequences are clear: they do not employ more people, they prevent profit or turnover from growing, and therefore automatically further economic growth. it is also difficult to compare the situation of family businesses across the eu member states. there are more than 90 different definitions of family businesses across the eu. i agree with the suggestions that more data, figures and facts from individual member states are needed to better understand the difficulties and challenges of family businesses and to encourage the exchange of best practice.

in writing. the european union has been working for some time to achieve gender equality in the academic appointments in academia and universities. positive developments have been made in these areas in recent years, but gender equality remains an urgent issue in the european union. according to the 2012 she figures, women account for only 10% of all rectors, and although for several years in a row the increase in the proportion of women in science was faster than that of men, this seemed a promising change, the number of female researchers is still far below that of the opposite sex. the contribution of women to society must be equally valued and respected. gender equality is an aspiration, but it is also a prerequisite for women and girls to enjoy their full human rights. this is the only way to empower them and strengthen their position in a male-dominated labour market and society. support networks and sharing of best practices will inspire women to pursue their careers and not allow a society governed by stereotypes to limit women's opportunities to pursue careers in science and academia. parliament encouraged the commission to build on existing programmes and initiatives and to develop positive campaigns, paying particular attention to the engineering and technology sector, where, despite recent achievements, the participation of women is below average. awareness-raising campaigns should target men and women who, consciously or unconsciously, promote gender stereotypes that make women unwittingly resist cultural and institutional barriers to advancing in the scientific career.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this recommendation, which seeks to conclude a protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement with guinea-bissau. the first fisheries agreement with guinea-bissau was concluded in 1980 and since then eu member states' fleets have been granted fishing opportunities in guinea-bissau's waters. several protocols to the agreement were subsequently signed, the last of which was in force until 15 june 2012. the new eu-bissau guinea agreement provides for an annual financial contribution of eur 9.2 million, i.e. eur 6.2 million for access to the resources of the bissau guinea economic zone and eur 3 million to support the development of the country's fishing sector. i support the conclusion of this protocol because it is of great importance both for guinea-bissau and for the european fleet fishing in its waters. however, it is important to carry out a more detailed assessment of the future prospects of this agreement. a better link should be established between support to the sector under the fisheries agreement and development cooperation measures. i agree that it is necessary to improve the quantity and reliability of information on the catch and conservation status of marine resources.

in the european parliament, we have repeatedly called on the commission and the council to take note and to take action on the spread of precarious employment, as abusive employment contracts, including those that do not specify working hours, are often abused and abused to avoid compliance with employment and social security obligations. there are many cases where employees are contracted on a temporary or part-time basis, even though people are actually working full-time and on a permanent basis. unfortunately, workers in these types of jobs are the most vulnerable, the most likely to lose their jobs and the least protected by social security. so, alongside high unemployment, the eu is also experiencing a rise in non-standard forms of employment. i therefore ask you, commissioner, whether action should not be taken as soon as possible in this area and consultations be initiated on possible european legislation on atypical forms of employment and contracts? because that's the only way we're gonna be able to do this job without any guarantees.
in writing. social entrepreneurship and social innovation in the fight against unemployment, which parliament is currently pursuing, are among the most important challenges facing the eu today. the economic and financial crisis has increased poverty and social exclusion. long-term unemployment has increased, particularly among young people. it is for these reasons that it is worth considering the possibility of developing a more sustainable economic model for the european union, with a greater focus on the creation and development of social and solidarity-based enterprises. social and solidarity-based enterprises have demonstrated their ability to adapt to economic and social circumstances and offer more flexible and innovative working conditions. this is reflected in the fact that social economy enterprises are well established at local and regional level, which gives them an advantage because they know the specific needs and can offer the right solutions. however, their main objective is not just to make a profit, but more importantly to have a positive impact on society, i.e. to fight unemployment, poverty and support education. also noteworthy is the feature highlighted by the reporter, which highlights the growing problems facing the european union an ageing society and the lowest population growth rates in the world. the commission and the member states are therefore invited to develop long-term plans to strengthen social and territorial cohesion in the union and to help overcome demographic challenges. support for social and solidarity-based economy enterprises will help to address many problems and, most importantly, to strengthen the position of the most excluded and disadvantaged groups in the labour market.

in writing. ‒ in its 2011 transport white paper, the commission set out an ambitious strategy for a future competitive transport system, with a view to enhancing mobility, removing bottlenecks in key areas and promoting growth and employment. together, these proposals will help to achieve a significant reduction in europe's dependence on imported oil and a 60% reduction in vehicle co2 emissions by 2050. i agree that the main objectives should be a reliable and competitive global transport system, competition for eu airlines, the transition to a low-carbon transport system, a balance between the different transport modes, and a common european transport area. it is important that the medium-term review of the transport white paper should be carried out with a long-term vision (2050). the list of initiatives and actions set out in the white paper should be continuously endorsed and complemented and their effectiveness in achieving the common long-term objectives assessed.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal on social entrepreneurship and social innovation in the fight against unemployment. the eu's 2020 strategy set out the guidelines to be followed in the coming years, but the economic and financial crisis has caused the eu to move away from these objectives. in the near future, the eu must address important challenges such as economic and financial sustainability, social well-being and, above all, job creation, with particular attention to the most vulnerable groups, such as, among others, young people, women, the elderly, the long-term unemployed, the disabled, immigrants or the roma community. i agree that the social economy has a key role to play in achieving these goals. social enterprises have demonstrated their resilience to economic shocks and have been able to offer innovative solutions that promote social cohesion, social inclusion or job creation. social innovation and social entrepreneurship are key drivers for the development of the social economy and should be promoted through action in the areas of education and training, better funding, increased visibility and better legal environment.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of a report on the use of social entrepreneurship and social innovation to combat unemployment. the economic and financial crisis has increased poverty and social exclusion indicators, as well as long-term and youth unemployment and social inequalities. this has affected the most marginalised and disadvantaged groups in the labour market, such as the disabled, young people, older people, women, the long-term unemployed and disadvantaged people in the labour market. the commission is invited to ensure that action is taken at eu level to support all types of social and solidarity-based enterprises. parliament is sceptical that the eu is lagging behind the europe 2020 targets, particularly in relation to employment, innovation and the reduction of poverty and social exclusion, but welcomes the 30% increase in the pre-financing budget for the youth employment initiative, which will help to promote social entrepreneurship and innovation.
in writing. ‒ unemployment in the eu remains a major challenge: in december 2014, the unemployment rate in the eu stood at 9.9%. addressing this challenge requires ambitious economic policy and labour market reforms to promote smart, sustainable and inclusive growth and create more jobs in order to overcome the distortions in the eu labour market. i agree with the need for reforms to increase labour market and career flexibility, improve skills and job matching, including greater interaction between education systems and enterprises. it is necessary to ensure better integration of young people, women and older workers, as well as skilled migrants, into the labour market. investments must be used to actively support job creation and employment opportunities. particular attention should be paid to the importance of continuing education and training in creating a competitive eu labour market and in promoting growth and employment.
in writing. ‒ the i voted on a report on creating a competitive european union labour market for the 21st century and matching skills and qualifications to demand and job opportunities to recover from the crisis. the european economic and financial crisis and the resulting economic slowdown have left many member states with high unemployment (9.8% in the eu-28) and problems of public debt, weak economic growth and underinvestment. parliament is concerned that the youth unemployment rate in many member states (28 eu countries 20.9%) is much higher and that improvements and lower unemployment rates are rare. parliament believes that ambitious economic and social policy and labour market reforms are needed, as well as economically sustainable social protection systems, including qualifications for the unemployed, and job opportunities for people with no or very low qualifications. parliament proposes to strengthen the existing eu skills panorama to better identify skills gaps and deficiencies relating to specific sectors, professions and regions and to ensure that information on changing skills needs is collected, processed and disseminated to decision-makers and public authorities, education and training providers and employers, in order to better anticipate future trends.
