in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal to ratify the wto protocol. the ilo convention sets out basic international labour standards, prohibits forced labour and criminalises such activities. the proposed protocol aims to address shortcomings in the implementation of the convention and to combat trafficking in human beings for the purpose of exploitation for labour more effectively, as well as to better protect and compensate victims of forced labour. the protocol also provides that effective measures are to be taken to identify victims of forced labour, to ensure their release, protection, rest and rehabilitation, and to provide other assistance and support. furthermore, member states of the octs must ensure that all victims have access to remedies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation, which supports the proposal that the council authorise member states, in order to safeguard the interests of the european union, to ratify the provisions of the protocol falling within the competence of the eu and recommend that they do so by the end of 2016. the 2014 protocol addresses fundamental rights, trafficking in human beings the crime that affects not only individuals but also entire societies and economies and combating trafficking in human beings. the ratification of this protocol is an important step in the fight against trafficking in human beings and in ensuring the rights of victims of crime throughout europe. the convention on forced or compulsory labour entered into force almost a century ago, but sadly, millions of people worldwide still suffer from forced labour. the protocol of the international labour organisation (ilo) requires member states to develop, in consultation with employers' and workers' organisations, national policies and action plans to eliminate forced labour effectively and sustainably. the protocol also sets out measures to be taken by the member states of the octs to prevent forced labour: by educating and informing people to ensure that legislation on the prevention of forced labour applies to all workers in all sectors of the economy, by protecting people from possible abuses and fraud in recruitment and employment, and by addressing the risk factors for the growth of forced labour.
in writing. i give my consent to the conclusion of this agreement. millions of people worldwide suffer from the crimes of forced labor and human trafficking. this is a serious problem which cannot be postponed. a proper mechanism for its prevention and criminalisation should be established. in view of this, it is essential that all states ratify the provisions of the protocol. more active action is needed to combat trafficking in human beings. in the fight against trafficking in human beings, particular attention should be paid to the identification of victims, the promotion of private sector accountability and more effective prosecution. the rights of victims of crime must be adequately and fully guaranteed throughout europe. the principle that no one shall be held in slavery or servitude (slavery and the slave trade in all their forms shall be prohibited) must be implemented without any reservations.
the ratification of the protocol by the member states will facilitate the fight against trafficking in human beings, and i therefore welcome the draft council decision and propose that parliament give its consent, and i call on the member states to ratify the protocol without delay.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, in which the european parliament supports the commission's proposal to mobilise the european union solidarity fund (esf) and to provide financial assistance to bulgaria following the severe winter weather conditions that led to the disaster, which is classified as a 'major natural disaster' under the esf. parliament also endorsed the proposal to grant financial assistance to greece following two disasters in the euro-region and central greece, which are classified as 'regional disasters' under the essf. in late january and early february 2015, a large part of bulgaria was affected by heavy rainfall, snow, floods and landslides, with the south-eastern regions of the country suffering the most damage. these events have caused significant damage to public infrastructure. in early february 2015, floods in eastern macedonia and thrace caused significant damage to key infrastructure, public buildings, private homes, businesses and greek agriculture, destroying agricultural infrastructure, warehouses and crops. water and sanitation infrastructure in 17 settlements has been damaged. at the same time, large areas of central and western greece were affected by other floods, which caused even greater damage, resulting in the interruption of electricity supply, the isolation of several mountain settlements and the destruction of some greek cultural heritage sites.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to extend the protection of geographical indications to non-agricultural products. a geographical indication indicates that the reputation, quality or other characteristic of a good is linked to a specific location. it is currently used exclusively for agricultural products and is used by some 3 000 agricultural products. i agree that it is necessary to exploit the economic potential of protecting the exclusivity and quality of non-agricultural products, to preserve the know-how and jobs associated with them and to contribute to the fight against counterfeiting. i therefore support the relevant eu rules proposed to this end.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, in which the european parliament considers that a safeguard measure at european union level should be created as part of a wider ambitious strategy to support high quality eu products and based on a stronger commitment by the eu institutions to consider the manufacturing and craft sectors as a driving force for economic growth and the completion of the single market, thereby increasing the value of local industrial and craft products, supporting the development of the local economy and job creation in the areas concerned, promoting tourism and enhancing consumer confidence. the european parliament welcomes the commission's initiative to organise a consultation of stakeholders to determine the possibility of extending the protection of a geographical indication of the european union to non-agricultural products, welcomes the results of the consultation concluded in october 2014 and expressly supports the eu system of protection based on geographical indications for non-agricultural products.
in writing. – the extension of unitary geographical indication (gi) protection to non-agricultural products at eu level is another step towards an even more unified single market. i voted in favour of this report as a gi protection system would be beneficial in economic, social and cultural terms. the commission estimates that there are around 4 million jobs directly and indirectly employed in these sectors and that two-thirds of the regions producing non-agricultural geographical indication products have a poverty rate or an unemployment rate above 20 percent. as the local products that may be subject to such protection are usually based on the activities of small and medium enterprises (smes), the extension of gis would enhance the competitiveness of smes in particular and would stimulate the grow of local industries. what is more, such local industries are very important sources of established yet vibrant cultural and social heritage, which further highlights the authenticity of european products and thus makes them even more attractive and competitive.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to better protect traditional products and knowledge. in particular, a common protection of geographical indications at eu level is necessary. geographical indications would help consumers to identify authentic products and ensure that those products meet the standards of origin and quality. the protection of geographical indications in the european union would enable consumers to identify authentic, original products. this would be an effective tool in the eu single market to help prevent abuse. it should be noted that at present there is insufficient protection for such products and their economic potential is not being exploited. it should be noted that the protection of a geographical indication for non-agricultural products would contribute to european economic growth and job creation.
in writing. ‒ the the current geographical protection of agricultural product names offers the opportunity to preserve the culture and culinary heritage of a country that has developed over the centuries. but as we know, heritage is not just food. it is also a variety of handicrafts. in lithuania, there is no evidence of abuses of geographical indications outside agriculture, although there are some unique products in my country, such as musical instruments, that have clear geographical indications. however, if such abuse is at least theoretically possible, it is necessary to prepare for it in advance. it would be a pity if, for example, the well-known bag of pipes in our country, the 'labanoro pipe', which has a clear geographical reference to the area from which this musical instrument originates, were to be produced by anyone other than the original samples. this would damage the name and authenticity of the work. i believe that there should be no distinction between agricultural and non-agricultural products in the protection of geographical indications. this will not be easy to regulate, but it will serve to protect the cultural identity of each eu country, which is becoming increasingly important in an increasingly globalised world.

in writing. i welcome the revision of this regulation, as it is primarily for the benefit of consumers the new rules will make it easier and cheaper to recover small debts in other eu countries, except denmark. the european small claims procedure will enable individuals and businesses to recover debts incurred in other eu countries using standard forms. this procedure will cover claims up to eur 5 000, without the need to hire lawyers to recover the amounts, and the nominal fee for this procedure will be reduced to that applicable to domestic debt recovery and will be payable not only in cash but also by bank transfer or bank card. this regulation obliges eu states to provide free assistance in filling in the dispute forms and choosing the competent court. member states are also encouraged to use video or audio conferencing for the settlement of disputes, in order to avoid the need for the parties to proceed to another country, which also contributes significantly to reducing the costs of debt recovery. this procedure has been in place since 2009 and the study revealed that since then the costs of litigation in cross-border cases have fallen by up to 40% and the duration of litigation has been reduced from two and a half years to five months. the improvements adopted by the european parliament this session will deliver even better results for our citizens, consumers and small and medium-sized businesses.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims at simplifying debt recovery in the eu. the european small claims procedure, which has been in operation since 2009, allows people and businesses to use standard forms to settle debts accumulated in other eu countries, for example, due to unpaid bills for services provided. the procedure does not require the use of a lawyer and the judgment is recognised and enforced in another eu country. the renewed european rules on small claims facilitate the recovery of debts from companies or individuals operating in another eu country. the debt ceiling for this procedure is raised from eur 2 000 to eur 5 000, the stamp duty is reduced and the use of videoconferencing for the settlement of disputes is encouraged. the use of european small claims has led to a 40% reduction in the costs of litigation in similar cases and a fivefold reduction in the length of proceedings.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which examines and amends regulation (ec) no 861/2007 of the european parliament and of the council establishing a european small claims procedure. this regulation aims to simplify and speed up the examination of cases of an international nature relating to small claims and to reduce costs. it was designed specifically to help consumers as well as small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) to bring their claims and thus ensure their access to justice. the rapporteur fully supports this objective. five years after the regulation entered into force, a comprehensive assessment has been carried out which has shown that the european small claims procedure is a useful tool. however, as highlighted in the commission's november 2013 report on the application of that procedure, there is still a great potential to extend and strengthen its uptake. the european small claims procedure has reduced the costs of litigation in cross-border small claims cases by up to 40% and the duration of litigation has been reduced from two years and five months to an average of five months.
in writing. i agree with the report. i believe that there should be uniform procedures across the eu to help simplify and speed up crossborder litigation in the eu, while also facilitating the protection of consumers' rights. every citizen must be able to exercise his right to go to court and to seek prompt compensation without incurring high costs. i support the proposal to increase the maximum amount from the current eur 2 000 to eur 10 000. it is also appropriate to include cases where both parties are domiciled or established in the same member state but which have a different cross-border element. the time, effort and expense involved must not be significantly disproportionate to the size of the claim. it is therefore necessary to simplify and speed up the resolution of such disputes, as well as to reduce the costs for individuals or small enterprises and to reduce the duration of the procedure. the use of the european small claims procedure should be encouraged.
in writing. – the proposal will have a positive impact on citizens undertaking cross-border businesses and is particularly designed to support smes by facilitating the litigation procedure and by reducing costs and administrative burdens, with the objective of boosting cross-border business activities eu-wide.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal to limit certain emissions into the air. the proposal contains provisions for medium-sized combustion plants. it aims to contribute to the reduction of nox, so2 and dust emissions by setting limit values for new and existing installations and by introducing a simple registration system to facilitate the implementation of a large part of the member states' emission reduction commitments.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the commission's proposal for a directive on the limitation of certain emissions of pollutants into the air from medium combustion plants. this proposal is part of the european union's action programme on air quality, set out in the revised eu thematic air pollution strategy, and is consistent with and supports the europe 2020 strategy's objectives of smart, inclusive and sustainable growth. it aims to protect the interests of small and medium-sized enterprises, in accordance with the principle 'think small first'. in order to avoid a significant impact on small and medium-sized enterprises, which operate the majority of medium-sized combustion plants, more lenient measures were considered, such as the provision that operators would not be required to obtain a permit but would have to notify the competent authorities of the operation of the plant, thus ensuring registration. in addition, in order to make progress towards the eu's long-term (post-2020) objective of further reducing the health and environmental impacts of air pollution, a range of policy options were evaluated in the search for a cost-effective package of measures. a sample of additional eu source control measures was examined, one of which was for emissions from medium-sized combustion plants.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this report. the importance of this report first and foremost stems from the fact that the proposal closes an important legislative loophole due to which emissions of air pollutants from medium combustion plants were left largely unregulated at the eu level. the eu must ensure that high quality of air is maintained and that the industry develops at no cost to the health of citizens. the clause on benchmarking progress and carrying out a review by the commission every 10 years takes into account the possible progress of cleaning technology and thus contributes to the practicality of this report. however, proper implementation of this report is very much necessary as about 75% of medium combustion plants are run by small and medium-sized enterprises, which have to be safeguarded from excessive amount of red-tape and double regulation.
in writing. a coherent and ambitious framework for tackling emissions needs to be developed at eu level. in particular, it is necessary to close regulatory loopholes and strike a balance between the costs and benefits of business to the environment and human health. air pollution must be controlled. it is therefore necessary to set limit values for new and existing installations, including the introduction of a simple registration system. however, the new regulation must not create an unjustified and disproportionate administrative burden. it is worth noting that reducing emissions from medium-sized combustion plants would contribute to the eu's energy and climate objectives, as well as to reducing greenhouse gases, increasing energy efficiency and promoting renewable energy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal to repeal directive 83/417/eec on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to certain caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption. this directive aims to replace the existing provisions with a new one in order to adapt them to the further development of legislation, in particular as regards the right to food. in addition, it is necessary to align the composition requirements for edible caseins with the international standard food code. such harmonisation will ensure a level playing field for food business operators on the world market. i support the casein and caseinate labelling requirements which will enable consumers, particularly those with food allergies or intolerances, to choose foodstuffs which are safe for them with sufficient information.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the directive of the european parliament and of the council on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to caseins and caseinates for human consumption. this commission proposal of march 2014 proposes to repeal the former directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to certain lactoprotein (caseins and caseinates) intended for human consumption and to replace it by a new directive, as the existing provisions need to be improved and the compositional requirements for edible caseins need to be aligned with the international standard (food code). the european parliament supports labelling requirements for casein and caseinates which will enable consumers, in particular those with food allergies or intolerances, to choose safe food products with sufficient information. the proposal should be considered in the context of the general food law, which aims to ensure the free movement of safe and wholesome food and thus to make a significant contribution to the health and well-being of citizens. it should therefore also be ensured that consumers are properly informed about the food they consume.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal on the financial rules applicable to the eu general budget. new provisions are included on market consultation, a new innovation partnership procedure, compliance with environmental, social and labour law as one of the key requirements, non-specific order of assessment of criteria, a methodology for awarding contracts based on the most economically advantageous tender. the financial regulation also includes, for the first time, works and service concessions and the same types of procedures as for public contracts.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with the commission's proposal to bring the financial regulation into line with the provisions of the new directives on public procurement and the award of concession contracts. indeed, the obligation to apply common eu procurement rules to crisis management measures under the common foreign and security policy, and in particular to civilian missions under the common security and defence policy (csdp), is a reason for delays in the procurement of essential equipment and services, with a significant negative impact on the work of the missions. as usual, csdp missions have to operate in crisis situations and for a limited time. they shall be launched by a unanimous council decision recognising the need for an immediate response to the crisis. the eu's international credibility is threatened when the union takes on important commitments for peace and security. in addition, the safety of mission staff is often of paramount importance and they do not have the necessary equipment, such as armored vehicles. the european parliament therefore considers that special rules should be established for csdp missions which are primarily operating in crisis or post-crisis conditions. this is in line with the conclusions of the european council of december 2013.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report. the rules on public procurement and concessions should also apply to contracts concluded on behalf of the eu institutions. it is therefore appropriate to align the financial regulation with the provisions of the new directives on public procurement and on the award of concession contracts. in order to ensure early detection and prevention of risks, a common system must be in place in the eu to ensure strict application of the exclusion. it should be noted that this system should be built on the basis of the existing central database on the prohibition of participation in the procurement procedure. the protection of the financial interests of the union must remain a priority in the pursuit of the objectives envisaged. this protection must be continuously strengthened. in this context, i support the proposal to include tax evasion in the procurement procedures of the union institutions as a ground for exclusion from the procedure.
blue-card question.– we heard a speech praising gazprom as the most reliable supplier of gas to europe. one might get this idea, but how do you explain the situation in gazprom? this is probably the most corrupt major company in europe, with its huge buildings, and owners or management with close ties to moscow, and some ‘black’ deals made. finally, how would you explain the fact that gazprom charges ukraine more than germany? is there anything political in this? do you see this as purely economic and based on financial issues? how, if you are an economist and you base your thoughts on this, can you explain these higher prices for ukraine than for germany?
reducing the european union's energy dependence on russia is one of the key objectives of the energy union. therefore, such a long-term agreement between european energy companies and gazprom on the doubling of gas supplies to the nord stream pipeline is clearly contrary to the energy policy of the european union. the agreement unfairly circumvents the central and eastern european member states, which are still cut off from the european energy gas and electricity networks. what is the situation now for the member states most affected by russia in terms of energy, which, like lithuania, have built a liquefied gas terminal at their own expense, without financial assistance from the european union, in order to have at least one energy alternative and to reduce the price paid for energy resources? if private companies can make decisions that may even harm the interests of individual member states, our partners like ukraine, and the european union as a whole, then the question arises of what value is there in all our efforts to strengthen our energy independence, to further distance ourselves from russia in terms of energy, to invest billions of dollars in the missing infrastructure, and so on. it is scandalous that we have not been able to ensure that the commission is obliged to be informed of all energy agreements and to assess their impact. this case, like the volkswagen scandal, raises serious doubts about the credibility of the institutions of the european union, commissioner.
mr president, back in july of this year a group of members of the european parliament, including myself, wrote to the commission to ask it to assess the plans to double the capacities of the nord stream. i was rather shocked by the commissioner’s written answer, i quote: ‘adding capacity to the nord stream pipeline system is first and foremost a commercial decision.’ i call it business as usual, nothing new. therefore, in addition to the many good opinions expressed by my colleagues, i wish to ask the commissioner three simple questions. firstly, are you still sure, bearing in mind all the geopolitics, that bypassing ukraine is first and foremost a commercial project? secondly, do you not think that the expansion of nord stream inherently contradicts the eu energy security strategy and eu energy union? and thirdly, how can you see doubling the nord stream capacity as being consistent with reducing eu energy dependency on russia?
the commission should not treat this project as a commercial venture only, but should look at it in its entirety in the context of the european union's geostrategic interests, security and climate objectives. this project does not meet the stated objectives of the european union in terms of energy diversification and does not create a new source or route. and it does not meet the european union's priorities for energy efficiency and energy independence. there is no need to build another infrastructure in the baltic sea region. especially when gas consumption is steadily decreasing. there are already alternative sources, such as the liquefied gas terminal built in lithuania, which unfortunately is only used for a third of the time due to the lack of separation and the lack of networks. i want to believe that nord stream 2 will not become another example of the failure of european solidarity, unlike its predecessor nord stream, and will not be recognised as a project of european interest. how much can you say and do?
in writing. the project of the second 'nordstream' branch, which is being pushed by russia, should be assessed in the light of the current geopolitical perspective. the fate of ukraine is far from settled, and a front that has a significant impact on the resolution of europe's biggest security crisis appears to have moved into syria. russia continues to deepen tensions with the west. although the european commission successfully suspended the southstream project, expecting that russian energy interceptors would not be able to cover all of europe, moscow and turkey agreed to implement the bluestream project. but now we see that the partners may also be in serious trouble over the pipeline, because of their different approaches to the middle east crisis. in this context, the second nordstream project therefore took on new colours. i would like to draw attention to two aspects. first, the implementation of the project would allow russia to achieve its long-standing strategic objective of bypassing ukraine as a transit country for gas to europe. ukraine would lose not only $2 billion in annual revenue but also the ability to counter russia's "gas policy". secondly, it is strategically very convenient for russia to have only its own corridors for transporting gas to western europe, so that no one pays for the transportation costs. however, this would only further entrench the already strong influence of the russian gas giant in europe it poses a serious threat to the energy security of the countries of central and eastern europe and is fundamentally contrary to the idea of european solidarity.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which gives parliament its support to the commission's proposal to amend the provisions of the directive on payment services in the internal market. improvements are needed as important technical innovations have been introduced in the retail payments market the number of electronic and mobile payments has increased rapidly and new types of payment services have emerged on the market which pose challenges to the existing system. the commission has consulted and presented a green paper 'developing an integrated european card, online and mobile payments market' in which it highlighted that important areas of the payments market, in particular card, online and mobile payments, remain fragmented across national borders. it has also been found that in certain cases the scope of the existing directive, and in particular the elements to which it does not apply, such as certain payment activities, are too ambiguous, too general or simply outdated in the light of market developments. this has led to legal uncertainty, potential security risks in the payment chain and a lack of consumer protection in certain areas.
in writing. in order to improve the legal regulation of payment services, it is appropriate to extend the scope of the directive. in order to promote competition, it is important to ensure that legislation ensuring legal certainty is applied in the field of payment services. it is also necessary to ensure secure, efficient, competitive and innovative electronic payments. the protection of the rights and interests of payment service users should play a particular role. it is important to promote and ensure the principle of the functioning of the single market so that consumers, retailers and businesses can enjoy the full benefits of the single market. it should be noted that the new regulation must be flexible, easily adaptable to new market developments and new services, as the services market is constantly undergoing active development. the identification of barriers to innovation and efficiency improvements in advance is essential for the effective functioning of the single market.

in writing. - i voted for this resolution on the red mud disaster. on 4 october 2010, a collapsed waste dump in hungary released nearly 1 million cubic metres of highly charged red mud, flooding several villages and killing 10 people and injuring nearly 150. this disaster is attributed to poor implementation of eu legislation, insufficient checks, gaps in the relevant eu legislation and the performance of the warehouse manager. unfortunately, lessons have not been learned from this disaster, as the relevant eu legislation and international conventions continue to be poorly implemented, and checks continue to be poorly carried out. i support calls for the commission to focus more on research and technological development in the field of prevention and management of hazardous waste. the commission should develop guidelines for stress testing in existing mines with large waste storage facilities.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution, which deals with the situation following the accident in hungary, where a landfill collapsed on 4 october 2010 and almost 1 million cubic metres of very high-purity red sludge were released. it flooded several villages, killed 10 people and injured nearly 150 and contaminated vast areas of land, including four natura 2000 sites. this red mud accident is the biggest industrial disaster in hungary. it was a time of rapid and effective response by national authorities and of great efforts by civil society to help in the event of disaster. however, the european parliament is concerned that there seems to have been little learning from the experience of the past five years, and that the relevant eu legislation and international conventions continue to be poorly implemented, checks continue to be poorly carried out and almost no gaps in the relevant eu legislation have been filled in the meantime. parliament also expressed concern at the existence of similar sites in several member states and called on all member states with red sludge tanks to verify as soon as possible that red sludge is properly classified as hazardous waste and to correct any permits that contained incorrect classification.

in writing. climate change is one of the greatest challenges facing humanity, with implications for sustainable development, health and the global economy. rising temperatures, melting ice caps, and increased droughts and floods are all signs that the climate is warming. the response to climate change therefore requires an urgent, responsible and global solution based on solidarity of the international community. on 6 march 2015, eu environment ministers formally committed to reducing greenhouse gas emissions in the european union. the european union and its member states have jointly committed to a binding target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions in the european union by at least 40% by 2030 compared to 1990. in march 2015, the european union informed the secretariat of the unfccc of the estimated national contribution. the european union's contribution should inspire other parties by ensuring clarity, transparency and achievement of objectives. the european union's ambitious commitments are crucial to ensuring its credibility in the negotiations. the eu needs to pursue an effective and ambitious policy to transition to a different energy system by 2050, using not only climate and energy policy instruments but also other areas such as transport, research, innovation, trade and development cooperation.
in writing. climate change is no longer a matter of debate, but a problem that must be addressed now. it is right that the european union is taking a leading role in setting ambitious targets to help tackle climate change. but we must not forget that the most important thing in this fight is to attract the solidarity of the entire international community. the efforts of the european union alone will not be enough, and it is therefore necessary to finally reach a global, binding agreement. in this global context, we should not forget the competitiveness of our industry and the problem of carbon leakage. i am convinced that the new energy model, focusing on energy efficiency and renewable energy sources, that we have chosen to implement in europe is the right way to fight climate change, and that clear progress has been made and that new opportunities must be exploited in the negotiations leading to the adoption of a new international climate change agreement in paris.

in writing. ‒ the the refugee crisis and ineffective management are now being identified as a fundamental problem for the european union, giving rise to economic and social problems. with the influx of refugees, old europe faces serious challenges and problems. therefore, a long-term solution should be provided for and a financial plan should be provided for. in order to respond to the current refugee and migrant crisis, it is appropriate to increase the union's resources. additional financial support is urgently needed for the eu countries most affected by the migrant flows. it could also be used by third countries hosting syrian refugees. this would contribute to the stabilisation of the countries of origin and assist the countries of transit. more attention should be paid to the activities of frontex. it is necessary to ensure better protection of the external borders and to control the flows of migrants by preventing smuggling.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is the report by which parliament decided to waive the immunity of the hungarian mep, béla kovács. the prosecutor general of hungary has requested the waiver of the immunity of this member of the european parliament in order to allow an investigation to be carried out on the basis of reasonable suspicions in order to determine whether mr kovács will be charged with the crime of espionage against the eu institutions. the hungarian criminal code provides that a person who conducts intelligence activities against the european parliament, the european commission or the council of the european union for the benefit of a non-eu country is punishable under article 261 thereof. the same article of the hungarian criminal code provides that a person who conducts intelligence activities against hungary for the benefit of a foreign state or a foreign organisation commits a criminal offence punishable by a term of imprisonment of between two and eight years.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for the request for waiver of the immunity of béla kovács. the request for the waiver of the immunity of béla kovács is made in order that investigations can be carried out, on the basis of reasonable suspicions, to see whether a charge will lie against him with regard to the offence of espionage against the institutions of the european union under section 261/a of act c of 2012 on the hungarian criminal code. according to that section, any person who conducts intelligence activities for a non-european union third country against the european parliament, the european commission or the council of the european union shall be punishable in accordance with section 261, paragraph 1 of which provides that any person who conducts intelligence activities for a foreign power or foreign organisation against hungary is guilty of a felony punishable by a term of imprisonment of between two and eight years. this is a very serious allegation and it is our duty to remove any obstacles for the investigation and to clear the path for the right and just decision to be made.

in writing. ‒ climate change is a present and real problem which can be addressed only by a joint international effort. the previous agreements such as kyoto proved to be effective to some extent – especially in the case of europe, which despite the steady gdp growth has reduced its emission levels by 19% since 1990. however, as a result of the new—growing economies in the east and other world economic activity, overall emission levels in the world have doubled and the costs of inaction might be very high. therefore, i very much support this resolution’s call for an ambitious, global and binding agreement. it is time to reconsider the action plan which could help mitigate climate change.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution, which sets out the mandate of the european parliament's delegation to the united nations climate change conference in paris at the end of the year. i support calls for binding targets to combat the effects of climate change: 40% reduction in carbon dioxide emissions by 2030, 30% for renewable energy and 40% for energy efficiency. the eu's climate policy needs to be stepped up to meet the eu's 2050 greenhouse gas emission reduction target of 80-95% compared to 1990 levels. measures to combat climate change need to be reviewed by 2020 to take account of the latest scientific assessments. in 2015, the eu and its member states should agree on a plan to contribute in good faith to the us$100 billion commitment to combat climate change by 2020. it is important to use additional sources of financing by deferring part of the marketing of allowances or by using the revenues from the control of emissions from the aviation and shipping sectors.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because the european parliament is actively involved in european policy on climate change. the european parliament recalls that it will have to give its consent for the european union to ratify the legally binding agreement adopted at the paris conference. the european parliament will therefore have to participate fully in the coordination meetings organised in the context of the paris conference. the european union's contribution should inspire other parties by ensuring clarity, transparency and achievement of objectives. the success of the european union (its emissions decreased by 19% between 1990 and 2012, and its gdp increased by 45%) and the fact that eu emissions are a decreasing share of global emissions show that climate change mitigation is compatible with economic development. the european union must continue and strengthen its diplomatic efforts to better understand the positions of partner countries, to encourage them to adopt ambitious policies to combat climate change and to build alliances to that end. the implementation of the commitments made by the parties to the paris agreement will also depend on the efforts of non-state actors such as cities, regions, industry and investors. the paris conference must give a clear signal to these actors to encourage them to take action, including international recognition of their efforts.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the resolution ‘towards a new international climate agreement in paris’. this resolution calls for an ambitious, legally binding and comprehensive global agreement with economy-wide reduction targets. it underlines that the agreement should have a long-term mitigation objective in line with scientific findings. it underlines that the agreement must contain a 5-year review process that enables a progressive strengthening of the agreement. therefore, based on these grounds i voted for this resolution.
in writing. ‒ climate change is one of the most pressing global issues. it is therefore essential that an agreement on a new international climate change agreement is reached in paris. we cannot remain indifferent to the challenges of climate change. the issues of climate change mitigation, adaptation, finance, technology development, transparency of action and support need to be addressed urgently. particular attention should be paid to the world's largest polluters, which should participate in the agreement and undertake equivalent commitments. all countries in the world should make legally binding climate change mitigation commitments after 2020. it should be noted that the new agreement should be in line with today's economic reality. all countries must contribute to the financing of climate change action and the divide between developing and developed countries must be removed.
the joint undertaking has made considerable progress in implementing the action plan to address the deficiencies identified by the court of auditors, as confirmed by the scl. the company's ex post audit strategy was improved in cooperation with the national funding authorities, a dedicated audit reporting format was introduced and a systematic assessment of the quality of these audits was carried out. this was accompanied by an exchange of information on the requirements of financial programmes and examples of good practice, as well as by an improved policy on the management and prevention of conflicts of interest and the development of a comprehensive database containing all information related to conflicts of interest and actions. since artemis and eniac no longer exist separately, any recommendations related to improvements in audit procedures will have to be implemented by the new ecsel joint undertaking, and it is therefore important to give it time and to provide it with a discharge.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for an eu-swiss agreement that would limit the ability of eu citizens to hide their finances in swiss banks and thus avoid paying taxes. from 2018, the eu and switzerland will automatically exchange data on the bank accounts of their citizens. this agreement on tax transparency contributes to the fight against tax evasion and fraud. it will not only exchange information on interest or dividends but also on account balances or sales of financial assets.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it gives parliament its consent to the conclusion of an eu-switzerland agreement on the automatic exchange of information on reportable accounts with a view to improving international cooperation and compliance in the field of taxation. this agreement is an important step in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion, updating the 2004 agreement which ensured that switzerland applied measures equivalent to those of the eu savings income tax directive. the eu and switzerland will automatically exchange information on financial accounts held by each other's residents as of 2018. the aim is to respond to cases where a taxpayer attempts to conceal capital, which constitutes income or assets for which no tax has been paid. the agreement also aims to ensure that switzerland applies stricter measures that are equivalent to the eu directive updated in march 2014 and that it complies with the provisions on automatic exchange of information on reportable accounts promoted by the 2014 global standards of the organisation for economic cooperation and development (oecd).
in writing. ‒ i voted for this agreement because it represents an important step in ongoing efforts to clamp down on tax fraud and tax evasion and upgrades the 2004 agreement that ensured that switzerland applied measures equivalent to those in an eu directive on the taxation of savings. i support the fact that, under this agreement, the eu and switzerland will automatically exchange information on the financial accounts of each other’s residents, starting in 2018. the aim is to address situations where a taxpayer seeks to hide capital representing income or assets for which taxes have not been paid.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report and i am in favour of the conclusion of this agreement. this agreement is necessary to prevent tax fraud and tax evasion. it is necessary to strengthen eu-swiss cooperation in the field of taxation. switzerland needs to become more open. therefore, the exchange of information on financial accounts between residents is necessary. in particular, it will ensure full tax transparency and cooperation between tax administrations and prevent illegal tax activities. it is essential that switzerland applies the stricter measures provided for in eu law. the contracting parties shall enhance international cooperation and mutual compliance in the field of taxation by providing each other with administrative and judicial assistance.

in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because it gives parliament its support for the commission's proposal to repeal the eu's savings tax directive 2003/48/ec. the commission notes that the 2014 guidelines are not binding on the member states and that the commission has not yet adopted a decision on the application of the guidelines. as a result, there is now a duplication of reporting standards in the union. in march 2015, together with the tax transparency package, the commission proposed to repeal the 2003 savings tax directive, so that member states would not be obliged to apply the provisions of both directives, avoiding the inconvenience of double data collection and reporting systems, and parliament agreed today.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because the scope of financial products covered by the eu savings tax directive and the directive on administrative cooperation, while generally similar, is not exactly identical. some products, mostly low-risk depository accounts promoted for savings purposes will not be reported anymore under the directive on administrative cooperation. while there are low risks for tax evasion, i believe it is important for the commission to continue monitoring that the repeal does not create loopholes.
in writing. i agree with the report. it is essential to close any existing legal loopholes and to prevent tax evasion or avoidance. in addition, only one standard for the automatic exchange of information should be applied in the eu. two standards cannot be applied in parallel. an effectively functioning common system will help to avoid duplication of reporting systems. in view of this, i think it is appropriate to repeal the savings income tax directive. this would give proper effect to the principles of better regulation, as well as clarity and legal certainty. in addition, the new legal framework will reduce potential additional risks and ensure effective safeguards and reduce administrative burden.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to give more rights to travellers who buy package tours. online shopping and the services offered by low-cost airlines have changed the way people buy their travel, so that many package holidays are now outside the scope of the eu rules that have been in force since 1990. in order to ensure adequate protection of travellers, the updated rules will clarify the provisions on package tours comprising different services (flights, accommodation and car rental) purchased together. it is important that travellers are afforded the same level of consumer protection, whether the package is purchased in an office or online. travel organisers will also have to provide their customers with detailed information about the upcoming trip and clearly identify who will be responsible for the proper execution of the package.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it gives parliament its support for the new european parliament and council directive on package travel and associated travel arrangements. from now on, whether a package is bought in an office or online, travellers will be afforded the same protection. the commission will also be able to provide information on the implementation of the new rules on the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment. parliament also included a provision whereby different services such as flights, accommodation and car hire purchased together are considered as part of a package. even if different travel services are purchased in one payment, whether online, at the office or by telephone, the same traveller rights as for package travellers apply to such a booking.
in writing. ‒ i have voted against because i do not support the recommendation approval for second reading on the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council on package travel and linked travel arrangements, amending regulation (ec) no 2006/2004 and directive 2011/83/eu of the european parliament and of the council and repealing council directive 90/314/eec.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of this text. this is a case of the eu responding and adapting to the changing and ever-modernising environment, where packaged sales and linked travel arrangements are becoming more and more popular. the new directive provides better consumer protection by setting clear standards on cancellation terms that limit post-contractual price increase to 8% (and establishing the right to cancel the arrangement free of charge in case of higher increases in price), ensuring the return of payments to customers in case of bankruptcy of a service provider though insolvency provisions, and so on. these new rules will protect the 120 million europeans that use combined travel arrangements. the commission estimates that the implementation of the new rules will reduce damages to consumers by about €430 million annually.
in writing. i agree with the report. it should be noted that the increasing use of the internet has made the current legal framework less clear and relevant. new rules are therefore needed to make the eu simpler and safer for passengers. the protection of travellers must be uniform, regardless of whether the travel is purchased at a post office or online, and the protection of travellers will be uniform. the eu needs to apply harmonised common mandatory rules on the protection of travellers. a high level of consumer protection is necessary. particular attention should be paid to cases where tour operators or service providers become insolvent. it should be noted that in order to improve competition in this market, a level playing field is needed for undertakings in the travel sector. in addition, the financial and administrative burden on businesses should be reduced and legal barriers to cross-border trade removed.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to abolish the roaming charge. the updated rules provide for the abolition of the eu roaming charge as from june 2017. they also propose to restrict the ability of internet access service providers to block or slow down the operation of competing applications. as of 15 june 2017, mobile operators will not be able to charge higher rates for mobile phone calls, text messages and data transfers when leaving the eu. the maximum allowable premium for a minute of a call abroad will not exceed €0,05, €0,02 for a message and €0,05 for a megabyte of data transmitted as from 30 april 2016. the new rules also require internet access providers to manage all traffic in the same way, i.e. not to block or slow down certain senders or receivers or the applications they use, unless necessary to comply with court orders, maintain network security and combat cyber attacks.
in writing. ‒ i have voted against the recommendation for second reading on the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down measures concerning open internet access and amending directive 2002/22/ec on universal service and users’ rights relating to electronic communications networks and services and regulation (eu) no 531/2012 on roaming on public mobile communications networks within the union. due to the fact that the parliament had to give in on a very complicated mechanism to ensure the sustainability of certain operators, even though the principle of this safeguard clause was shared, the design is very complicated.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a very important piece of eu legislation. this new law, when implemented, will have a positive impact that citizens of the eu will be able to experience themselves in their day-to-day life. this law will put an end to roaming charges as of 15 june 2017. a barrier that has been a hindrance in our single eu market, where people could move between countries freely but could not use electronic communications as they would do at home, will be abolished. people will be able to pay the price they pay at home for texts, calls and mobile data everywhere in the eu.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report. in order to achieve the digital single market, no roaming charge should be applied in the eu. the eu must have access to an open internet and the principle of net neutrality must be properly implemented. all internet data flows should be treated equally. in addition, an effective open internet protection mechanism is needed. to this end, common rules for electronic communications should apply. the new legal framework will help ensure the openness of the internet, while avoiding the fragmentation of the internal market due to measures adopted by individual member states. internet service providers should not block or slow down the performance of competing applications. it is therefore necessary to ensure that all flows are managed in the same way by the service providers. all internet traffic should be treated equally. particular attention should be paid to the implementation of the principles of the right of consumers to access and to disseminate content of their choice online.

in writing. ‒ i have voted for the report on trade in certain goods which could be used for capital punishment, torture or other treatment or punishment because i condemn the death penalty and torture wherever it occurs. with this vote i support vital technical updates that ensure tighter controls and a level playing field in europe, without creating excessive bureaucratic burdens or restrictions on legitimate medicine use. this regulation is one piece of the bigger legislative puzzle that should ensure europe is a strong global player that leads in terms of values such as respect for universal human rights.

in writing. - i voted for this motion on ebola. since march 2014, sierra leone, liberia and guinea have been the victims of the largest ebola epidemics ever recorded. the current ebola crisis has exposed structural weaknesses in several countries and at the same time reminded the european union's decision-makers of the need to stick to their commitment to allocate at least 20% of their public aid to the development of key social sectors, in particular health.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because it is a report by parliament that seeks to assess the ebola crisis and to draw long-term lessons and identify ways to strengthen health systems in developing countries to prevent future crises. in its report, parliament thus criticises the slow international response to the crisis in its first months, but notes the actions and commitments undertaken by the eu and its member states since march 2014 to help stop the spread of the ebola virus. parliament welcomed the development of a new vaccine in a record time, with 100% efficacy confirmed in the vaccination of persons in guinea since 23 march 2015, and called for the availability of this vaccine at an affordable price for all persons in liberia and sierra leone to be ensured as a matter of urgency. finally, parliament called on all parties concerned, in particular developing country governments, european institutions and international organisations, to draw lessons from the crisis, to take account of the negative impact of imf and world bank structural adjustment programmes on the health sector in developing countries and to develop effective measures to manage international health crises.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for the report on the ebola crisis: the long-term lessons and how to strengthen health systems in developing countries to prevent future crises. i believe that the european parliament, as always, has made it clear that its task here is to scrutinise the executive, to take on its role as legislator, and lastly to provide a political impetus. i strongly believe that we can insist that the eu should press ahead with its efforts, so that others can follow its example. the eu’s voice must be heard, particularly in this, the year of development.
in writing. the ebola virus outbreak is the largest and most complex in history. the ebola crisis exposed the inefficiencies of most health systems. it is worth noting that past adjustment and reforms and one-sided development policies have contributed to the inefficiency of health systems. it is therefore essential to learn from this crisis and develop effective tools for the management of international health crises and to better coordinate and strengthen health systems in the member states. in addition, the delayed response to this crisis, which was not decisive and did not reflect the scale of the crisis, needs to be self-critically assessed. i support the proposal to set up a permanent european rapid response team which could be relocated as soon as possible. in the future, we cannot afford to make mistakes in tackling such complex challenges, because the consequences are very painful. we must eradicate this disease completely.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it was parliament's response to the recent volkswagen scandal involving falsified car emissions tests. parliament called for a full investigation into the falsification of car emissions tests and for the perpetrators to be punished. the resolution proposes to reform the eu's vehicle emission control system, introduce real-world emissions testing and allow national authorities to revoke the authorisation to operate vehicles that exceed eu emission limits. parliament strongly condemned the fraudulent practices of car manufacturers which had been revealed and regretted the disappointment of millions of consumers and the continuing pollution and damage to human health. the parliament also fears that the scandal could undermine the competitiveness of the eu's entire automotive sector, which contributes to growth, innovation and job creation.

i regard the communication on the macroeconomic conditionality mechanism as important and well-designed, and the draftsman as constructive and responsive to all views. i would point out that the macroeconomic conditionality mechanism is a highly controversial instrument of eu economic governance. the principle that member states' economic mismanagement will be punished by reducing their ability to implement cohesion policy seems strange. this is all the more strange when we realise that the local and regional authorities who implement cohesion policy directly and are closest to each citizen will be the first to suffer as a result of the failures of national governments. we wanted to narrow the scope of the conditionality mechanism. if we cannot reject this mechanism, we must at least ensure that its application is as little detrimental as possible to the union's important objective of cohesion policy.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal on certain emissions into the atmosphere. air pollutants are a major transboundary human health and environmental problem that has a huge impact on all eu citizens and requires urgent action. poor air quality contributes to premature death, disability due to illness and high healthcare costs. in europe, the total external cost of air pollution to society in relation to health is estimated at between eur 330 and 940 billion per year. in addition, there is growing evidence that atmospheric nitrogen deposition changes the natural environment, such as eutrophication and acidification, leading to a decrease in the diversity of surface vegetation, a slowdown in plant growth and an imbalance in nutrition. efforts are being made across the union to reduce air pollution, but most member states are not meeting agreed standards. the commission proposal repeals and replaces the existing national emission limits (nel) directive by setting new limits for emissions of sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, ammonia and non-methane volatile organic compounds in 2020 and 2030.

blue-card answer.– thank you very much. what i stressed is that there have been a lot of achievements with the single market over the last 50 years. economic growth is not doing great – obviously we know that – and for that we need structural reforms and serious reforms for that to be achieved. i do not think we can have just a financial stimulus from the ecb. so if we all unite and carry out further reforms that are necessary, and member states carry out those reforms, growth rates would be significantly higher.
we will not overcome longterm unemployment unless we can offer the unemployed quality jobs. it is therefore essential to promote investment in quality jobs in the first place. secondly, it is really important to provide some incentives for employers to take long-term unemployed people into these quality jobs. we're not going to get rid of long-term unemployment unless we work patiently and consistently with each individual unemployed person, because these people have lost any motivation to work, they've lost any professional skills, and so they need to be invested in in a very special way. finally, we need to register these people so that we actually know how many there are so that we can work with them. and we need to encourage those same unemployed people to work, not live on welfare. so a lot of questions. the answers are in your hands and in your work.

in writing. ‒ the european police college (cepol) is the agency responsible for training law enforcement officers. cepol is not a traditional training institution, but its training takes place across the eu, mostly through a network of national police training colleges. in march 2013, the commission presented a proposal for a training scheme for law enforcement officers. this training system aims to identify and address the current gaps in the training of law enforcement officials in cross-border matters. it shall apply to all levels of law enforcement officials and shall be based on current training at national and eu level and delivered through modern training tools such as specialised courses, joint training programmes, online learning material and exchange programmes. i support the current proposal for a regulation to modernise cepol's legal framework, to make it compatible with the changes envisaged by the treaty of lisbon (including the role of the european parliament and national parliaments), and to empower it to implement the principles of the training system for judicial officers set out in the aforementioned commission communication.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to increase the transparency of securities financing transactions. the global financial crisis that erupted in 2007-2008 exposed excessive speculative activity, significant regulatory gaps, as well as weaknesses such as ineffective supervision, opaque markets and overly complex products in the financial system. the european union has taken a number of measures to make the banking system more resilient and stable, including stricter capital requirements, better governance rules and supervisory and resolution regimes. the progress made in creating the banking union is also very important. the crisis has also highlighted the need to increase transparency and to strengthen supervision not only in the traditional banking sector but also in the areas of non-bank lending activities, i.e. the shadow banking sector. the new transparency rules require the disclosure of data on the sfts of all market participants both financial and non-financial , including information on the structure of the underlying collateral, whether the underlying collateral may be or has been drawn, and the haircuts applied. in order to minimise the additional operating costs for market participants, the new rules and standards should build on the existing infrastructure and procedures in place in the field of otc derivatives.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it supports the commission's proposal for a regulation on the transparency of securities financing transactions. the global financial crisis has exposed excessive speculative activity, significant regulatory gaps, as well as shortcomings such as ineffective supervision, opaque markets and overly complex products in the financial system. the union has taken a number of measures to make the banking system more resilient and stable, including stronger capital requirements, better governance rules and supervisory and resolution regimes. parliament called for the financial sector to be able to focus on the real economy and not on speculation. in the course of their work on the fight against shadow banking, the financial stability board and the european systemic risk board identified risks posed by securities financing transactions (sfts). in particular, the lack of transparency in the use of the ssmef has prevented regulators and supervisors and investors from properly assessing and monitoring banking-like risks and interconnections in the financial system in the period before and during the financial crisis. therefore, the new transparency rules provided for in this regulation require the disclosure of data on the mmfs of all market participants both financial and non-financial entities , including information on the structure of the underlying collateral, where the underlying collateral can be or has been drawn, and the haircuts applied.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which aims to improve the integration of the long-term unemployed into the labour market. as a result of the economic crisis and its consequences, long-term unemployment has doubled since 2007 and now accounts for half of total unemployment, i.e. 12 million people, or 5% of the eu's active population, are long-term unemployed. this proposal encourages a more ambitious effort to register the long-term unemployed with the employment services in order to ensure full accounting; to assess the personal potential and needs of the long-term unemployed and the jobs they would prefer before 18 months of unemployment; and to offer a tailored, balanced and comprehensive reintegration contract between the long-term unemployed and the relevant services no later than 18 months of unemployment. i support calls for member states to coordinate eu funding for national policies to tackle long-term unemployment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution by the committee on employment and social affairs on the integration of the long-term unemployed into the labour market. i am pleased that the commission has finally presented the long-awaited council recommendation on long-term unemployed. of course, council recommendations may not be enough to bring about a rapid improvement in the situation of the long-term unemployed, and it is therefore necessary to encourage member states to achieve concrete results. it is important that any programmes for the reintegration of the long-term unemployed are adapted to the needs of the labour market and developed in close cooperation with the social partners. it is necessary to encourage member states to align eu funding for national policy measures to tackle long-term unemployment, in particular from the european social fund, with corresponding national funding. it is also necessary to encourage member states to motivate employers, including in the spirit of corporate social responsibility, to actively offer job vacancies to the long-term unemployed. cooperation between the commission and the member states and, at national level, between the (sectoral) social partners, civil society organisations representing the unemployed, local and regional authorities, public and private employment services, social and health care providers, local and regional education and training bodies, as well as active involvement of employers, is therefore crucial for the effective implementation of this recommendation, in order to better understand the requirements and needs of businesses.
in writing. the goal of economic policy in each country is full employment. to achieve this, europe should accelerate job creation, boost the economy and ensure social justice. however, the number of longterm unemployed in europe is currently only increasing. long-term unemployment is a particularly complex problem, as even when new jobs are created, it is often difficult for the long-term unemployed to successfully re-enter the labour market. it is therefore essential that these individuals are individually assessed and that a specific and tailored reintegration plan is drawn up. the involvement of the social partners in the preparation, planning and implementation of the council proposal is to be ensured at both eu and national level. employers should be encouraged to participate actively in developing partnerships with public authorities. they should also be offered targeted financial incentives. the financial and administrative capacity of public employment services also needs to be strengthened.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it was the report of parliament on the safe use of remotely piloted aircraft systems in civil aviation. these professional-use remotely piloted aircraft systems also offer many benefits in various areas of civil use, with additional benefits increasing with the distance between the aircraft and the remote control. the potential uses of these systems are very diverse and may be further developed in the future: they help, for example, to carry out security checks and to monitor infrastructure (railways, dams and energy installations), as well as to assess natural disasters, to carry out (environmentally responsible) precision farming activities, to develop media production, to perform aerodynamic thermography or to deliver consignments to remote regions. we can anticipate that new applications will be developed rapidly in the near future. the parliament therefore considers that the lack of harmonised regulation at union level may hamper the development of the european remotely piloted aircraft market, as national level authorisations are not generally recognised in other member states. welcomes therefore the fact that the commission's legislative proposal in this area is to be adopted by the end of 2015. new standards for the regulation of civil remotely piloted aircraft systems will be established covering safety, security, privacy, data protection, insurance and liability aspects. the commission is seeking to enable the eu industry to become the global business leader in this emerging technology.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report on the agreement between the european union and the australian tuna commission. the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) is a priority for the european union. iccat is responsible for the conservation of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and adjacent seas. this organisation was established by the plenipotentiary conference which drew up and adopted the international convention for the conservation of atlantic tunas, signed in rio de janeiro in 1966. following ratification of the convention, the commission for the conservation of australian tunas (ccsbt) officially came into being in 1969 as a regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) responsible for the management of the australian tuna stock in all waters. the convention for the conservation of australian tunas entered into force on 20 may 1994. since 2006, the european union has been a cooperating but independent entity of the enlarged commission of the ccsbt. the catches of bluefin tuna by the eu fleet in the bluefin tuna area consist mainly of small quantities of bluefin tuna caught as bait in the iotc convention area for bluefin tuna and related species. since 2006, the eu has applied an annual quota of 10 tonnes to the catch of bluefin tuna in ccsbt waters.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to update the rules on insurance intermediation in order to ensure greater protection for insurers, to prevent the provision of incorrect and misleading information and to harmonise the requirements for the provision of insurance services. the new rules stipulate that all insurers must be registered with the competent authorities of the eu countries in which they are resident and that insurance company staff must be appropriately trained. before signing the contract, policyholders will have to receive standard, unambiguous information on the identity of the agent selling the insurance, the type of insurance, the obligations of the purchaser, the risks covered, the premiums, the price of the contract, etc. to protect customers from the insolvency of insurance intermediaries, insurers will be obliged to ensure that 4% of annual premiums, but not less than eur 18 750, are always freely available.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report on the distribution of insurance products. insurance products may be distributed by various persons or institutions, such as agents, brokers and bank insurance operators, insurance companies, travel agents and car rental companies. the uniform approach to operator and customer protection requires that all those persons or institutions are covered by this directive. this directive aims at minimum harmonisation only and should therefore not prevent member states from maintaining or adopting more stringent provisions in order to protect consumers, provided that such provisions are compatible with european union law, including this directive. consumers must enjoy the same level of protection despite the different distribution channels. in order to ensure that consumers are afforded a uniform level of protection and that consumers benefit from comparable standards, in particular in the area of disclosure, it is important to create a level playing field for distributors.

in writing. - i voted for this report. child poverty is a multifaceted social problem and requires particular attention to address it. measures to monitor the implementation and impact of the different policies need to be identified and implemented in order to reduce and prevent child poverty and social exclusion and to promote child welfare. it is noteworthy that despite economic growth, the percentage of people living in poverty has not decreased. it is therefore necessary to address child poverty as soon as possible, which has long-term or irreversible consequences for the children themselves and for society. children raised in poverty are more likely to be poor themselves. it is therefore essential to ensure that children from poor families do not fall into the 'poverty trap'. they must be given the opportunity to move up the social ladder from poverty. children of all ages should receive free, inclusive and quality public education and training. we need to break the cycle of poverty, reduce social fragmentation and social tensions.
in writing. ‒ the i support the report by mr zuber for several reasons. all the available reports point to an intensification of child poverty in europe. between 2008 and 2012, europe saw an increase of almost one million children at risk of poverty or social exclusion. the percentage of children living in absolute and long-term poverty (more than 3 years) is dramatically increasing. social inequalities are passed on from generation to generation, and the negative effects of poverty and social exclusion can last for a lifetime for children, because cognitive and socioeconomic skills are developed during the first years of life, which means that today's unfavourable policy actions will have negative consequences for the lives of these people and for society as a whole. member states should therefore be encouraged to invest more in actions to combat child poverty. we should do so in the light of europe's christian roots.
in writing. child poverty is increasing alongside social inequalities. social inequalities translate social disadvantages from generation to generation and the negative impact of poverty and social exclusion on children can last for a lifetime, as children develop their cognitive and economic and social skills early in life, which means that negative policy measures taken today will have irreversible negative impacts on their lives and on society. poverty is multifaceted and must be understood not only as the inability to meet a child's basic needs, such as food, clothing and housing, but also as the lack of access to education and quality health care and the inability to participate in sports, culture and other leisure activities.
