in writing. i support the position of the european parliament on the commission's proposal for a strategic programme for the eu's safety and health at work for 2014-2020. all workers, regardless of the size of their employer, the member state of employment or the nature of the contract of employment under which they are employed, have the right to the highest level of protection of health and safety at work. as the commission underlines in the eu strategic programme on safety and health at work, effective management of safety and health at work remains a challenge for micro and small enterprises. we therefore need to take action to promote compliance and effective management of occupational safety and health in these establishments. at national level, labour inspectorates play an important role in ensuring the effective application of occupational safety and health legislation. companies can benefit from the assistance and information provided by labour inspectorates on preventive measures and legal requirements, and it is therefore necessary to allocate more staff and resources to labour inspectorates to enable them to fulfil their duties. successful risk prevention in the workplace requires social dialogue, employee representation and commitment from managers. we can also do more at member state and eu level to train and encourage health and safety representatives to take action.
in writing. more than 4000 people die each year from accidents at work, and the number of deaths from occupational diseases exceeds 15 000 per year. the right to good health is a fundamental right in europe, but despite improvements in occupational safety and health, the most serious threats to workers' health and safety have still not been addressed. the european labour market is changing. there has been a rise in the popularity of precarious employment and new forms of employment, like new technologies, have brought new health and safety challenges to be addressed. recall that job insecurity is one of the major problems, especially in the new member states of the european union, and this has a negative impact on occupational safety and related rules. the european commission needs to take account of the increasing number of workers with chronic and long-term illnesses and disabilities in order to ensure that they have an accessible and safe workplace. measures for the integration and rehabilitation of disabled people should also be encouraged. for these reasons, the european parliament should take more initiative on this important issue. all workers, regardless of their employer, the country in which they work or the type of contract under which they are employed, have the right to the highest level of health and safety at work.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which examines the possibility of mobilising the european union solidarity fund to pay advances. the european union solidarity fund (essf) aims to enable the european union to respond to emergencies caused by major natural disasters and to express european solidarity with the regions of europe affected by disasters. the fund may provide financial assistance to member states and countries negotiating eu membership in the event of a major natural disaster, i.e. where the total direct damage caused by that disaster exceeds eur 3 billion. it may also be mobilised in the event of a regional disaster. it should be noted that the advance may be paid at the request of a member state and after a preliminary assessment by the commission of the relevant essf application. the amount of the advance should not exceed 10% of the amount of the financial support provided and should not exceed eur 30 million. the advance shall be paid without prejudice to the final decision on the mobilisation of the essf and the european commission shall recover the amounts of the advance wrongly paid to the member states. the european parliament recalls that the essf is not just another source of eu financial support, but also helps to send a clear political signal of solidarity and to provide much-needed assistance to the citizens affected. the rapid response capabilities, including the advance payment, will therefore help the european union to achieve these objectives.

in writing. the european union solidarity fund (essf) aims to enable the union to respond to emergencies caused by major natural disasters and to express european solidarity with the regions of europe affected by disasters. the fund may provide financial assistance to member states and countries negotiating union membership in the event of a major natural disaster, i.e. where the total direct damage caused by that disaster exceeds eur 3 billion in 2011 prices or 0,6% of the country's gross national income, whichever is the lower. it may also be mobilised in the event of a regional disaster.

in writing. ‒ i have voted for the objection pursuant to rule 106: granting an authorisation for uses of bis(2-ethylhexhyl)phthalate (dehp). ehp should be identified as a substance of very high concern because it meets the criteria set out in article 57(f) of the reach regulation in that it is a substance with endocrine disrupting properties for which there is scientific evidence of probable serious effects on human health, which give rise to a level of concern equivalent to that for other substances listed in points of the reach regulation.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report. i believe that the commission should not authorise the use of bis (2-ethylhexyl) phthalate by business operators. it should be noted that this chemical is dangerous and has been linked to infertility, cancer, and adverse effects on the brain. in addition, there is scientific evidence of adverse effects on endocrine function and of a causal relationship between these effects and adverse effects on human health. it should be noted that the granting of an authorisation would create a very unfavourable precedent for future decisions on authorisation under reach. therefore, the use of this substance should be withdrawn as a matter of urgency from all remaining applications in order to ensure adequate protection of humans and to eliminate adverse effects on human health.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which contains decisions on taxes and other measures of a similar nature or effect. luxleaks brought these problems to the attention of the public and the media by exposing the questionable tax practices promoted by accountancy firms in one particular member state. the commission's investigations and the work of the european parliament, with the participation of its special committee, have shown that this was not an isolated case but a widespread practice in europe and beyond, where tax measures are taken to reduce the overall tax liability of certain large corporations in order to artificially increase the national tax base at the expense of other countries (some of which are subject to austerity measures). such practices, which often result in a disconnect between the place where value is created and the place where profits are taxed, go beyond pre-tax rulings and include a wide range of harmful tax practices by national tax administrators inside and outside the eu. the european parliament therefore calls on the commission to use all available means to promote a more coordinated approach towards developed countries in order to promote greater respect for the principle of reciprocity in tax matters, in particular in the exchange of information with the united states of america, following the entry into force of the foreign account tax compliance act.

in writing. ‒ i voted for the report on the eu strategic framework on health and safety at work 2014-2020 because a large number of workers die due to accidents at work and the number of fatal work-related diseases amounts to more than 150 000 every single year! that must stop. good health is a fundamental right in europe and even though considerable progress has been made in the area of occupational health and safety throughout the years, major risks to workers’ health and safety continue to exist. the economic costs of work-related injuries and illnesses are significant and the highly challenging nature of many new and emerging risks calls for immediate measures to be taken at eu level.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament considers the eu osh programme to be essential to ensure uniformly high standards and to improve working conditions across the eu. it should be noted that, according to statistics, cancers and chronic diseases, rather than accidents at work, account for the largest share of work-related deaths in the european union. member states should therefore pay greater attention to prevention in this particular area. attention must be paid not only to the physical but also to the mental health of workers, as work-related stress and strain also have a significant impact on work performance and the well-being of workers and their families and can have long-term consequences. it is also necessary to ensure the integration of people with disabilities into the labour market, providing safe working conditions and taking their needs into account.
in writing. ‒ the i agree with the report. safe and healthy working conditions must be provided for every worker. the health and productivity of citizens are the foundation for the economic and social well-being of any country. the issue of human safety at work is of particular relevance and therefore, in order to introduce a higher level of protection for workers, it is necessary to establish clear and effective rules in the field of occupational safety and health. we need to reduce legal regulation without reducing the level of occupational safety and health. particular attention should be paid to the safety and health of workers in small and medium-sized enterprises. the strategy must strike a balance between a high level of protection and the administrative burden on businesses. employee education, training, collective bargaining and agreements with the social partners are important tools for improving the safety and health situation of workers. in setting appropriate measures, the importance of bullying and the fight against harassment and violence at work must be given high priority. in order to implement the prevention of work-related diseases and of new and emerging risks, member states should make more effective use of the european funds.

in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution on the current state of the doha development agenda in the run-up to the 10th wto ministerial conference. the doha negotiations were launched in 2001 with the aim of creating new trade opportunities, strengthening multilateral trade rules and correcting existing imbalances in the trading system by focusing on the needs of developing and least developed countries. i support the wto structural reform needed to better ensure a non-discriminatory trading system. trade liberalisation is an important tool for sustainable economic growth and development, but trade liberalisation also requires the implementation of appropriate accompanying policies, including budgetary transparency, fiscal policy, administrative simplification, education and training, institutional reforms and social policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the current state of the doha development agenda in the run-up to the 10th ministerial conference of the world trade organisation (wto). the european parliament supports the wto structural reform needed to better ensure a rules-based, open, fair and non-discriminatory trading system that takes greater account of the roles and interests of the various economic operators, such as small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), micro-enterprises and innovative start-ups. parliament called on wto members to actively support the efforts of the wto by establishing effective and efficient working relationships and ensuring closer cooperation with other international organisations whose activities are related to global trade negotiations, in particular the international labour organisation, the world health organisation and the united nations and its agencies. parliament also considered it essential to conclude the long-drawn-out doha round of negotiations in the implementation of the development mandate. calls therefore on all wto members to consider all options to achieve a large-scale, universal, sustainable and realistic outcome with this ultimate objective in mind.
in writing. ‒ the i agree with the report. greater efforts are needed to bring the doha round to a swift conclusion and ambitious results. it is clear that the long delay in these negotiations will create major problems. in particular, rules for international trade that are acceptable to all parties should be established to justify the desire of the parties to act more fairly and openly. more consideration should be given to the very different economic development and individual needs of developing countries. more advanced developing countries should assume some responsibility already in the current round and contribute according to their level of development. in addition, structural reforms should be undertaken in the wto to better ensure an open, fair and non-discriminatory trading system based on commonly applicable rules. we need to create opportunities not just to help the weak economies of the world, but to help the strong economies to grow. it is therefore essential that all wto members ratify and implement the trade facilitation agreement as soon as possible.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement between the european union and liechtenstein. it is a great preventive measure to stop the evasive spread of tax fraud and tax evasion. exchange of information relating to income in such forms as interests and dividends will help to better administrate tax matters in cross-border related situations, avoid tax evasion and help to reduce the administrative burden by avoiding unnecessary investigations.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal for the approval of an agreement on the exchange of automatic financial account information for tax purposes with liechtenstein. the eu and liechtenstein signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information in october 2015 to improve international cooperation and compliance in the field of taxation. this is a major contribution to the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. from 2017, the eu and liechtenstein will automatically exchange information on the financial accounts of their residents in response to attempts by taxpayers to conceal capital consisting of income or assets for which no tax has been paid. i agree that the tax authorities in the member states and liechtenstein should correctly and clearly identify the taxpayers concerned, administer and enforce their tax laws in cross-border cases, assess the possibility of tax evasion and avoid unnecessary further investigations.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report on the taxation of interest income from savings between the european union (eu) and liechtenstein. the eu and liechtenstein signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information on 28 october 2015 with a view to enhancing international cooperation and compliance in the field of taxation. the agreement is an important step in the ongoing fight against tax fraud and tax evasion, and it amends the 2004 agreement which ensured that liechtenstein applied measures equivalent to those of the eu savings directive on taxation of income. under this agreement, the eu and liechtenstein will exchange information on financial accounts held by their residents automatically from 2017. the aim is to respond to cases where a taxpayer attempts to conceal capital consisting of income or assets for which taxes have not been paid. the agreement aims to ensure that liechtenstein applies more stringent measures that are equivalent to the eu directive as revised in march 2014 and that it complies with the provisions on automatic exchange of financial account information promoted by the implementation of the 2014 oecd global standards. the eu-liechtenstein agreement should enter into force on 1 january 2016.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the report on the eu-liechtenstein agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information. the european union and liechtenstein signed an agreement on 28 october 2015 on the automatic exchange of financial account information, aimed at improving international tax cooperation and compliance. it is a very important step in ongoing efforts to clamp down on tax fraud and tax evasion and upgrades the 2004 agreement that ensured that liechtenstein applied measures equivalent to those in an eu directive on the taxation of savings income. under the agreement, the eu and liechtenstein will automatically exchange information on the financial accounts of each other’s residents, starting in 2017. the aim is to address situations where a taxpayer seeks to hide capital representing income or assets for which taxes have not been paid.
in writing. ‒ the i agree with the report. this eu-liechtenstein agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information in tax matters is a major step forward in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. it is essential to ensure that liechtenstein applies measures equivalent to those of the eu. it should be noted that the automatic exchange of information is a crucial tool to ensure full tax transparency and cooperation between tax administrations on a global scale. therefore, a harmonised, consistent and comprehensive approach to the automatic exchange of financial account information in the internal market should be applied throughout the european union. in addition, automatic exchanges of information should be promoted to become the european and international standard for the exchange of information in the field of transparency and taxation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to assess the special report of the european ombudsman's own-initiative inquiry into frontex. frontex is working to strengthen respect for fundamental rights through measures such as the establishment of a system for reporting unforeseen events, the development of codes of conduct, the establishment of a consultative forum on fundamental rights and the establishment of a fundamental rights office. i agree that, in view of the continuously growing humanitarian and legal challenges at the eu's external borders and the strengthening of frontex operations, a mechanism is needed to deal with individual complaints about alleged fundamental rights violations in frontex operations.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, in which the european parliament welcomes the special report of the european ombudsman's own-initiative inquiry into frontex. parliament acknowledges the ongoing efforts of frontex to strengthen respect for fundamental rights through measures such as, but not limited to, the establishment of a system of notifications of contingencies, the development of codes of conduct, the establishment of a consultative forum on fundamental rights and the establishment of a fundamental rights office. however, on the other hand, the european parliament expresses its serious concern about the legal vacuum regarding third-country posted officials in return operations, as indicated in the european ombudsman's report, as well as the lack of accountability that would be encountered in the event of human rights violations by third-country posted officials. parliament therefore considers that the introduction of an individual complaints mechanism would enable individuals to exercise their right to an effective legal remedy in the event of a breach of their fundamental rights. moreover, the establishment of such a complaints mechanism would ensure greater transparency and respect for human rights, including in the application of frontex working arrangements, by better informing frontex and the eu institutions of potential fundamental rights violations that might otherwise go unnoticed, unreported and unaddressed.
in writing. ‒ my vote on the special report of the european ombudsman in the own-initiative inquiry concerning frontex was decided by the fact that, in view of the ever-growing humanitarian and legal challenges at the eu’s external borders and the strengthening of frontex operations, there is a need for a mechanism that is capable of processing individual complaints about alleged breaches of fundamental rights occurring in the course of frontex operations or cooperation with third countries, thus becoming a first-instance body for complaints.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report. in view of the activities carried out by frontex and its growing role under eu law, as well as the recommendations made by the ombudsman, i believe it appropriate to establish a mechanism for handling individual complaints within this agency. the agency would become the first-instance complaints body. it should be noted that the rights of the individual must be not only formally but also in reality and effectively protected against unlawful acts by private persons and officials alike. it is therefore essential to ensure that the new mechanism ensures the proper handling of complaints concerning possible infringements of fundamental rights in the context of frontex operations. in addition, the complaints mechanism must be in line with eu law and the principle of good administration would also help to implement the agency's fundamental rights strategy more effectively. this would enable victims to exercise properly their right to an effective, cost-effective and expeditious remedy for their infringed rights.
in writing. ‒ rapporteur ska keller takes up a very important issue, which seeks to reconcile two of the most important issues facing europeans today: ensuring the security of citizens while respecting human rights. frontex is bound by the charter of fundamental rights, like any other institution or agency of the european union. in view of the increasing number of humanitarian and legal challenges at the external borders of the eu, it is necessary to establish a mechanism to allow for the analysis of individual complaints concerning suspected violations of fundamental rights that may arise from the activities of frontex or from cooperation with third countries. in democratic countries such legal instruments must be guaranteed, and i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to reorient urban mobility towards sustainable modes of transport in order to meet the challenges of our age: climate, health and the environment, well-being and safety for all. it is projected that by 2050, almost 82% of all eu citizens will live in urban areas. about 50% of eu citizens use their cars on a daily basis, only 16% use public transport and only 12% use bicycles. eu citizens consider lower public transport prices (59%), better quality of public transport services (56%) and better infrastructure for cyclists (33%) to be the most effective measures to improve urban mobility. i agree that the main priorities for improving urban mobility should be: return of space and infrastructure to all citizens and improvement of accessibility, improvement of the environment, quality of life and health, energy saving and climate protection, innovation, more sustainable and safer urban mobility, reduction of external costs and ensuring higher quality investments, etc.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report, which deals with urban traffic, i.e. traffic congestion, traffic regulation, human safety on the streets and roads, environmental and health impacts, etc. mobility is not an end in itself, but it should become a right for all citizens. with 80% of europeans living in cities, mobility should enable everyone, including people with reduced mobility, to study, work, participate in cultural activities, have free time and access to healthcare. however, urban mobility is often seen as a constraint, due to the excessive use of private cars powered by traditional fuels. the transition to more sustainable modes of transport is therefore very slow: the car remains our main means of mobility, accounting for 43% of the world's kilometres and three quarters of european journeys. the car addiction and its consequences congestion on the roads, which costs €80 billion in all european cities make urban dwellers prisoners of compulsory mobility (which they cannot choose). the aim of this report is therefore to reorient urban mobility towards sustainable modes of transport in order to meet the challenges of our age: climate, health and the environment, well-being and safety for all. current and future urban mobility must be based on ecological mobility and cooperation networks. new urban driving practices such as car sharing are developing and it is essential that such practices are integrated into the multiple mobility chain alongside cycling, walking and public transport.
in writing. ‒ my vote was decided by the fact that mobility can provide a vital boost for our economy and if we are to deliver economic growth. with this in mind, we want to promote inter-modality and co-modality in a way that can deliver more sustainable and efficient urban transport modes. we should also encourage cooperation, sharing of best practices and integration of innovation and digitalisation into forthcoming mobility planning.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report. transportation is our mobility. urban mobility plays an important role in shaping transport policy. the changing urban transport system must ensure the mobility needs of each citizen and the accessibility of urban areas within the shortest distance and the shortest time, while protecting the environment and improving the quality of life. the development of sustainable and environmentally friendly urban transport strategies and sustainable mobility plans should therefore be encouraged. it should be noted that the development of sustainable mobility plans is an important element of the financing of eu projects in the field of urban transport. it is essential that the esi funds are systematically used to develop and implement comprehensive and integrated plans for sustainable urban mobility. urban mobility should contribute to the eu's resource efficiency goals, reducing air pollution, noise, greenhouse gas emissions and energy consumption. however, i do not believe that the high consumption of diesel in the european union has been driven by favourable taxation rules and i do not support the proposal calling for immediate action to phase out fossil fuel subsidies.
in writing. ‒ 80% of europeans will live in cities, so mobility should promote access for all, including people with reduced mobility, to schools, work, culture and health facilities. in the meantime, urban mobility is often mistakenly perceived as an inconvenience. the report aims to shift urban mobility towards more sustainable vehicles in order to meet the challenges of our age, such as health and environmental protection or safety. to achieve this, the european union needs to set itself ambitious targets so that the member states, regions and local authorities can work together to implement this new model of sustainable urban mobility. it is therefore worth supporting this report.
in writing. it is symbolic that today, as we are discussing a resolution on european electricity interconnections with our colleagues in the european parliament in strasbourg, the long-awaited electricity interconnections with sweden (nordbalt) and poland (litpol link) are officially being inaugurated in lithuania. thanks to the persistence of the baltic states and the support of the european union, one of the most isolated energy islands has disappeared today. the baltic states have become full-fledged european market participants thanks to the electricity bridges built. this is good news for the low-cost electricity consumers. this is also good news for local energy producers, as the interconnectors will allow electricity to be exported. it is also good news for all those who care about our environment, as connectivity is a prerequisite for the development of renewable sources. so, in short, it's a good day for all of us who want an independent, secure, third-party-free energy system. true, the baltic states remain in a sense dependent on russia, since the electricity transmission system itself is still controlled from moscow. i would therefore like to congratulate my colleague, peter eriksson, who in his report on electricity interconnections also draws attention to the so-called problem of synchronisation of the baltic electricity systems. it is not normal that transmission systems in even three eu member states operate in a different political and economic space. i hope that the european parliament, by voting in favour of this resolution, will express its full support for the synchronisation of the baltic transmission system with the continental european networks.
in writing. with the agreement reached at the climate change conference, the creation of a european energy union is even more urgent. the european energy union needs to be effective and able to respond and adapt to new challenges in the global energy and geopolitical context. the communication is a compromise text and therefore cannot be ideally balanced. however, i believe that the objectives and measures of the energy union are clearly set out in it. adequate attention shall be paid to internal aspects of the energy union, such as the establishment of the internal market, security of supply, infrastructure, energy efficiency or the reduction of greenhouse gases. but the secondary plan should not be to consolidate a genuine european energy foreign policy. the recent vision of a european energy union is, i believe, still lacking, as we can see from the decision on the nordstream 2 pipeline. solidarity is often expressed in words rather than in deeds. i am convinced that the success of the energy union will depend not on the lofty goals we set but on how we achieve them. i therefore believe that increased supervision and control by the commission is necessary. i would urge my colleagues to concentrate on those areas of energy policy where consensus is possible. the commission presented the first annual report on the energy union last month and i hope that parliament will be able to formulate its position in time.
the european commission's decision to authorise a new genetically modified maize variety is another example of arrogance. i would point out that the maize variety in question is a hybrid of the previously authorised variety 603 , which is infamous for the research carried out by the french scientist seralini. he found that this gmo caused multiple illnesses and tumours in laboratory mice. an attempt was made to refute the conclusions of this study. the european food safety authority has joined the wave of criticism. but in two trials in paris, on november 6 and 26, the scientist defended his honor. the european commission should therefore take the potential risks to human and animal health posed by these gmos more seriously. i support this resolution of the european parliament and i call on the commission to finally start working with parliament and not against it.
in writing.– the completion of the economic and monetary union should be of the highest priority in order to unleash the full potential of the single currency and structures and economic instruments at our command. the euro has already become a currency recognised and used worldwide. however, we still need to aim not only for a better representation of the euro in relation to monetary and banking union but also to reinforce the governance of the eurozone – for this a genuine dialogue between the member states and the european parliament is the key.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this report because it gives parliament its support for the conclusion of an agreement between the european union and the dominican republic on the short-stay visa waiver. this agreement on the short-stay visa waiver is the result of the development of relations between the european union and the commonwealth of dominica, further confirming the important political importance of the cotonou agreement, and is a complementary instrument to strengthen economic and cultural links and to promote political dialogue on a wide range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. this agreement establishes a visa-free regime for citizens of the european union and the commonwealth of dominica who intend to enter the territory of the other contracting party and stay there for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa-free regime applies to all categories of persons (civilians, diplomats, officials and/or officials and holders of special passports) travelling abroad for any purpose other than gainful employment.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to amend regulation no 609/2014 by including a number of questions and clarifications of a more technical nature. i support the proposals set out to provide for effective rules on how member states should make timely contributions to the union budget. it should be noted that the commission has the possibility of requesting the member states to pay the third twelfth of the vat and gni-based resources during the first half of the year, in order to enable the commission to reduce the higher share of late payments in previous years. it is important not only to provide for more incentives for late payment by providing for higher payments for late payments, but also to ensure proportionality by providing that the increase in the interest rate cannot exceed the limit of 20 percentage points. i support calls on the commission to examine the recommendations on the accounting methods for national contributions to the union budget, which vary widely, in order to facilitate comparisons between member states. i agree that the own resources system remains too complex and needs to be fundamentally restructured under the next multiannual financial framework.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it gives parliament its approval, with minor amendments, of the council regulation on the methods and modalities of the provision of own resources based on vat and gni and on the arrangements for meeting cash requirements. in its communication, parliament notes that, in general, member states have paid all their vat and gni-based contributions to the union budget without undue delay, even in times of crisis and very high fiscal constraints. however, in order to meet the cash needs, the provisioning and adjustment of member states' contributions to the union budget should not be subject to political negotiation but should be a technical process. in that report, parliament also asked it to submit annually a report on the calculation and supporting data of vat and gni adjustments to the balance sheet, as well as the dates and amounts of the contributions of the member states to the union budget, in order to ensure maximum transparency.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the option granted to the commission to ask member states for the payment of 3/12th of vat and gni resources in the first half of the year, in order to allow the commission to reduce a more important part of the previous year’s payment backlog in the european agriculture guarantee fund and in the european structural and investment funds, and to reduce default interest.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report. in particular, it is essential to allow member states, under certain conditions, to defer payments and to transfer the adjusted amounts of vat resources and additional resources in instalments. in this context, it is necessary to lay down rules governing the timely presentation by member states of their contributions to the union budget in order to enable the commission to manage its treasury effectively. the objective of each state is to ensure macroeconomic stability and economic development in the country. in order to help national treasuries to manage the financing of possible adjustments more efficiently, the deadline for the transmission of data should be postponed and the date for the submission of amounts should be adjusted. this would facilitate the conduct of effective public finance policies by member states and ensure their economic and financial stability.

in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to mobilise the egf to help finland to support the reintegration of workers made redundant in 69 companies active in the field of computer programming. the egf is intended to provide a total amount of eur 2 623 200. this will support 1 200 of the 1 603 redundant workers. the redundancies were due to changes affecting nokia in recent years, which had a significant impact on the finnish ict sector. thousands of finnish residents have been employed in nokia's development and design of mobile phone operating systems, particularly in the oulu region, and these functions are currently being transferred to countries outside europe. the tailor-made services to be provided to redundant workers include counselling, employment and business services, training, wage subsidies, etc.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to reform the system of trade mark registration. the reorganisation would make this registration cheaper, faster and more predictable. the new rules, agreed with the eu council in april this year, will also give the authorities the power to seize counterfeits that are being transported across the eu. the updated rules maintain the possibility of registering a trade mark either in a specific eu country or across the union and offer simpler registration and the possibility of registering new trade marks, such as sound. at the same time, the fees for renewal of the trade mark registration are reduced.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because it gives parliament its support for a partial amendment to eu law on the eu trade mark. in 2009, a council regulation established a specific system of trade mark protection in the european union, providing for trade mark protection at the level of the european union in parallel to the protection of trade marks under national trade mark systems at the level of the member states. the experience gained since the establishment of the community trade mark system has shown that the system has been adopted by undertakings in the union and in third countries and has become a successful and viable alternative and complementary system to the protection of trade marks at member state level. however, national trade marks remain necessary for those undertakings which do not wish to protect their trade marks at union level or which cannot obtain union-wide protection but can obtain national protection without obstacles.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal, which asks the commission to withdraw its draft implementing regulation and to submit to the committee a new draft listing invasive alien species of union concern. the first commission proposal omits many of the most problematic invasive alien species, while it includes some species that are unlikely to have a significant negative impact on biodiversity, ecosystem functions, human health or the economy, or for which the measures to be applied would incur disproportionate costs. since the reasons for including species in the union list are based on political rather than scientific criteria, i agree with the need to submit a new draft regulation.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution because it was the parliament's decision to ask the commission to withdraw its draft implementing regulation containing the list of invasive alien species of union concern and to submit a new draft to parliament. species not included in the initial list submitted by the commission are among the most harmful invasive alien species in europe. however, some land plant and mammal species fulfil the criteria and are subject to a detailed risk assessment, but these species are not included in the union list. the list also excludes mammalian species which are mentioned among the most widespread alien species in europe in recent years and, since the list also excludes widespread and rapidly spreading plant species with significant and well-documented adverse effects on human health. the initial list of the commission has been criticised by several competent national authorities, stakeholders and the general public to such an extent that these stakeholders now have serious doubts about the effectiveness of the future isr regulation, mainly due to the fact that many of the most problematic invasive alien species are not included in that list, while some species are included that are unlikely to have a significant negative impact on biodiversity, ecosystem functions, human health or the economy, or for which the measures to be applied would incur disproportionate costs.
in writing. ‒ my vote was decided by the fact that the regulation is based on an eu list of invasive species of european concern. it is important that this list is comprehensive and based on solid science and risk assessments, as the law requires. the first list which is now being adopted by the commission should not be blocked, but it should be kept under review and be complemented and improved in the coming years.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because in it parliament decided not to approve the commission's draft implementing decision authorising the placing on the market of products containing genetically modified maize nk603 × t25 and asked for a new draft decision to be submitted to parliament. on 17 may 2010, the company 'monsanto europe s.a.' submitted to the competent authority of the netherlands an application, in accordance with articles 5 and 17 of regulation (ec) no 1829/2003, for the placing on the market of foods, food ingredients, and feed containing, consisting of, or produced from nk603 × t25 maize. the application refers to the presence of glyphosate-containing proteins in genetically modified maize and the international agency for research on cancer the world health organisation's specialized agency for cancer classified glyphosate as a substance with probable human carcinogenicity on 20 march 2015.
in writing. ‒ the gm maize nk603 × t25 is a crop made tolerant to both glyphosate and glufosinate-ammonium-based herbicides. it was produced through the crossing of two previously authorised gm maize varieties and developed by monsanto europe s.a. the commission’s draft implementing act approves the placing on the market of food, food ingredients and feed containing, consisting of, or produced from this maize while the cultivation remains prohibited in the eu. that is why i have voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the objection to the authorisation of genetically modified maize. this is important for european agriculture and for the safety of the food that reaches consumers. as indicated in the notification, the genetically modified maize contains a protein which confers resistance to the herbicide glyphosate and to the ammonium glyphosate, which has been classified by the international agency for research on cancer as carcinogenic to humans. therefore, an objection on this issue is necessary and any decision should be suspended until a new regulation is adopted.

on behalf of the alde group.– mr president, 2014 was certainly not a good year when it comes to human rights and democracy in the world. 26 pages of the european parliament’s annual report, i believe, is a sad manifestation of this. to me, this only proves two main things. first of all, it is for us, the european union and its member states, to make sure that we will remain an example to be followed. 2014, and now even more so 2015, proved the opposite. the tendencies are rather worrisome. secondly, it is time to come back to the very basics. it is a primary responsibility of the european union to find the ways and means of how to be more effective in dealing with freedom of expression, freedom of thought, conscience and religion and freedom of assembly and association. if it continues like this we may end up with a 2015 report containing 70 pages, i am afraid.
the protection of human rights is often referred to as a priority for the european union. but i do encourage everyone to be honest with themselves and with each other. we often sacrifice human rights for geopolitical reasons. a good example is the human rights situation in belarus and turkey. today, relations with belarus are warming up, but have there been any significant changes in the country's human rights record? no, it didn't. the same is true of turkey. there is also no freedom of speech, the media is persecuted by a regime that is not comfortable with it, but turkey has become an important partner because of the refugee crisis. it's strange to me that you're constantly being asked to choose between sacrificing the economy and security or human rights. i call on the commission and parliament to stop playing games and to continue to fight human rights violations by negotiating cooperation with other countries.
the commission's reply was full of talk about the need to protect the biotechnology industry, but i think that protecting farmers' rights should be one of our priorities. we know that most farmers do their own selection. we cannot allow small farmers to be destroyed by having to pay for even the varieties produced by conventional breeding. ladies and gentlemen, today i want to ask the question: who should we protect: the big corporations or farmers and consumers? if you are a farmer, then i urge you to support the green amendments, especially by protecting farmers from being sued for accidentally polluting their varieties with patented plant pollen.

in writing. ‒ i have voted for the annual report on human rights and democracy in the world 2014 and the eu policy on the matter because the european parliament expresses deep concern that human rights and democratic values, such as freedom of expression, freedom of thought, conscience and religion, and freedom of assembly and association, are increasingly under threat in many parts of the world, including under authoritarian regimes. the european parliament calls for the eu and its member states to enhance their efforts to effectively regard human rights and democratic values.
in writing. ‒ the dayton peace agreement was signed in paris on 14 december 1995, ending the bosnian war. the dayton peace agreement is not perfect, but it remains the basis for the territorial integrity, sovereignty and political independence of bosnia and herzegovina. progress has been made in the country and the region over the past two decades, but more needs to be done to develop and strengthen democracy. it is important to highlight the positive changes that have taken place in bosnia and herzegovina over the last 20 years: from a war-torn country recovering from the war, it has become a country aspiring to join the european union. i support calls for the authorities to use the 20th anniversary of the dayton peace agreement as an incentive to implement the necessary reforms. meeting the social and economic needs of citizens, as well as the creation of an effective mechanism for coordinating eu issues, must be a priority. it is also important to continue political reforms and the democratisation of the political system.
in writing. ‒ the i voted for this resolution because it marks the 20th anniversary of the dayton peace agreement. on 14 december 1995, the dayton peace agreement was signed in paris, ending the bloodiest war in europe since the end of the second world war - the bosnian war. in its resolution, parliament recalled the importance of the signing of the dayton peace agreement, recalled all the tragic victims of the war in bosnia and herzegovina and expressed its sincere condolences to the families of those who had lost their lives. however, parliament regretted that after the end of the war and 20 years after the conclusion of the general framework agreement, which defined the main aspects of the peace agreement and the future character of the country, the governments that subsequently ruled the country had failed to create a fully functioning and viable state. parliament called on the authorities to use the 20th anniversary of the dayton peace agreement as an incentive to carry out the necessary reforms, particularly in relation to bosnia and herzegovina's future application for eu membership.
in writing. ‒ i agreed to the resolution on the 20th anniversary of the dayton peace agreement because the european parliament reminds local political leaders that reforms focusing on inefficient, ineffective or inconsistent laws and institutions are needed; highlights the need for measures to protect political, civil and human rights, calls for the rule of law to be restored, and encourages leaders in bosnia and herzegovina to make significant efforts to implement the political system envisaged in the dayton constitution.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because it is the one that parliament has used to speak out against arms exports to the eu. in its report, parliament noted that the global security environment in the eu's neighbourhood had changed substantially, particularly in the eu's southern and eastern neighbourhood. in its report, parliament noted that the uncontrolled proliferation of weapons poses a serious threat to peace and security, human rights and sustainable development, with one person killed every minute somewhere in the world as a result of armed violence and 15 new weapons being produced. parliament expressed its deep concern at the spread of violent conflicts, in particular in ukraine, syria, iraq, libya and yemen, and of all international conflicts, which in an increasingly globalised world threaten global stability and security and have led to a less stable and secure eu neighbourhood, and noted that arms transfers to states in conflict have contributed to these conflicts. parliament regretted the frequent disregard for the common position's provisions on arms exports, in particular the fact that european defence companies are increasingly compensating for their reduced turnover in europe by exporting outside the eu, and the serious concern about the consequences for the security and defence of the eu of the transfer of confidential information and classified technology to third countries, which shows a greater risk of dependence on third countries with different strategic interests.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for the report on arms export: implementation of the common position 2008/944/cfsp because the european parliament expressed concern about the spread of armed conflicts, notably those in ukraine, syria, iraq, libya and yemen as well as all international conflicts, which, in an increasingly globalised world, are a threat to world stability and security and have determined a less stable and less secure neighbourhood for the eu. the european parliament also stresses that arms export controls are an integral part of eu foreign and security policy and must be guided by the principles enshrined in article 21 teu, notably the promotion of democracy and the rule of law and the preservation of peace, prevention of conflicts and strengthening of international security.
in writing. ‒ access to biological material is essential to stimulate innovation and the production of new varieties, to ensure global food security and to combat climate change. intellectual property rights are important to maintain economic incentives for the export of new plant products and to ensure competitiveness. following the decision of the enlarged board of appeal of the european patent office in cases g2/12 (tomatoes) and g2/13 (broccoli), the epo may start issuing more patents relating to the natural characteristics of new varieties resulting from essentially biological processes such as crossing or selection. i support the calls on the commission to clarify the scope of directive 98/44/ec, in particular articles 4, 12 (3) (b) and 13 (3) (b) thereof, and how to interpret those provisions in order to ensure legal clarity on the prohibition of patenting products derived from essentially biological processes.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution because it is a resolution that parliament is advocating for the protection of patents and breeders' rights. access to biological material, including plant traits, is essential to stimulate innovation and the production of new varieties, to ensure global food security, to combat climate change and to prevent monopolies in the plant breeding sector, while creating more opportunities for smes. intellectual property rights are important to maintain economic incentives for the export of new plant products and to ensure competitiveness.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for the resolution on patents and plant breeders’ rights because with it the ep calls on the commission to clarify the scope and interpretation of directive 98/44/ec, in particular article 4 along with articles 12(3)(b) and 13(3)(b) thereof, in order to ensure legal clarity regarding the prohibition of the patentability of products obtained from essentially biological processes and the fact that breeding with biological material falling within the scope of a patent is permitted.
in writing. ‒ following the attacks on three military camps in bujumbura, the security situation in burundi has deteriorated sharply in recent days. burundi held parliamentary and local elections on 29 june 2015 and presidential elections on 21 july 2015, but neither of these processes was considered by the international community to be transparent, inclusive, free and credible. according to the office of the high commissioner for human rights and other human rights organisations, human rights violations and disregard for human rights and violent acts against opposition figures, human rights defenders and especially journalists have been committed in their country for political reasons both in the pre-election period and afterwards. the recent violent attacks and human rights violations must be strongly condemned. it is necessary to put an immediate end to the violence, human rights violations and political intimidation of opponents in strict compliance with international law and human rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution because it is the parliament's voice on the situation in burundi. in the wake of the attacks on three military camps in bujumbura in recent days, the security situation in burundi has deteriorated significantly, with at least 87 people killed by burundian security forces on 11 and 12 december 2015. burundi held parliamentary and local elections on 29 june 2015 and presidential elections on 21 july 2015, and neither of these electoral processes was considered by the international community to be transparent, inclusive, free and credible, which led to the suspension of the eu electoral mission in burundi and the decision of a large part of the burundian opposition to boycott the elections. according to the office of the high commissioner for human rights (ohchr) and other human rights organisations, both in the run-up to the elections and in the aftermath, there have been politically motivated human rights violations and abuses and violent acts against opposition figures, human rights defenders and, in particular, journalists in their country. parliament strongly condemned the recent violent attacks and the increase in human rights violations and abuses, including killings, extrajudicial executions, violations of the physical integrity of the population, torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, arbitrary arrests and unlawful detention, including the imprisonment of children, the occupation of schools by soldiers and police, and strongly condemned the violations of freedom of the press and of expression and the prevailing impunity.
in writing. ‒ my vote for the report on the situation in burundi expressed the concern about the situation in burundi, that has seriously deteriorated, following the attacks of three military camps in bujumbura; whereas burundian security forces killed at least 87 people on 11 and 12 december 2015; whereas many of these killings seem to have been random executions.
in writing. ‒ virunga national park, located in north kivu and eastern provinces of the drc, bordering rwanda and uganda, is africa's oldest national park and a unesco world heritage site, known worldwide for its unique habitats and rich biodiversity, making it the most biodiverse park in africa. armed groups have been threatening the park for decades with poaching and deforestation. at the same time, oil fever could have serious social and environmental destabilising effects, given the massive poverty, instability, poor governance and regional insecurity. i support calls for the european external action service to coordinate the diplomatic response of eu member states and other potential donors to the drc to help the drc government to abandon oil exploration and extraction in the virunga park and other unesco world heritage sites in the drc. i support calls on the commission and the member states to ensure the integrity of the park's territory, for example by increasing their commitments to finance the preservation of sustainable cultural heritage and sustainable economic development and diversification in the surrounding region.
in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of this resolution because it was the one in which parliament spoke on the protection of the virunga national park in the democratic republic of congo. virunga national park (vnp), located in north kivu and eastern provinces of the drc bordering rwanda and uganda, is africa's oldest national park and a unesco world heritage site, known worldwide for its unique habitats and rich biodiversity, making it the most biodiverse park in africa. the park is best known for its mountain gorillas, a rapidly disappearing species. however, despite its status as a protected natural area, the park has been threatened for decades by armed groups engaged in poaching, deforestation, and other forms of unruly and illegal exploitation of natural resources, and virunga is listed as a world heritage site in danger. in 2007, the drc government granted oil concessions covering 85% of the park area, and soco international plc (soco) is so far the only company that has carried out exploration activities in the park. the commission notes that the goc has not provided any evidence that the soco exploration licence is in line with the environmental legislation of the drc. in its resolution, parliament called for the irreparable damage to the virunga national park to be prevented and regretted that the virunga national park had also become one of the most endangered wildlife areas in the world.
in writing. ‒ i have voted for the resolution on protection of virunga national park in the democratic republic of the congo. it is of absolute urgency to prevent irreversible damage to virunga national park and put pressure on drc government not to give license to another oil operator – as soco no longer holds the license for exploitation.
